author: IMI Kids Monkey Desk B
text: Max had a bot to get a pea. Ned got it a nut. The bot had the nut and did not go. Max got it a pea. It did not let go of the nut. Ned got the nut. The bot did cry. Max put it in its paw. Ned got the pea. Now the nut had a pet and a tin paw.

title: The web jet
target: A space pilot mistakes his own toy tether for an invisible obstacle
author: IMI Kids Monkey Desk B
text: Bo had a toy jet. Pip put it on a web. Bo got in. The jet got as far as a log. "Why am I by the log?" Pip had the web in his paw. He let it go. The jet got by the log. Bo was off. Pip had to run to get it.

title: The spy ray
target: A laser security system accidentally becomes a limbo game
author: IMI Kids Monkey Desk B
text: Fay had to get by a red ray. Gus had a box to get it low. Fay got low. The ray got low too. Fay got too low to get up. Gus got it low too. Fay lay on a mat. The ray did too. Fay sat up. "You try!" Gus got low. Fay hit the red dot on his box. She got by Gus.

title: The odd egg
target: A detective mistakes a dyed nut for his own missing egg
author: IMI Kids Monkey Desk B
text: Dot had a tan egg in a box. Gus saw it. His egg was tan too. "Did you get my egg?" Dot had a pot of tan dye. Gus saw a rod by it. He got the egg up. It had a cut. Dot cut it up. It was a nut. Gus had to get his egg out of his bag.

title: The hero knot
target: A grand entrance ends with the hero tied down by the work she interrupts
author: IMI Kids Monkey Desk B
text: Fay had to tie a web to a cot. Kit ran in to aid her. "I am in!" she did cry. Kit got her paw in the web. Fay did tie the web to the cot. Kit did bow. The web did tug. Kit sat. Fay had Kit in a web on the cot. "I am in," Kit did say. "I am in a web!"

title: The sleep switch
target: A sleep ray appears effective because its target is already napping
author: IMI Kids Monkey Desk B
text: Ned had a ray to get Bo to nap. Bo lay on a cot. He had a nap. Ned hit the ray. Bo did not go. Ned hit it a lot. Bo did not go. Ned put his ear by Bo. Bo had a nap. Ned sat. He had a nap too. Bo got up and put a rug on him. The ray had won a nap for Ned.

title: The great finale
target: An oversized victory flag is repurposed as a tea decoration
author: IMI Kids Monkey Desk B
text: Pip got to a red orb in his jet. Dot had a red rag on a pin for him. "You won!" Pip got the pin in his paw. It was too big for the jet. Dot put it in a cup and put tea in it. Pip got the cup. His big win was a cup of tea.

title: The crown that rang
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pip found a gold crown in a tree. Each time he put it on, it rang like a bell. The troop came to bow, then held their ears. Pip hid his tail in his fur and tried to look grand. Dot gave the crown a tap with her paw. A bee flew out. Its hive had a new king, and that king owed rent.

title: A pea with a plan
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dot slept on a stack of beds to prove her rank. A pea lay at the base. She felt no lump, but her tail hung down and her paw hit the floor. At dawn the troop found green vines all in her fur. The pea had grown up the beds. Dot won the test, then made the royal chef mow her room.

title: The shoe fits the tree
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: May left a glass shoe at the ball. Rex took it round the troop to find its mate. Each paw was too wide. Each tail got in the way. May saw him try the shoe on a limb and had to laugh till her fur shook. It fit the tree just right. Rex gave the tree a dance, while May went home in boots.

title: The bean fare
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gus sold a cow for a sack of beans. The beans grew a stalk up to a cloud. Gus went up with his tail round each leaf and dew in his fur. A huge paw held out a fare chart. The cloud troop ran a lift now. Gus had no coins, so he gave the lift a scrub and rode down with a mop as his prize.

title: The frog on strike
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: A frog asked Ivy for a kiss. Ivy said she could give him a plum. He took it and asked for more. Soon the troop sat by the pool with fruit in each paw. Ivy wiped juice from her fur and hid her tail. The frog would not turn into a lord. He liked free lunch far more than he liked a crown.

title: The slow race notice
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo raced a snail to the gate. He ran so fast his fur blew back and his tail flew high. The troop gave a cheer. Bo put one paw on the gate and took the prize. The snail gave him the race rules. They had to reach their own home next. Bo had a long way left to run. The snail had its own home and won.

title: The crumb map
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pip left bits to mark his trail. Dot ate them as they went. By dusk their troop was lost. Pip waved his tail and shook his fur. Dot put a paw on a tree. It had jam on its bark. She had wiped her paws on each tree after each snack. They went home by the jam trail and had soup for tea.

title: The cloak with pockets
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rex got a cloak no one could see. He wore it to meet the troop. His fur was cold, and his tail shook. Ned gave him a real coat. Rex put his paw into its deep pouch and found a note from the cloak shop. It said the cloak was free, but the pouch cost gold. Ned used the note to light the stove.

title: The tower delivery
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: May lived in a tall tower. She let her tail hang down so Gus could climb. He had a cake in one paw. Bits got in her fur, and the cake fell on the troop below. May went down to taste it. Gus gazed at the open door. All week he had come up by the wall. The door had been for cake carts all along.

title: The dragon candle
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dot met a beast with smoke in its nose. The troop hid, but Dot held up a cake. She asked it to light the wick. It blew once. Her fur got warm and her tail rose. She gave a glad clap. The beast had hoped to guard gold. Soon it stood at the cake shop, with a line of cakes and a sign for tips.

title: The sword in the loaf
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned drew a blade from a loaf. The troop named him as king. He wiped flour from his fur with one paw and held his tail high. The baker came out and asked for his knife. Ned gave it back. The troop still bowed. The baker made him king of the wash bowl, where he ruled ten bowls and a spoon with jam on it.

title: The wish coin back
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ivy paid for a lamp and made a wish for gold. A gold fish came out. She made a wish for a crown. A crown of weeds fell on her fur. Her tail shook. The troop said to try once more. Ivy put her paw on the lamp and made a wish for a coin back. A coin fell out. She got a plain lamp that did what lamps ought to do.

title: The red hood feast
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dot wore a red hood to take bread to May. A sly guest met her in the wood and asked where she went. Dot held her paw to her lips. Her tail hid the bread bag. The troop had sent her with a quiz for spies. The guest got each guess wrong. At the feast, May gave him a cloth and wiped bits off his fur.

title: The royal nap alarm
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: The troop said a spell had made Rex sleep for years. Pip went to wake him with a kiss, but found the whole troop at rest too. Fur lay on each chair. Tails hung from the lamps. Pip put his paw on a gong. He hit it once. Rex sat up and asked for tea. The spell had no power. The royal lunch had just been much too large.

title: The troll toll book
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo asked for a toll at his span. Each guest had to tell a joke. Gus gave him one about a tail in a pie. Bo had a laugh and let the troop pass. Then he saw Gus come back with fake fur and a new hat. Gus told the same joke. Bo put a paw out for coins. His span now had a fee for old jokes.

title: The seven small seats
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: May found a hut with seven seats. She sat on one and broke it. Her tail sent two more down. A nail tore her coat. The troop came home to find her on the floor. May held a bent peg in her paw. She fixed each chair, then made one big bench. The troop sat on it and asked her to break the table too.

title: The glass gets a day off
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rex asked his glass who was best. The glass said Dot. Rex wiped his fur and tried again. It said Dot once more. He hid his tail and hit the floor. The troop came to see the fuss. Dot stood right in front of the glass. Rex moved her aside. The glass said it could see a wall now, and the wall was quite nice.

title: The ginger loaf ferry
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, Gus, all fictional monkeys
text: A loaf ran from the oven and dared the troop to catch it. Pip used his tail to swing ahead. Dot held out one paw, but the loaf got past her. It came to a pond and asked Gus for a ride. Gus had flour in his fur and a boat full of buns. The loaf took one look, went home, and chose a cool shelf.

title: The royal tax on rain
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rex taxed each drop of rain. The troop set jars out to count the debt. Pip kept his tail dry, but his fur got wet. He took one paw full of rain to the king. Rex asked for the fee. Pip asked for a slip for each drop. By noon Rex had no ink left. He made rain free and put a tax on ink.

title: The pillow shield
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gus held a soft pad to block each blow. The troop sent him to face a stern guard. His tail shook, and his fur stood up. The guard swung a staff. The staff tore the pad and sent fluff out. Fluff flew past his paw. The guard had to snort so hard he lost the gate key. Gus came home with the key and a flat pad.

title: The spell check fairy
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ivy cast a spell to make Pip bold. She said cold in error. Frost grew on his fur. His tail stuck to a rail. The troop got hot soup while Ivy tried again. She said gold. Pip shone, but still shook. He held his paw over her mouth and asked for a coat. Ivy gave him one. He faced the dark wood in warm plaid.

title: The moat lesson
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned dug a moat to keep pals out. Soon his troop could not get in for lunch. He waved a paw from the wall. His tail sank and his fur smelt of mud. Dot tied a rope to a cart full of pals and threw Ned the loose end. Ned drew so hard the cart flew over the moat. He had pals at last, all in his soup.

title: The goose accountant
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: May owned a goose that laid gold eggs. She got a grand nest for it. The troop came to see her gold. May wiped her fur and held up an egg in one paw. Her tail swept a pile of bills. The nest cost more than the eggs. She sold the nest and got straw. The goose liked that, and May could at last pay for toast.

title: The quest for a spoon
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pip went to find a lost spoon. He went past a bog and wore mud in his fur. His tail saved him from a deep hole. At last he found a chest. He pried its lid up with one paw. The troop saw all the gold and cried out. Pip shut the lid. He still had soup to eat. The spoon lay under the chest, where it held one short leg still.

title: The cloak of good manners
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dot wore a cloak that said "May I" each time she moved. The troop liked it at first. Then her tail hit a door. "May I?" She gave her fur a rub. "May I?" She held a paw to eat. "May I?" Dot gave the cloak to a shop bell. It said "May I" when pals came in. At night she shut the shop and heard it say "May I" to each moth.

title: The map that folds
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pip has a map of the whole realm. He folds it to fit his paw. Now the sea lies next to the seat. The troop takes a boat to the king. Pip has salt in his fur and a wet tail. The king asks how they got past his walls. Pip opens the map. They all land in the royal bath.

title: The royal soup trial
target: Trial to win a royal hand
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: May sets a test for each brave beau. Each must eat her soup. Gus dips one paw in the bowl and loses some fur. His tail goes stiff. The troop begs him to stop. He asks May for bread to cool the soup. She gets a loaf. He finds her lost ring in it and wins her nod, plus lunch for the troop.

title: The quiet horn
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned buys a horn to call his troop on a quest. He blows so hard his teeth ache. No sound comes out. Dot puts a paw in the horn and finds a sock. Ned pulls it out with his tail. Now the horn works. The troop comes up to the hill. The quest is to find the owner of a very ripe sock.

title: The tiny curse
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ivy puts a spell on Rex to make him small. He hides in her fur and nips her tail. The troop can hear his laugh but can not see him. Ivy asks him to stop. Rex asks for a crumb in each paw. She gives him a whole cake. He says the spell must stay till he can eat it all.

title: The door with tests
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo keeps a door that gives a quiz. Pip knows the right reply, but the door tests him. Pip rubs his fur and wraps his tail round the knob. The troop waits in the rain. Bo puts his paw on a hinge and asks the door to state its proof. The door has none. Bo gives it a book to study. It opens to let him turn each page.

title: The king of puddles
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rex calls a pool his realm. He puts a flag in it with his paw. The troop bows, but Dot grins into her fur. Rex curls his tail on his new seat. Then the sun dries the pool. Rex moves his flag to a cup of tea. Dot sips it. His next realm has a lid and a sign that says do not sip.

title: The giant boot garden
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gus sees a huge boot by the road. The troop fears its owner will crush their huts. Gus rubs mud from the toe with one paw. His tail hooks a lace. Seeds fall in his fur. No owner comes. They fill the boot with soil and plant peas. When the giant seeks his boot, Gus asks him to wait till the peas are ripe.

title: The wish for silence
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dot asks a star for quiet. The troop falls mute. Her tail makes no swish, and her paw makes no tap. Even her fur can not swish. Dot likes it till the tea boils. She can not hear the pot. She waves for her next wish. Sound comes back just as the pot tips. The star gives her a mop as a free third wish.

title: The crown of ants
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pip wins a crown of leaf bits at the fair. The troop lifts him high. His tail curls with pride. Then his skin grows itchy. He feels ants on each paw. The crown was their old roof. Pip sets it on a stump. He makes a fresh crown from paper. The ants vote him king again, for his fine grasp of home care.

title: The false last page
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: May reads that her tale must end with a feast. She cooks for the troop and wipes her fur clean. Her tail holds the spoon as her paw turns the last page. There is one more page. It says wash up. May tears it out and makes a paper crown. At the feast, she names Gus king of all the dirty bowls.

title: The north wind scarf
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: The wind tries to pull a scarf off Bo. Bo grips it with one paw and holds his tail tight. His fur stays warm. The sun tries next. Bo opens the scarf but puts on a shade hat. The troop bets on who will win. Dot gives Bo a plum. He takes off the scarf to make a fruit bag. Dot keeps the bets.

title: The castle with round discs
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned makes a fort on discs. The troop rolls it up a hill to gain a grand view. Ned has dust in his fur and a sore paw. His tail slips off the brake. The fort rolls down to the lake. It bobs. Ned calls it a royal barge. Dot asks for a ride, then notes that the seat is now the drain.

title: The jewel in the soup
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ivy finds a red gem in her soup. She holds it up with her paw. The troop roars. Her tail waves, and her fur glows in the light. Rex says the gem once sat in his crown. He takes it and puts it on his head. The gem pops. Red juice runs down his nose. Ivy asks for her plum back.

title: The quest of the spare sock
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo seeks the mate to his sock. He asks each one of the troop to lift a paw. No luck. His tail drags in mud and his fur fills with burrs. At dusk he sits on a stump and sighs. The sock hangs on his own tail. He puts it on at last, then finds he has lost the other one.

title: The oath at lunch
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gus vows to guard a pie till the troop comes home. He sets his paw on his chest. His fur is neat and his tail is still. A fly lands on the crust. Gus eats that bit to save the pie. A new fly lands. By dusk only the dish is left. Gus waits proud by it. No fly has hurt the dish.

title: The fairy census
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dot hears a voice in a rose. It asks for milk. She sets a cup by the rose. Next day ten cups stand on the step. The troop helps her fill them. Dot gets milk on her fur, tail, and paw. She asks how many fair folk live there. One voice says one. It has ten tiny cats. Dot sets out a cow and goes back to bed.

title: The royal bath lake
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rex wants a bath as wide as a lake. The troop digs one, and rain fills it. Rex dips a paw in. He jumps back. He puts his tail in and pulls it right out. The lake is far too cold. Dot hands him a pot. Rex heats one cup of lake water and takes a royal bath in his old bowl.

title: The hero with a receipt
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pip saves a crown from a well. He hands it to May with a wet paw. His tail drips, and his fur reeks of moss. May gives him any prize he wants. The troop waits for him to ask for gold. Pip asks for a fence round the well. May nods. Next week he saves her fence from the same well.

title: The queen of moss
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ivy makes a crown from moss. It grows down her fur and round her tail. Soon she can just lift a paw. The troop soaks her each day. She asks them to stop, but they think it is royal music. Dot hears the words and cuts the moss. Ivy is free. The troop keeps the crown on a stump, where its reign is far less noisy.

title: The gift that glows
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned gets a stone that glows at night. He shows the troop and puts it under his bed. His fur glows blue, and his tail casts a long shade. He hides his eyes with a paw. He can not sleep. Dot buys the stone to light her shed. Ned gets a plain dark rock for his bed and has the best night in years.

title: The cloud steps
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: May ties ropes to make tall steps up to a cloud. The troop holds the base. Her tail curls round each rung, and her fur fills with mist. She puts a paw out at the top. The cloud moves. May sways over the town. She lets go above a pool. The troop calls it a bad quest, but May sells seats for the ride.

title: The knight of the leaf
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo wears a leaf as his badge. He tells the troop that he will fear no storm. His fur is dry and his tail is high. The first gust rips the leaf away. Bo grabs it with one paw and folds it into a boat. He sets it in the ditch. Now he is lord of the fleet, and the storm gives him free wind.

title: The spell in the jam
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ivy makes jam that lets each eater sing. Gus tries it, and his voice fills the room. Each note makes his chest shake. His tail keeps time. The troop holds paws over their ears. Ivy puts the lid back on the jar. The jar sings too. Gus takes it on stage and lets it do all the hard high notes.

title: The brave broom
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dot asks a broom to sweep the hall. It tries to clean her tail as well. She holds a paw in front of her face and sends the broom out the door. The troop sees it clean the path, the hill, and the whole town. Dot gives it a tiny brush. At last it sits down to clean the dust from its own straw.

title: The royal image itch
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rex sits for a grand image. He keeps his tail rigid and his paw on a gold ball. His skin grows itchy. He moves. The troop tells him to hold still. Dot draws each pose on a fresh sheet. Rex sees a blur of arms when she flips them. He buys the whole stack and calls it his first royal film show.

title: The missing goal
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: The troop comes to play ball, but the goal is gone. Pip finds two long marks in the mud. The marks lead to a shed. Gus sits there with the goal round his bed. He says it keeps flies off. Pip finds the net full of fruit. Gus is glad to move his bed to the field. Now each goal earns a free plum.

title: The whistle in the cake
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Rex, Ned, all fictional monkeys
text: Dot hears a high note at the bake sale. Each time Ned takes a bite, it sings again. She asks him to open his mouth. There is a small pipe in his cake. The troop knows whose it is. Rex has lost his pipe for the race. He must now ask Ned to chew when it is time to start.

title: The dry paw clue
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rain falls all day. A pie is gone from the hut. Dot looks at each paw in the troop. Only May has dry fur. Dot feels sure she has her thief. May shows her a hole in the roof. Her bed is wet too. She dried her paws at the fire, where the chef ate the pie right out of the pan. Dot puts the empty pan in jail and gives May a towel.

title: The high jump crown
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo tries to jump over a pole. His tail hooks it on each try. The troop says he must tuck his tail. Bo does, but now he lands flat. Dot puts the pole on the grass and asks him to lift it. He lifts it past his head. He wins the high lift prize. The jump judge asks where the pole went.

title: The echo witness
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, Gus, all fictional monkeys
text: Pip hears a voice shout thief in the cave. He leads the troop in with a torch. No one is there. He calls out who said that. The cave asks him the same thing. Pip goes red under his fur. Dot taps his paw and tells him to ask a fresh query. He asks where the pie is. Gus gives a laugh in the dark. The sound leads them to Gus and his pie. Dot lets the cave ask him for a slice.

title: The last lap snack
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gus leads the race till the last lap. He sees a fruit stall and stops for lunch. The troop races past. Gus asks the chef to pack his meal in a paper cone. He uses his tail to hold it as he runs. At the line he is last, but all the rest want a bite. He gives out bites in trade for each prize bow.

title: The blue ink trail
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, May, all fictional monkeys
text: May finds blue marks on her clean floor. She calls Dot to solve the case. Dot looks for blue paws in the troop. No one has them. But Pip has a blue tail. He used it as a brush to make a map. Dot reads the trail as lines on a map. It leads to the milk jar, which Pip has put on the roof. Dot gets it and hands Pip a mop to draw his next map.

title: The extra tennis ball
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Rex, all fictional monkeys
text: Rex wins each point with a fresh ball. The troop sees a sly trick. Dot peers into his pouch. It is empty. Rex puts up both paws with a grin. Gus looks at his tail. It holds a tube of balls out of sight. Rex gets a new job. He now feeds balls to the whole troop and wins no games at all.

title: The case of the loud sock
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: A chirp keeps the troop awake. Dot looks at the gate, the beds, and the roof. Pip walks with her. Each time he moves, the chirp moves too. She lifts one of his feet and finds a toy duck in his sock. Pip says he put it there to keep it safe. Dot gives the duck a nest. It gives her one last chirp.

title: The wrong finish tape
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: May runs past the red tape with a cheer. The troop gives a cheer too. Gus asks why she is in his yard. The tape marks his new paint. May has red lines in her fur. She looks down the road and sees the true goal. She runs there. The judge gives her a prize for best lines, while Gus hangs wet paint signs high up.

title: The clue in the ice
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dot finds a key in a block of ice. The troop needs it to open the snack shed. She holds it near the fire. The ice melts, but the key melts to a thin curl. It was made of sugar. Pip says he froze it for a prank. Dot asks him to fetch the real key. It is in his hat. He now keeps all candy far from the fire.

title: The boat race anchor
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned rows hard, but his boat does not move. The troop calls out hints from the bank. He pulls with both paws and wraps his tail round the seat. Dot dives in to look. A rope holds the boat to a tree. Ned frees it and races ahead. He wins the race, then comes back for his lunch, which still hangs from the tree.

title: The missing chess king
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Ned, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: Bo finds his king gone from the board. The troop looks under the rug. Dot spots a tiny crown in his fur. His tail had swept the king off the board and into his hood. Bo puts it back. Ned says the move is wrong. Bo nods and puts the king in his hood. From there it rules a warm realm with no foes in sight.

title: The race on poles
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pip ties long poles to his feet to beat the tall troop in a race. He takes huge steps till a paw slips. He lands on his back while the poles run down the slope. Dot grabs them at the line. The judge says the poles win. Pip asks them to speak. They stay mute, so he takes the prize for them and buys a pair of flat shoes.

title: The locked jam jar
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, May, all fictional monkeys
text: May locks a jar of jam in a glass case. At dawn the jam is gone. Dot tests the lock and finds it sound. The troop fears magic. Dot finds a straw in a tiny hole in the case. It leads up to the roof. Gus sits there with a red paw and a full belly. May ties a bell to the straw. At his next sip, the whole troop comes for jam.

title: The golf hole thief
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, Rex, all fictional monkeys
text: Rex hits a ball at the hole. It rolls out each time. The troop looks on as he tries again. Dot bends to look into the hole. Pip has put his tail in it to keep worms warm. Rex asks him to move. Pip lifts his tail, and six balls fall in at once. Rex marks six wins on his card. Dot takes away his pen.

title: The muddy alibi
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned says he was out in the rain when the cake was lost. His fur is full of mud. Dot puts one paw in the mud. It is warm and has a sweet scent. The troop sees Ned lick his cuff. He used cake mix to fake the rain. Dot leads him to the bath. Now he has a real need to be wet and no cake.

title: The pool lane dispute
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: Gus and Bo race in the pool. Gus wins, but Bo says his tail hit the line first. The troop reads the rules. They say first paw wins. Dot lays a plank over the pool. Gus walks over it on his paws. Bo swims below it. Gus wins again. The judge adds one word to the rules, and the plank is now a swim ramp.

title: The case of the double hat
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Rex, May, all fictional monkeys
text: Dot sees a thief in a tall red hat. She stops Rex, who wears the same hat. He waves at May, who wears one too. The troop has a whole box of them. Dot goes back to the scene and finds red paint on a leaf. Rex has red paint on his tail. He wore the hat on it to fool her. Dot asks him to raise both paws and his tail. The lost cake drops out.

title: The tug rope knot
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: The troop makes two teams to play tug. Pip ties his tail to the rope for more grip. Dot tells him to use his paws. He says his plan is smart. Each team pulls. Pip flies up and lands on a low limb. His tail holds the rope there as both teams let go. The game ends as a swing game, and Pip needs the first push.

title: The secret pie code
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gus gets a note that says pie twice. Dot calls it a code. The troop tries each mark on the shed lock. No code works. Dot folds the note and finds jam on its pages. Gus has sent his own wish list. He lost the first note, so he wrote a new one. Dot opens the shed with the key taped to the list.

title: The table tennis sneeze
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, May, Ned, all fictional monkeys
text: May hits a tiny ball. Ned blows it back with a loud snort. The troop calls foul. Ned says his nose is a kind of bat. Dot reads the rules and finds no ban on noses. May puts dust on the ball. Ned gives a snort so hard the table slips away. The judge lets him keep his nose, but asks him to use a clean bat.

title: The clock that lied
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: The troop says Pip stole a plum at noon. The clock stood at noon when the plum was lost. Pip says he was at the pond. Dot opens the clock and finds a plum pit in its gears. The chef used the clock as a bin. Its hands have been stuck for days. Pip goes home with his name clear and a job to clean the clock.

title: The pole vault picnic
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo bends a pole to leap over a bar. His tail hooks a flag, and he flies into the snack tent. The troop runs to see if he is hurt. Bo sits in a bowl of jelly with both paws full of buns. He asks for one more try. Dot moves the snack tent. Bo now asks if he can skip ahead to the medal meal.

title: The lost library hush
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dot hears a faint chirp in the book room. The troop can not read in peace. She looks on each shelf and finds no one. May shows her the sign that says hush. A toy wheel turns at its back when the wind blows. Dot shuts the pane. The sound stops. Then the room gets hot. The troop opens the pane and reads books about noisy gears.

title: The chalk clue
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dot finds white dust on the floor. A cake is gone, so she tests each paw for chalk. The troop lines up. Bo has white fur and must go first. Dot tries one speck. It is flour. She goes to the oven and finds the cake still there. Bo asks her to say sorry. Dot gives him the first slice and a clean class slate.

title: The ski hill queue
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned puts wax on his skis. He races past the troop and over the hill. At the base he finds a long queue. No one can walk back up the slick snow. Ned has waxed the whole slope with his skis. Dot lends him a rope. He goes up the tree and uses his tail to haul each skier up. The prize is a broom.

title: The hatbox witness
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: May says she saw the thief from a hat box. Dot asks how she got in. May says she slept there. The troop looks at the tiny box. May can fit one paw in it. Dot asks her to show the view. May puts her eye to the hole. She sees a face on a sign. The thief is a model for cheap hats. The lost coins roll out when May lifts the hat box.

title: The ball that went home
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: Pip hits a ball out of the park. The troop runs to fetch it. The ball rolls into a hole and stays there. Dot looks in and sees Bo at rest with it under his head. He used it as a soft bed last night and wrote his name on it. Pip buys a new ball. Bo asks him to sign a lease if he wants to use the old ball again.

title: The case of the wet stamp
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gus says a thief took his note. Dot looks in the post bag. It is full of wet paper. The troop used the bag as a rain hood. Gus holds up his paw and says his note was dry. Dot reads his name on the hood. The ink has run, but his words are clear. He asked the troop to bring him a dry coat.

title: The limbo judge
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo bends under a low bar. His tail hits it. The troop says he lost. Bo asks if the tail rule is in print. Dot gives him the rules. He folds the page into a tube and uses it as a new bar. Now his tail can brush it with no harm. Dot bends under it once and takes the prize cup while Bo reads the rules.

title: The silent bell case
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: The bell does not ring at noon. Dot asks each one in the troop where they were. Pip says he was in the bell tower. He hoped for a quiet nap, so he put wool in the bell. Dot pulls out the wool with one paw. The bell rings. Pip sits up in alarm. Dot puts the wool in a sack and gives it to him.

title: The cricket tea break
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Rex, all fictional monkeys
text: Rex bats a ball into the tea pot. The troop calls it out. Rex says the pot is still on the field. Dot pours the tea and the ball rolls into a cup. Gus sips his tea and spits the ball back onto the pitch. The judge halts the game to give a rule. The rest drink all the tea while he reads.

title: The clue with teeth
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, May, all fictional monkeys
text: May finds bite marks on the gate. Dot asks the troop to show their teeth. Each grin is too small. Gus shows them a saw. The marks match its teeth. May had asked him to make the gate lower, then lost track. Dot says the case is done. Gus asks if she means the gate. He has cut its latch in half.

title: The slow bike medal
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pip rides hard with his tail round the seat. He goes past the troop, but his wheel comes off. He hauls the bike to the goal on his back. The judge says he must ride it. Pip sits on it and asks Dot for a push. She gives him a push over the line. He wins last place and gives Dot the bell from his old bike.

title: The wrong scent
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dot takes a trail of roast nuts. She hopes to find the lost snack box. The troop waits at the shed. Dot finds a bath, where Rex has nut soap in his fur. He shows her the box by the tub. He used its lid as a tray. Dot finds the nuts in the soap dish and asks Rex which ones he ate.

title: The hoop in the tree
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gus puts a hoop high in a tree. The troop lobs balls but can not score. Dot goes up and finds a nest in the hoop. She moves the nest to a safe limb and drops the hoop. Gus says the game is too easy now. Dot puts him in the nest. He must keep each ball out. By dusk he asks to join the team on the grass.

title: The lunch bell thief
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: The lunch bell is gone. The troop waits at their desks with empty bowls. Dot sees Ned wave both paws at the cook. He has tied the bell to his tail. Each wag rings it, but the thick door stops the sound. Dot opens the door. The cook comes with soup. Ned tries to sit down, and the bell calls for lunch all over again.

title: The bowling alley hill
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, May, all fictional monkeys
text: May rolls a ball down the lane. It turns left and hits the shoe rack. The troop tries again with a new ball. The same thing takes place. Dot puts one paw on the floor. The lane tilts to the door. Gus set one leg of it on a plum. They take out the plum. May bowls a great game while Gus eats the plum.

title: The disappearing clue
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dot cuts a clue in ice to keep it fresh. The troop goes with her to the crime scene. The ice melts in her paw. Now she has no clue and a wet map. Pip asks what the clue said. Dot says it said keep cool. The lost cake was in the cold room all along. She puts her next note on paper and keeps it dry.

title: The rugby ball nest
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo sees an odd egg on the field. He puts it in his fur to keep it warm. The troop hunts for their ball. Dot asks Bo what he found. He shows her the egg. She says it is their rugby ball. Bo will give it back if they do not drop it. The whole game is now a very soft game of catch.

title: The footprints on the roof
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dot sees paw marks in a cake on the roof. No steps lead up the hut. The troop fears a thief with wings. Gus says he threw the cake up there to cool. Dot finds a pie fork stuck in it. Its five tips made the marks when Gus threw the cake. Gus gets his cake and Dot gets a slice for the clue to a crime with five metal toes.

title: The trophy that rang
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, Rex, all fictional monkeys
text: Rex can not find his cup after the race. The troop looks in each bag. Dot hears a ring from the shed. Pip has hung the cup from a rope to call the troop for lunch. Rex asks for it back. Pip gives it to him. Now Rex hears a ring each time he moves his paw. He finds the lost spoon still tied in the cup.

title: The badminton shade
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ivy hits a cork with a plume into a stiff wind. It lands in a tree. The troop calls for a new serve. Ivy looks up and sees six more corks on the same limb. She puts her tail round the trunk and gives it a shake. All seven fall onto the court. Dot hits them back one at a time. The troop plans to play under a roof next week.

title: The case of the red moon
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Rex, May, all fictional monkeys
text: May sees a red moon above the shed. She calls Dot to solve the odd sight. The troop comes in fear. Dot walks up to it with a stick. The moon hangs from a cord. It is a red globe Rex got for his play. May asks why it has teeth. Rex says the crowd got bored with his plain old moon last week.

title: The fishing line race
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, Gus, all fictional monkeys
text: Gus hooks a huge fish. He pulls so hard his tail grips the bank. The troop helps. At last a boot comes out of the lake. Dot reads a tag in it. Pip says he lost that boot last week. Gus says he still wins the best catch. Pip says the boot must go on a scale. He takes out the huge stone he hid in it.

title: The password sneeze
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dot needs a code word to enter the club. She hears Gus snort at the door. The troop lets him in. Dot gives a snort too, but gets no reply. She peers in the lock hole. Gus has dust in his fur from the attic. The guard knows he found the lost games. Dot gets a game and gets in with a clean nose and dry lips.

title: The skating rink thaw
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned makes a rink in his yard. The troop has steel on each shoe. They wait for the judge. The sun rises, and the rink melts. Dot finds a pair of shoes. She puts them on and leaps into the pool. Ned calls it a new sport. They award her a medal for best leap. The judge comes dry and goes home with mud up to his knees.

title: The library card chase
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pip loses his card in the book room. Dot asks where he last used it. Pip says at lunch. The troop goes to the cafe and sees the card under a short table leg. It makes the table level. Dot pulls it out. Soup tips out. Pip gives it back and pays cash for his next book. The clerk gives him a card with four tiny legs.

title: The baton in the bread
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Gus, May, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: May gives the baton to Bo. He runs to the goal, but the judge says no. Bo holds a loaf. The troop mixed up the snack bag and the race bag. May runs back to fetch the baton. She finds Gus with jam on it. The judge waits while they wash it, then gives the troop a prize for a very slow clean pass.

title: The moon rent
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pip put his flag on the moon. His troop had a fine new home. Then Dot came out of a cave with a bill. She had got there first and owned the land. Pip had no gold, so he gave her his flag. Dot used it as a mop. The moon was dusty, and rent was now one clean cave each month.

title: The floating soup
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gus made soup on the ship. He took off the lid, and a warm blob rose into the air. The troop tried to catch it in bowls. Gus held a spoon in each paw but got no soup. Dot set a fan to blow. The soup blew into the air vent. Gus set cups below it. Lunch came from the roof with a fine gust.

title: The star that blinked
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: May saw a star blink three times. She sent her troop to help. Their ship flew close and found Ned in a tin shed. He had run out of light bulbs. He waved a torch to ask for a spare. May gave him a bulb and asked about the star. Ned held up a glass. He had hoped to read by the stars.

title: The space suit zipper
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo wore his new suit to step out of the ship. His tail stuck out of the back. The troop could not close the seal. Dot put a pipe over the tail and fixed a cap on it. Bo went out and waved. He used his new tail pipe to hook lost bolts. Dot made him chief of all ship tool work.

title: The crater cake
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, Rex, all fictional monkeys
text: Rex found a round hole on the moon. The troop dug down and found a cake tin. Rex said the moon must be one huge cake. Dot took a bite of a rock and spat it out. Pip came from the ship with flour on his fur. He had tried to bake a cake out there. It flew away, and only the tin came back.

title: The alien welcome mat
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ivy put a mat by the ship door. It said wipe paws. A new guest had ten feet and no paws. The troop had to wait while he wiped each toe. Ivy took the mat away. The guest went in and left a trail of mud. Ivy wrote a new sign. It said take off boots. The guest left ten boots by the tea tray.

title: The slow light beam
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned built a beam to send fruit to the moon. The troop stood by to test it. He put a plum in the beam. The plum shone, then fell off the stand. That was all it did. Dot read the box. Ned had paid for a lamp. He kept it to light his desk and sent the plum by mail. It got there far less shiny.

title: The robot tail
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gus made a robot to brush his fur. It did a fine job till it saw his tail. It saw the tail as a rope and tied it to the chair. The troop set Gus free. Dot used a doll to teach the robot about tails. Now it combs the doll all day. Gus sits next to it and waits for his turn.

title: The rocket salad
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: May put green fuel in her ship. It would not rise. The troop had a look in the tank and found pea soup. Gus had used the fuel jar as a lunch pot. May took out the soup with a cup. Gus gave her the real fuel from his lunch flask. The ship rose at once. Gus sat by each bowl to check it prior to tea time.

title: The silent comet
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pip led the troop to hear a comet sing. They wore ear cups and sat in space for hours. No song came. Dot asked Pip who said a comet sings. He gave her a book of poems. She gave him a drum and asked him to make the score. The comet went past to a fine beat. Pip sold the drum track with his quiet film.

title: The treasure hammock
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo dug for gold on an isle. His troop dug till the pit was deep. Dot found a cloth chest at the base. It held a net and two hooks. Bo was sad till Dot hung the net in a tree. It made a fine bed. Bo lay in it and told the troop to dig some more. They put dirt in the pit and went for a swim.

title: The map on the sail
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rex drew a map on his sail so he could not lose it. The troop set off to find the gold. Wind blew in the sail, and the map went round a pole. Rex could see only half. Dot cut a small map from paper. Rex said that might blow away. Dot put it in a box. Rex did not know maps could fit in boxes.

title: The polite boarding party
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: May put her paw on a ship rail and asked to come on board. Its troop said yes. She asked for the gold. They said no. May gave a bow and went back to her boat. Gus asked where the loot was. May held up a cake. The ship had given her tea, and she had found the gold was just a cheap foil trim.

title: The parrot clerk
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned had a bird that spoke each word he said. The troop loved it till Ned named the spot where he hid his gold. The bird told the whole port. Ned wrote a false place on a card and told the bird to read it aloud. The bird said read it aloud. It knew the trick. Ned paid it one seed to keep each hint for a day.

title: The plank contest
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gus told Pip to walk the plank. Pip put his tail round the rail and made the plank into a slide. The troop gave a clap. Gus tried the slide too and fell into the sea. Pip used the plank to pull him out. Gus asked for one more turn. The ship sat in port all day while each crew mate tried to land feet first.

title: The sea chest lock
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dot found a chest with seven locks. The troop tried seven keys. None fit. Bo held it up to shake it. The base fell off, and coins fell out. Dot saw that the locks were just glued to the lid. But the gold was real. Bo put each coin back and tied the chest shut with rope. No one could find the knot again.

title: The captain hat tax
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rex wore the high hat on the ship. He said that made him boss. The troop piled hats on their heads to claim his rank. Dot came with no hat at all. She could see under the sail, so she held the wheel while the rest hit the rails. Rex gave her the wheel. She sold the hats to buy a chart of small reefs.

title: The anchor garden
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: The troop could not lift the iron hook. Gus drew the rope, but it was taut. Dot went down to look. Roots had grown round the iron. The ship had sat in port for weeks. Bo got a saw and freed it. Gus held up the iron hook with green vines on it. He set sail at last, with tiny vines hung on the bow.

title: The ghost ship laundry
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: May saw white forms move on a dark ship. The troop hid below deck. May took a lamp on board. The forms were wet coats on a line. Wind blew them up as if alive. She found Ned as he tried to fold them. May used her tail to hold the line still. The troop came back, and each got a clean shirt in place of a scary tale.

title: The gold tooth route
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pip hid a coin under a loose tooth. No thief would look there. At lunch he bit a hard nut, and the tooth came out. The troop ran round the deck to find it. Dot found a nut with a coin in it. Pip had spat the coin into its shell. He put the coin in a pouch and let the tooth lie under his soft bed for a fair trade.

title: The spell for toast
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ivy told the class to turn bread into toast. Pip waved his wand and said roast. His whole desk grew hot. The troop let air in the door to drive smoke out. Ivy gave him a plain pan. Pip made toast in it while the rest did magic. His was the only meal free of frogs, fire, or bits of desk.

title: The wand with a leash
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo lost his wand each day. Ivy tied it to his paw with a cord. At class he cast a spell to make it fly. The wand rose and took Bo with it. The troop held his tail. Bo hung over the desk till Ivy broke the spell. She tied the wand to the desk next time. Now Bo takes his desk to every class.

title: The frog exam
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: May had to turn a cup into a frog. She cast her spell and heard a croak. The troop gave a cheer. Ivy asked her to lift the cup. A real frog sat below it. May had found it in the pond. Ivy said the test was not done. May made the frog a cup at last, then gave tea to a very dazed class.

title: The flying broom closet
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned chose a broom from the class shed. He rode it to the sky. The troop saw the broom shake free. Ned clung to a cloud and held on. Ivy sent up a mop. Ned flew home on it and asked why the broom had fled. It still had its price tag. The shop asked for it back till he paid the bill.

title: The potion label
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gus made a green drink for his class. Ivy said it would make fur glow. The troop took a sip and got shiny lips. Gus read his label. It said lips, not fur. Ivy made him write each label twice next time. Gus made plain water and gave it two tags. The class read both and still asked which spell would make them shine.

title: The spellbook lunchbox
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ivy gave Pip a book he must not open till noon. Pip put it in his lunch box. At noon he took it out and found jam on each page. The troop tried to read the words, but each word ran into the next. Pip cast one and made a huge loaf. Ivy kept the book. It was now the best lunch text in class.

title: The moon cheese lease
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gus went to the moon to get Swiss. The troop took bread. Gus found only stone, but he had told them to leave the Swiss at home. Dot set a slice of rock on her bread and took a fake bite. Gus asked how it was. Dot said it could use salt. They went home, where Gus had to buy Swiss for each empty slice.

title: The gravity switch
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned found a red lever on the ship. He hit it to make tea. The troop rose from their seats and hit the roof. Ned hung by his tail and tried to reach the lever again. Dot threw a shoe at it. They fell back down. The tea was still cold, so Ned wrote do not use for tea on the red lever.

title: The fairy chalkboard
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo wrote a spell on the class slate. The words slid off and ran out the door. The troop ran after them into the yard. Ivy told Bo to write a stop spell. He wrote stop, and the words lined up by the fence. Bo used them to spell out lunch. Ivy gave a sigh and let the class eat while she swept the last word off the path.

title: The telescope queue
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: May set up a scope to view a rare star. The troop stood in line all night. Each guest saw one round light. At dawn Dot put her paw over the front. The light shone on. May had left the lens cap on, and a small lamp lit the glass from the back. The troop asked for coins back. May gave each one a turn to view a real star at night.

title: The ship in the bottle
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rex put a tiny ship in a glass flask. Then he cast a spell to make his troop fit in it. They went round the cork and had no way out. Dot used her tail to haul the mast up. The mast poked the cork out. They all grew big again. Rex kept the flask as a vase. Dot put a large rose in it to block the port.

title: The comet hairbrush
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ivy took a brush from a comet. The brush made her fur glow. Her troop could see her all night. She liked it till she tried to hide in a game. Dot found her in the dark shed at once. Ivy gave the brush to the lamps in the hall. Now the lamps glow, and Ivy can hide till her tail pokes out.

title: The pirate fruit treaty
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: Bo and Gus both took the same isle. Both crews met on the beach. Dot drew a line down the sand. Bo got the trees, and Gus got the brook. Gus got fish, but Bo had no water for fruit. They gave one cup for one plum. At dusk the tide took the line away. They kept the trade since both liked their meal.

title: The spell for spare hands
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: May asked Ivy for extra hands to wash the bowls. Ivy gave her four. May held more bowls, but her cuffs did not fit. The troop gave her a huge coat. Each new hand got stuck in a pouch. May could not reach the bowls. She asked Ivy to take them back. Ivy left one spare hand to hold the towel while May had a wash in her old shirt.

title: The lost space parking ticket
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pip left his ship on a small rock. He came back with his troop and found a fine on the door. The fee was one moon stone. Pip chose a small rock to pay. Dot said he could not take the rock his ship sat on. Pip gave the guard his stone stud. The guard took it, and Pip held his shirt shut all the way home.

title: The sea monster menu
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: The troop saw a huge fin near the ship. Gus held out a fish to make peace. The fin went away, then came back with a card. It had a menu on it. Dot read that the fin was a sign for a cafe below the sea. Gus asked for lunch. A net rose with hot fish in it, plus the fish Gus had sent to pay for his meal.

title: The rocket countdown nap
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rex set a timer for lift. The troop saw the timer count down. At zero, a bell rang, but the ship did not move. Rex had used his nap timer. Dot asked where the real ship key was. Rex had it under his bed. He went to bed to fetch it and fell into sleep. The troop flew at last with their chief snug in his bunk.

title: The invisible ink test
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dot wrote all her work in ink no one could see. Ivy held the page up to the light. It was blank. The troop said Dot must have won. Ivy gave her a prize no one could see. Dot felt the empty box with one paw. She asked for plain ink next time. Ivy gave her a real pen and kept the blank prize for the next test.

title: The star chart stain
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned spilt soup on the star chart. The troop had to steer by the red dots. Each dot led them to the same old world. Dot tried one. It was a red bean. Ned wiped the chart and found the true path below. The ship got home at last. Dot made a fresh chart on a plate and told Ned that he could eat those stars at home.

title: The pirate flag seamstress
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: May sewed a skull on her flag. She hoped the troop would seem scary. The skull had a grin by error. Each ship waved and came close for tea. May tried to sew a frown. Her tail shook, and the skull got one shut eye. She gave up and made the ship a cafe. The happy flag got more gold than any raid had done all year.

title: The spell that swept names
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Ivy, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: Bo cast a spell to clean the class list. It took each name right off. The troop could not reply at roll call. Ivy asked Bo who he was. He did not know. Dot found the names in a dust pan. She put them back by size. Bo was Gus for one day. He liked the large lunch, but Gus asked for his small boots back.

title: The space elevator button
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gus rode a lift up to the stars. The troop had hit each knob to see what it did. The lift had a stop at every cloud. Dot asked them to stop. Gus put his paw over the knobs, but his tail hit the one for down. They rode all the way home. Next time Dot gave the troop toy knobs and kept the real ones in her pouch.

title: The treasure island picnic tax
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ivy dug up a chest on the isle. The troop gave a cheer at the gold in it. Then they saw a bill for harm to the grass. Ivy owed more gold than she found. Dot put the grass back in the hole. The bill grew green and fell apart. Ivy kept the gold, but now she had to water the hole each day so the bill would stay small.

title: The magic hat filing cabinet
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pip put all his class notes in a magic hat. He asked for his sums, and a hare came out. He asked for his magic, and got a new hare. The troop found a whole class of hares in the hat. They had used his notes for their desks. Pip gave them roots in trade. They gave back his work with red marks where he had got each sum wrong.

title: The asteroid ball game
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rex hit a ball from one rock to the next. The troop stood ready to catch it. The ball went round the rocks and came back to Rex. He hit it again. Dot said he was alone in the game. Rex asked her to throw from the other side. Both balls hit the same net and stuck. The troop had to pull them free and start a new sport.

title: The pirate eye patch swap
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned put on an eye patch to look bold. He hit a mast. The troop gave him a cane, but he hit a rail next. Dot found that Ned had put the patch over his good eye. He moved it to the other side and saw the whole deck. Now he could steer the ship, while Dot used the cane to hang his wet socks.

title: The spell for neat desks
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ivy cast a spell to make the desks neat. Each desk shut up to form a small cube. The troop had no place to sit. Bo put a cube in his paw and shook it. The desk rose up and threw his books. Ivy told the troop to give each cube a soft tap. They shut their desks after class and took the whole room home in their lunch bags.

title: The rocket pet door
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: May took her pet frog onto the ship. It leapt at the red door knob. The troop ran to stop it. Dot hid the knob with a cup. The frog sat on the cup for the whole trip. When they got home, it would not move. May gave it a fly. Dot cut a small pet door in the main door. The frog leapt out for the fly, and May freed the knob at last.

title: The pirate tide alarm
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gus tied a bell to the dock to warn of high tide. The troop heard it ring all night. At dawn Dot saw a crab pull its rope. Gus freed the rope and let the crab go. The tide rose with no sound, and the ship blew out. Dot gave the crab a job to ring the bell only at noon. It rang when he got lunch.

title: The magic graduation robe
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Ivy, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: Bo wore a robe that grew as he did. At the class feast he ate three cakes. The robe grew right over the hall. The troop fell over its hem. Ivy asked him to stand up. Bo could not find the cuffs. Dot cut a hole in the top, and Bo poked his head out. The robe was now the feast tent, and Bo sat in it till wash day.

title: The memo about memos
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Rex, all fictional monkeys
text: Rex sent a memo to ban memos. Dot sent a reply to ask if notes back were still fine. The troop got both and sent kind notes. By noon Rex had a desk full of notes. He gave a talk to clear it up. Gus wrote the talk down and sent it to each desk. Rex put his tail over the inbox and went out for tea.

title: The cake procurement trial
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, May, Ned, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: May asked for cake for the staff feast. Ned said she had to get three bids. She asked the troop for bids. Gus said cake is nice. Dot said cake is round. Bo said cake is gone. Ned put each bid in a file and gave his stamp. May held out the empty tin. Bo had given the most exact quote of all.

title: The chair promotion
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pip got a new rank at work. His desk was small, but his chair grew tall. The troop had to look up to speak to him. Pip could not reach his files. Dot put steps by his chair. He went down each time a task came in. By dusk he gave the chair his rank and sat on a stool to do the work.

title: The zero inbox contest
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Rex, May, all fictional monkeys
text: Rex gave a prize for an empty inbox. The troop raced to clear their mail. Gus put his box in a bin. Dot sent all hers to Rex. May made a new box with no lid, so notes fell out. Rex won the prize, since his desk broke under all the notes. His box now lay flat under the floor, where no mail could fit.

title: The remote work vine
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo asked to work from a tree. Ned said yes if he could still reach the staff. Bo ran a vine from the tree to each desk. The troop gave tugs to send news. A hard tug drew Ned out of his chair. Bo wrote it down as a plea for help. Ned let him stay in the tree but asked that all new notes come by paper plane.

title: The mouse in the audit
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Rex, all fictional monkeys
text: Dot found a hole in the files. Rex said the staff kept files badly. The troop swept each desk for the lost sums. Gus found a mouse at rest on torn paper. Dot put it in a box with a blank form. The mouse ate the form. Rex said the audit was now done. Dot wrote that the chief had let the sole clue eat the proof.

title: The daily standup
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, Gus, Rex, all fictional monkeys
text: The troop stood for a daily work chat. Rex said no one could sit till each task was clear. Pip asked what his task was. Rex said to state his task. Dot asked who chose it. Rex said they would talk of that next week. Gus put seats under each tail. The troop sat at once. Rex named it a bold pilot and made a new chart.

title: The stolen stapler warrant
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Rex, Ned, all fictional monkeys
text: Ned lost his clip tool and sent Dot to the desk. She saw one bent pin in the rug. The troop kept quiet as she read the pin trail to Rex. His pants were full of them. He had used the clip tool to fix his hem. Dot took it back with a paw. Rex asked if he could keep the pins. His pants were now at risk.

title: The tea expense
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, May, Ned, all fictional monkeys
text: May paid for tea and filed a claim. Ned asked for proof. She gave him the bill. He asked who had drunk it. The troop held up their mugs. He asked if the tea aided work. Dot put cold tea on his stuck desk lock. It swung open. Ned let the claim pass as tool care and asked if they could fix his loud chair with bread.

title: The clock overtime
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Rex, all fictional monkeys
text: Gus put his name in at dawn and left at dusk. Rex paid him for one hour. The clock had died. The troop knew Gus had done the work, but Rex asked for a time stamp. Dot put the dead clock on the desk of Rex. She asked him to fix it in the paid hour. He spent all night at it and gave Gus his wages prior to his next try.

title: The fax jungle
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Rex, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: Bo sent a fax to the next room. The troop heard a grind, then saw paper climb the wall. Bo had fed the fax a long roll. Dot took its tail end and tore it free. The fax had split hello into five parts and put one part on each page. Rex put all five pages on the wall as proof that his firm used less paper.

title: The court of crumbs
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, Gus, all fictional monkeys
text: Pip sued Gus for the last slice of cake. The judge asked for proof. Dot held up a crumb. Gus said a crumb could come from any cake. The troop gave a nod. Dot asked Gus to open his mouth. He had blue icing on his teeth. Gus said that meant only that he liked blue. The judge told both sides to bring whole cakes for a fair test.

title: The tail on the witness stand
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Rex, May, all fictional monkeys
text: May swore to tell the truth. Her tail wound round the court chair. The judge asked if she saw Rex take the pie. May said she saw a red hat. The troop all wore red hats that day. Dot held up the pie tin. May sent her tail to the tin. The judge let her eyes rest and asked her tail to state its case.

title: The lawyer who billed silence
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, Ned, all fictional monkeys
text: Ned said he could win the case with one word. Pip paid him a coin for each pause in court. Ned sat quiet. The troop saw the judge wait. At last Dot said yes. Ned stood and said no. He had used his one word. The judge asked him for proof. Ned said his one word was used up and sent Pip a bill for the pause.

title: The jury snack deadlock
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, Gus, May, all fictional monkeys
text: The troop sat as a jury. They all said yes to the case at once. Then they had to pick a lunch. Gus asked for pie, and May for soup. Pip chose cake, which made both sides cross. Dot sent a note to the judge. It said we are stuck. He sent in ten plain rolls. The troop gave their reply at once and asked never to serve as a jury again.

title: The verdict stamp
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rex made a stamp that said wrong to save the court time. Dot used it on the first file. It was a claim for a leaky roof. The troop heard the judge blame the roof. Rex said the stamp was fine and the file was wrong. Dot took him out in the rain. He found all the proof he could want on his wet fur. He told the crew to fix the roof.

title: The bank vault fan
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo chose to steal a gem from a vault. His troop wore black and crept in. The alarm was quiet, but a loud fan blew their hats away. Dot ran for hers and hit the alarm lever. Bo asked why she let the plan fail. Dot said the hat was on loan. They left the gem and stole back only their own hats, then paid the bank a mop fee.

title: The decoy decoy
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Gus, Rex, May, all fictional monkeys
text: Pip hired Rex as a decoy for the gem theft. Rex hired Gus to play the decoy in his place. Gus sent May, who sent a doll. The troop put the doll by the gate. The guard held it and asked for its name. Pip took the gem. He then had to steal the doll too, since it held all the keys in its tiny felt paw.

title: The getaway cart permit
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dot chose to flee fast in a cart. Ned asked for a pass to park it by the vault. She wrote out the form while the troop took the gold. The guard put his seal on it and gave her a spot far down the hill. Dot moved the cart. The troop went out with the gold at noon, in a legal march led by a cart with a pass.

title: The locksmith souvenir
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gus could open any lock. The troop paid him to open a safe. He did it in one try and took the key as his fee. Dot asked why he kept it. Gus said he had a box of keys at home. He could not open that box. The troop gave him a new box with no lock, and Gus gave back the fee to pay for it.

title: The rubber jewel
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: May stole a ruby from a hall. Her troop met her by the van. Dot let it fall. It went to the far side of the road. It was a soft prop. May went back to ask why. The owner said the real gem had been gone for weeks. May said she would help find it if she could keep the ball. They hired her to guard the empty case all day.

title: The safe with a window
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Rex, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: Rex built a safe no thief could crack. He made a pane so the troop could view the gold. Dot asked if the glass was tough. Rex said no one had tried it yet. Bo hit it with a spoon. The gold fell out. Rex added a cloth and said the flaw was fixed. Dot put the spoon back and took her gold to a new bank.

title: The elevator alibi
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pip used a lift ride as his alibi. He said he was mid ride when the coins were lost. Dot read the lift log. The troop had used it all day, but Pip had never hit a knob. He had been on the roof of the car. Dot found the coins under his tail. Pip said he was just there to hold them down so they would not roll.

title: The merger of snack clubs
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Rex, May, all fictional monkeys
text: Gus ran a pie club. May ran a soup club. Rex made them one club to save money. The troop now got one bowl with pie in soup. Dot said she liked one at a time. Rex said she had fear of new ideas. She sold the bowls as dog food and used the coins to buy two lunch tins. Rex gave the firm his best sales chart yet. It had a dog on it.

title: The office cactus promotion
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Ned, all fictional monkeys
text: Ned gave a prize to the one who asked least. The troop had a row over the prize. Dot chose the plant by the door. It had asked none. Ned gave it a gold badge and its own desk. The plant asked for a large pot. The troop gazed at it. Gus came out from under the desk with a hose and said the new chief could use water.

title: The meeting room booking
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dot got a room for the troop. Rex got the same room for his wet hat. Dot put the hat on a chair and began the talk. Rex came in to claim his slot. The hat sat at the head of the table. The troop made it chair. It gave no long talks and cast a fine shade over the pie. Rex asked to join its team.

title: The badge reader audit
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, Rex, all fictional monkeys
text: Pip got a badge to enter work. The gate would not let him in. He held it with his paw, then his tail. No luck. The troop waved from the glass door. Dot came out and read his badge. It said guest. Pip had done work there for years. Rex wrote old guest on it. Pip still had to knock each day to get past the gate.

title: The legal dictionary dinner
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gus spoke in court with a book of long words. The judge asked what he meant. Gus read a word twice as long. The troop slept on the bench. Dot took the book and asked Gus to use words he used at home. Gus said pie. The judge knew that at once. He split the pie in half and used the book as a tray for both sides.

title: The team building raft
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Rex, May, all fictional monkeys
text: Rex asked the troop to build a raft from junk. Dot tied seats to a desk. Gus added the clock. May put the files on top. The raft could float. Rex asked what they knew now. Dot said their work place made a fine boat. They set sail while Rex ran along the bank. He held the task list and asked them to come back for a talk.

title: The quality assurance plum
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned tried each plum to test its taste. He took one bite to see if it was ripe. The troop sent back each half eaten plum. Dot told Ned to use just one plum for the test. He did, but that plum was sour. He wrote sour on each crate and paid less for them all. Dot found him at lunch with sweet plums and no test log.

title: The empty suggestion box
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: May asked the troop for ideas. She put a box by the door. No notes came in. Dot saw that the slot was too short for notes. May said the box was fine since no one said it was not. Dot put a coin in the slot. May tried to get it out and broke the box. Dot wrote make a wide slot on the new lid.

title: The grant for a ladder
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo asked for steps to fix the roof. Rex said he must prove the roof was bad. Bo sent a photo from below. Rex asked for one from above. The troop made a stack of boxes. Bo went up with his phone. The stack fell, but he got his shot. Rex paid for the steps but said no to the bill for the boxes. Bo sent a photo of those too.

title: The contract with crumbs
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, Gus, all fictional monkeys
text: Pip put his name on a deal at lunch. Jam stuck two pages shut. The troop read just the first page. Dot got them apart at dusk. The next page said Pip owed Gus a pie each week. Gus gave a grin. Dot held the page by the fire. More jam fell off. A third page fell out. It said Gus had to bake each pie. Gus got his apron.

title: The false safe alarm
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned heard a click from the safe and ran. The troop fled with him. Dot had a look. It was a toy clock set for lunch. She took the gold and met Ned by the gate. Ned said he had saved them from a trap. Dot gave him the clock as his cut. He kept it shut all day for fear of the bell. It rang at lunch in spite of that.

title: The open door policy
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rex said his door was never shut. The troop went in to ask for more pay. Rex shut it at once. Dot took off the hinge pins to keep his word true. Wind blew his notes into the hall. Rex said he would pay more if she fixed the door. Dot put the pins back but kept the door wide open. The troop lined up for more pay.

title: The change control fan
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Ned, all fictional monkeys
text: Gus asked to turn on a fan. Ned said each new step must have a form. Gus wrote it out while the troop got hot. Ned asked Dot to test the form. Dot used it as a fan and sent it round. The troop got cool. Ned said no new step was now due. Gus kept blank forms by each desk and put the fan away to make room for them.

title: The court lunch recess
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: The judge said take a break. The troop ran to the yard to play. The judge meant a pause to read the file. Dot found him by the glass door as he eyed their game. He asked what the score was. Dot said tied. The judge took a bat and hit a home run. They came back to court with a clear score and mud on the case file.

title: The decoy beard
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo wore a false beard to enter the vault. His troop wore wigs. Dot used glue to hold each beard in place. At the door a fan blew the wigs off. The guard let them in as a choir on tour. Bo sang while Dot took coins. They could not flee till the guard heard the whole song. Bo had to hum the last verse since the words were in his lost wig.

title: The lease on the desk
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rex made the troop pay rent for each desk. They did work on their laps. Rex then asked rent for seats. Dot went up a tree and did work on a limb. Rex asked rent for the tree. Dot asked for proof he owned it. He went to fetch the deed. The troop moved to the next tree. They sent Rex a bill for shade while he read his deed.

title: The privacy screen
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, May, Ned, all fictional monkeys
text: May asked for a cloth to hide her work. Ned gave her one full of holes. The troop could read each note. Dot hung a coat over it. Ned said that was wrong. May wrote her next notes on the coat. Ned could not read the back, but wore it to see his boss. His boss saw May ask for more pay in huge red words all over his back.

title: The witness clock
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pip took a clock to court to prove the time of the theft. The judge asked it to speak. Dot wound the clock. It rang at noon. Pip said that was the time of the theft. The judge wound it again. It rang at noon once more. The troop gave a sigh. Pip took back the clock and gave the judge his lunch bell. Court ended early for soup.

title: The copier portrait
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Rex, all fictional monkeys
text: Gus put his face on the copy box. The troop saw his nose on each memo. Rex asked who had made the new logo. Dot said the box had. Rex asked for more. Gus tried to clean the glass, but Rex said stop. He liked his new logo. Gus now had to put his face on the glass each week. He lost all taste for the prank by June.

title: The gold sack receipt
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dot took gold from a vault but left a bill. The troop asked why. Dot said the owner must know how much was gone. The owner read it and found she had taken one coin too few. He sent the spare coin by post. Dot said the mail fee cost more than the coin. The owner sent her a rare stamp. Dot now had a stamp worth more than all the gold. She left the gold and took just the stamp books after that.

title: The boardroom swing
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rex used a swing as his chair. The troop had to push him while he spoke. Dot gave one hard push, and Rex flew out the door. He went on with his talk in the hall. The troop heard his voice grow faint. Dot said the talk was done. Rex came back at lunch and spoke well of their drive. He had to push his own swing after that.

title: The briefcase maze
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned put his notes in a case in a case. He said that made them safe. At court the troop saw him open each lock. Dot asked for the key to the tiny case. Ned said it was in the large one. The judge took a break while they had a look. Dot found the notes on top of the first case. Ned had left them there to make a label.

title: The official lunch count
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, May, all fictional monkeys
text: May used the lunch count to see who came to work. Gus took two bowls and wore a new hat for the next count. May put his name down twice. Dot asked why the firm had more staff than desks. Gus put one bowl on the floor. May gave the floor a staff badge. It was never late and never asked for leave. Gus kept its lunch.

title: The bank robber bond
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo went to the bank to ask for gold. The clerk asked if he would like a loan. Bo said no, but the troop liked that plan more. Dot read the terms and said the loan cost too much. Bo put his sack on the desk and left. The clerk put forms in it. Bo got a bill for the time spent on his loan. He paid it with his own gold.

title: The apology form
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rex lost the troop pay. He said sorry and gave Dot a form. She had to sign to say he was sorry. Dot asked where the pay was. Rex gave her a new form to ask for a form. Dot made him sign the first form. She wrote that he owed them his own pay. He gave that pay to the troop. Rex had to fill out six forms to ask for it back.

title: The case of the printed tail
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: A tail mark was on a memo. Dot asked the troop to line up. Rex said no. He was the boss. Dot held the memo up to his chair. The ink was the same as the seat. Rex had sat on the memo to hide it. Dot gave him a clear chair. He hid no more notes under it, but his hat soon grew very full and fell off.

title: The court sketch artist
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: May drew the judge for the news. The troop saw a stern face with huge ears. The judge said the image was wrong. May made the ears small. He still said no. Dot asked what he liked. He asked to look pure. May put a halo on his head. The troop had a good laugh. The judge ruled that he was less pure with a hoop over his head.

title: The duel at five past noon
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Rex, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: Rex asks Bo to meet at noon for a duel. The troop waits by the clock. Bo comes late by five ticks. Rex says the duel is void. Bo says the clock is fast.
