Dot takes both hats and asks them to fix the clock first. They climb the tower and find a loose gear. At noon next day they argue over who did more work, then go for lunch.

title: The sheriff badge polish
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pip wears a badge so shiny the town shuts its eyes. The troop asks him to dull it. Pip says a law chief must shine. Dot puts mud on the badge. Pip wipes it off at once. A thief rides past while he buffs it. Pip sees the thief in the badge and gives chase. He keeps a small muddy spot on it for his next case.

title: The stagecoach fare
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gus stops a coach to take its gold. The coach chief says the coach has only bills. The troop looks in the sacks. Each sack has rent bills. Gus tries to leave, but Dot says he made the coach stop and must pay the late fee. Gus hauls it to town on his own. He gets there with no gold and a new job as a horse with a hat.

title: The cactus shade claim
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Rex, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: Bo buys a patch of land with one plant. He says the troop can rent its shade. At noon the shade is tiny. Dot lies flat and fits under it. Rex tries and gets a thorn in his tail. Bo asks for a fee to pull it out. Dot says she can pay him with shade from her hat. By dusk Bo gives the land in trade for the hat. The troop gets the plant as well.

title: The train tea whistle
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned owns a train that makes no noise. The troop fails to see it at the stop. Dot lends him a bell. He rings it and gets every cow in town to trail it. The train moves at a crawl with cows on its rails. Ned asks for a pipe to use. Dot gives him a tea pot. The train now stops for tea at every stop, and the cows stay home for milk.

title: The lasso laundry line
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Rex, May, all fictional monkeys
text: May joins the rope game. The troop ties hoops for each throw. May fails at each hoop but hooks a pile of wet coats. She lifts them up onto the rope. They dry in the sun while Rex wins the prize. Dot pays May to wash her coats too. Rex asks what he won. His prize is a clean shirt, and May gets the money used to pay for it.

title: The paper deputy
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, Gus, all fictional monkeys
text: Pip names Gus his aide. Gus asks for a badge. Pip has only one, so they share it on odd days. The troop takes cases on the wrong day. Dot draws a new badge on paper. Gus wears it with pride till rain turns it blue. Pip gives him the real one and wears the paper badge. In the next storm he sits under a tree. He gives out soggy notes.

title: The gold rush lunch
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Rex, all fictional monkeys
text: Rex finds a gold flake in the brook. The troop runs to pan for gold. Dot tries one flake and says it is corn. Gus has lost his lunch in the brook. Rex says corn can still be sold. The troop fills sacks and heads to town. Gus meets them with a bill for his lunch. The gold rush ends in a long talk about who owns the bits.

title: The tumbleweed post office
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dot ties a note to a dry weed. Wind rolls it to town. The troop goes with it to see if it gets to the post hut. It rolls past the door and into the yard of Rex. Rex reads the note. It asks him to keep weeds out of the lane. Dot holds out her paw for a mail fee. Rex pays with a new weed and asks her to send his reply.

title: The horse parking ticket
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Ned, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: Bo ties his horse by the bank. Ned puts a fine on its mane. The troop asks what rule it broke. Ned says the horse took two white spots. Dot tests the spots with a rope. One is just large for a hat. Bo puts his hat there and keeps the horse in the other one. Ned asks the hat for rent, and Dot calls for a new mayor.

title: The saloon milk duel
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Rex, all fictional monkeys
text: Gus asks for a very stiff drink in town. The troop goes still. Dot gives him warm milk with five heaps of sugar. Gus tips some on his hat and chair, then asks for more. Soon he is stuck to the seat. Rex gives him a drink to free him. It is plain water. Gus says the town is soft, but his hat stays on the floor since the sugar has glued it there.

title: The wanted poster typo
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: A sign calls Pip a bread thief. The troop spots him by the bread shop. Dot asks why his face is on the wall. Pip reads the sign. The baker meant to call him bread chief. One word is wrong. Dot makes a new sign. Pip gets the job but still wears a mask. Flour dust makes him look a lot worse than the face on his old sign.

title: The wagon wheel feud
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, May, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: May and Bo fight over one wagon wheel. The troop can not solve the claim. Dot cuts the wheel in half. Both say no to their share. Dot says that shows they both care for the wheel. Gus says it shows a half wheel can not roll. Dot glues it back up and keeps it from both. She makes a swing with it and makes both sides pay for rides.

title: The sunset ride invoice
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rex rides west as the red sun sinks. He has saved the town. The troop waves him off. After five ticks he rides back. His horse is owned by Dot, and she wants it home prior to dark. Rex tries to state why he must leave. Dot gives him a broom. He can ride that all night if he wants. Rex walks home, and the broom has a fine view of the red sun.

title: The silver spur alarm
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned wears loud spurs to scare a thief. The troop hears him come from miles away. A thief hides each time the spurs ring. Dot wraps them in cloth. Ned grabs the thief. No one hears him come back. He rings a spoon on his badge. The town comes out to cheer. Dot takes the spoon back and asks him to wash the spurs while she makes soup.

title: The action hero lunch break
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pip has ten ticks to stop a loud alarm. The troop eyes the clock. He leaps over boxes and slips under a gate. Dot uses the open side door. She turns off the alarm and puts lunch on the table. Pip comes in with torn pants and a grand pose. Dot asks him to carry the soup. He says his knees need a stunt aide for that scene.

title: The secret agent beard
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Rex, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: Bo wears a false beard to spy on Rex. The troop says he is too easy to spot. Dot gives him a plain coat to use. Bo goes to the cafe and sits near Rex. Rex asks why he is there. Bo says for tea. Rex gives him a job since that is the first clear reply he has heard all day. Bo tells the troop that the enemy now pays his wages.

title: The laser maze dust
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Rex, May, all fictional monkeys
text: May faces a maze of red beams. The troop tells her to crawl. Dot sees dust in the air and asks for a broom. May uses the broom while Dot turns off each lamp. The beams fade. Rex comes in to test his new alarm and finds a very clean floor. He hires May to sweep. She gets a key to every vault and will never have to crawl again.

title: The rooftop chase lift
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: Gus runs after Bo over the roofs. The troop roars as he leaps a gap. Dot takes the lift and waits at the next roof. She grabs Bo by his tail when he lands. Gus asks why she did not make the leap. Dot says the lift was free. Gus pays for his torn shoes, and Dot rides down with Bo, who asks if the lift can be used to flee too.

title: The explosion countdown clock
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, Gus, Rex, all fictional monkeys
text: Rex sets a timer to scare the troop in a drill. Pip runs in to cut a wire. Dot reads the label. It is an egg timer. Rex says he meant to test their nerve. The timer rings, and Gus comes with eggs. Pip holds the cut wire. His eggs are cold since he cut the stove wire. Dot gives him an egg and asks for the wire back.

title: The secret tunnel tour
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned digs a shaft under the vault. The troop goes after him. At the end they find a sign for tours. Dot has made the shaft a tour stop. Ned says she broke the plan. Dot holds up the tour fees. They have made more than the vault holds. Ned fills the shaft in for a high price tour where each guest must guess what was once under the soil.

title: The villain chair warranty
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, Rex, all fictional monkeys
text: Rex spins in his tall chair to greet the troop. The chair spins on and on. Dot tries the brake, but it snaps off. Rex yells that he will rule the world once each turn. Pip puts a broom in the wheel and stops him. Rex asks who broke his chair. Dot hands him the sales slip. His next plot is to get his coins back from the chair shop.

title: The parachute tablecloth
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo leaps from a tower with a cloth on his back. The troop gasps. Dot says it is her lunch cloth, not a chute. Bo lands in a cart of soft hay. He holds the cloth up as proof his plan won. Dot shows him the hay. Bo hires the cart for each new leap. His next stunt must wait since the cart is busy with hay for the cows.

title: The secret code dinner
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, Rex, all fictional monkeys
text: Pip says the code word is soup. The troop goes to the cafe to meet a spy. Each guest asks for soup, so Pip can not tell who is the spy. Dot asks who wants a fork with it. Rex lifts his paw. The real spy knows the next code is fork. Dot gives him a spoon to use. He must eat lunch till they can talk of the plan.

title: The heroic door kick
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Rex, all fictional monkeys
text: Gus kicks the door to burst into a room. It does not move. The troop asks him to try again. Dot reads the sign that says pull. Gus pulls, but the door still stays shut. Dot shows him the latch. Gus lifts it and gets in at last. Rex has left for lunch. Gus sits in the empty room and asks Dot to film his exit this time.

title: The love letter rent
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, May, all fictional monkeys
text: Pip sends a love note to May. He says her smile is worth all the gold in town. The troop reads it in error and feels he has found a mine. They dig under the porch of May. Dot asks what they seek. Pip shows her the note. May comes out with a bill for the porch. Pip sees the price of a smile when it comes with six bills to fix a porch.

title: The balcony vine
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo sings under the high porch of Dot. His song goes on so long that the troop can not sleep. Dot lets down a vine to pull him up. Bo feels it means she loves him. She hands him a cup of tea and shuts the door. Dot asks him to sip it while it is hot. His lips stay busy. The troop rests while Bo looks at the cup and waits for more tea.

title: The fake wedding cake
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, May, all fictional monkeys
text: May and Gus act as bride and groom so they can get cake. The troop gives gifts too. Dot asks where the vows are. Gus says he is still at work on them. May asks for a slice while they wait. Dot gives them a cake made of wood. It suits the false vows. May and Gus buy real cake, share it with the troop, and keep the wood one as their table.

title: The rose allergy
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Rex, Ivy, all fictional monkeys
text: Rex gives Ivy a rose at their first date. Her nose gives a blast and his hat blows off. The troop grabs it. Rex gets one more rose, but Ivy gives a snort again. Dot gives him a paper rose. Ivy grins and puts it in a vase. Rex asks why it is so much nicer. Ivy says it stays fresh and never makes her nose try to leave her face.

title: The love poem meter
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned sends a poem for Dot. Each line ends with love. The troop says it needs rhyme. Ned swaps every last word to dove. Dot reads it and asks where all the birds came from. Ned goes to buy a dove as proof. The bird eats his poem. Dot likes the bird more than the verse, and Ned asks it to write his next love note.

title: The cafe seat shuffle
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, Gus, May, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: Pip plans to meet May at a cafe. The troop has taken every seat. Dot moves them round so Pip can sit next to May. Gus ends up with three cakes, and Bo loses his soup. By the time Pip sits down, May has gone to pay. Dot moves the whole troop to the till. Pip and May meet there and go to a new cafe to eat in peace.

title: The raincoat rescue
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gus sees Dot stand in the rain and gives her his coat. She gives a nod and runs home. The troop roars for his kind heart. Gus stays in the rain with his tail round his bag. Dot comes back with a spare coat. It is tiny. Gus wears it on his head. Dot says that is where all his best ideas seem to leak out, and they use a large shade hat.

title: The rival love duet
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Rex, May, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: Bo and Rex both sing for May. The troop roars at each tune. May asks them to sing as one so she can judge. Each voice jars, and the panes shake. Dot shuts the glass and turns the duet into a quiet show. May likes the moves and hires both to mime at her shop. Bo and Rex vie to stay quiet. Their next duet has no words at all.

title: The secret admirer stamp
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Ned, Ivy, all fictional monkeys
text: Ivy gets a box from a shy fan. It holds a plum and no name. The troop tries to guess who sent it. Dot looks at the stamp. It has a paw print made by Ned. Ivy gives Ned a hug for the plum. He says he sent a whole crate. Dot takes a trail of pits to Gus. Ivy says Gus saved her from a belly ache, then asks for the crate to store her notes in.

title: The dance card auction
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Rex, May, all fictional monkeys
text: May puts names on a dance card. Rex buys it as a list of debts. He asks each one in the troop for a coin. Dot reads the card and takes his paw. They dance till Rex is dizzy. May says he must dance five times more. Rex gives the card back for free and asks to sit down. Dot puts his last coin in the music box.

title: The train station farewell
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pip runs to stop the train May is on. The troop waves from the track. Pip yells that she must stay. May leans out and asks why. He holds up her lunch. She left it on the table. May takes the bag with her tail and gives him a kiss. The train goes. Pip finds her pass in his paw. It had stuck to the bag. He has to run after the train once more.

title: The mistaken love charm
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: Bo buys a charm to make Dot love him. He wears it to the troop feast. Dot asks him to pass the salt. Bo feels the charm has won. She asks Gus the same thing. Gus gets no nod. Dot sees the charm and reads its tag. It says charm for soup. Bo puts it in his bowl. The soup is fine, and he asks for one more date with it.

title: The love nest zoning
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Ned, Ivy, all fictional monkeys
text: Ivy and Ned build a nest in a tree. The troop calls it a love nest. Dot reads the town rules and says it needs a pass. Ned says birds need none. Dot asks him to prove he is a bird. Ned sings, but Ivy says he can not fly. They move the nest to the floor and call it a rug. Dot says yes to the rug, which keeps the mud off their feet.

title: The candlelit invoice
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Rex, May, all fictional monkeys
text: Rex takes May to a dim cafe. The troop waits out front to hear how it goes. Rex asks for the best meal for all. He can not see the bill in the dark. May sets a wick on fire and reads it aloud. Rex goes pale. Dot gets a big lamp from the road. The bill is for a whole troop. Rex has asked for a meal for all, and they come in to help him eat.

title: The beach proposal shell
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gus puts a ring in a shell for Dot. The troop waits close by. A crab takes the shell and runs off. Gus runs after it down the beach. Dot looks on till he comes back with the crab in a pail. She opens the shell and finds the ring. The crab finds a new home in the empty ring box. Dot says yes to both the ring and the tiny guest.

title: The matching scarf
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, May, all fictional monkeys
text: Pip gives May a scarf to match his own. The troop feels it looks sweet. Dot finds that both wraps are parts of one long strip. Pip and May can not walk apart. They try a date, but each takes a fork to a cake at the far end. Dot cuts the scarf in two. May eats plum, Pip eats pear, and both agree that two short wraps make lunch much less messy.

title: The love quiz referee
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Ivy, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: Bo and Ivy take a quiz to see if they match. The troop reads each query aloud. Bo likes rain. Ivy likes sun. Bo likes pie. Ivy likes soup. Dot asks what both like. They say sleep. Dot ends the quiz and gives them two soft pads. They nap while the troop has a row about the score. When they wake, they agree not to take a quiz till they have eaten lunch.

title: The ice cream reunion
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, May, Ned, all fictional monkeys
text: May meets Ned after years apart. The troop hopes for a grand talk. Ned gives her an ice cream. May takes it and asks what he has done all these years. Ned says he has sold ice cream. Dot asks why he never wrote. Ned holds up his messy paws. May buys him a spoon and a pen. He puts his first note on the paper wrap while she eats his whole stock.

title: The romance novel route
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dot reads that love must start in a storm. She goes out with the troop when rain falls. Bo stays at home and makes tea. Dot comes back wet and cross. Bo gives her a towel. She reads the next page, where the hero gives a towel. Dot shuts the book. Bo asks for it to level his chair. Their first date is tea by a chair held level by a soggy love tale.

title: The box of chocolates map
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Rex, Ivy, all fictional monkeys
text: Rex gives Ivy a map in place of candy. She opens it and sees a trail. The troop goes to a tree, then a bench, then the cafe. Rex waits there with the candy. Ivy asks why he made her walk so far. Rex says he spent all his coins on candy and had none left for a cab. Dot hands him the fare for a bus and eats the first sweet.

title: The love song rehearsal fee
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, May, Ned, all fictional monkeys
text: Ned hires Gus to teach him a love song. The troop hears him sing. Dot asks who the song is for. Ned says May. May comes in with a bill for the room they are using. She owns the music hall. Ned sings to pay his rent. May takes the song but bills him for the echo. Gus gives Ned a small song of just one verse to learn next time.

title: The two picnic blankets
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Rex, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: Bo and Dot each plan a meal. The troop helps carry their bags. They reach the hill and lay two mats side by side. Bo has bread but no jam. Dot has jam but no bread. They join the meals and sit close. Rex says the match is fine. Then rain falls. Both lack a cover. The troop uses one tree while Bo and Dot each get a mat to wrap round their head.

title: The ring size chart
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Dot, May, all fictional monkeys
text: Pip asks May for her ring size. She feels he means the show ring where she works. The troop helps him gauge it. Pip buys a hoop as wide as a hut. He bends a knee to offer it. May grins and uses it for her next show. Dot gives Pip a tiny ring to try again. May says yes, but asks that the big one stay since it earns their rent.

title: The red hat date
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, Gus, Rex, Ivy, all fictional monkeys
text: Ivy waits for Rex in a red hat. The troop wears red hats too, so Rex goes to the wrong table. Gus eats the cake Rex gave him. Dot asks Rex to read the names on the place cards. Rex finds Ivy and gives her a bloom. Ivy says she likes cake more. Gus takes back the empty dish and asks for the bloom in trade. Ivy sends both to the cake shop.

title: The vow in the wind
author: IMI Five Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dot, May, Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: May and Bo write vows on loose cards. Wind takes the cards with no time to read them. Dot runs for the pages. She gets a store list and a rent bill in their place. May reads that she will buy milk. Bo vows to pay rent. The troop roars since those vows are of some use. Dot finds the real vows later and uses them to wrap the cake they take home.

title: The soap actor and the twin door
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Alf was a lost twin in a soap show. Bea stood by the door, set to gasp when he came in. Alf came too soon. Bea gave her gasp to an empty chair, for his tail was stuck on a coat peg. The crew had to stop. Bea freed him, then wrote Enter on the right page. They did the scene once more. Alf came in on cue. Bea gave a real gasp this time, since he wore her coat and all her hats at once.

title: The quiz buzzer loaf
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bex knew each quiz fact, but her bell was mute. Cole told her to clap if she knew the next one. Her soft claps could not reach him. Bex hit a spoon on a loaf tin from the snack desk. The clang rang clear. Cole gave each guest a tin so the round was fair. Bex won by one point. She took the cash prize and got warm bread. They ate it from the same tins, and Cole kept one as a spare bell for the next show.

title: The nature film tame roar
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Cam shot a film about the wild woods. He asked Dot for a great roar. Dot gave a soft peep. Cam put a roar on tape, but it went on while Dot sat still and took fleas from her fur. Dot asked for the real sound. Cam shot her paws as she took seeds from a shell. The film used that quiet scene. Fans tried her neat trick at home. Cam put the roar tape away and paid Dot a whole bowl of seeds.

title: The sitcom couch move
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dax asked to move the couch on the set so he could walk to the door. Eve said it must stay for the wide shot. Dax tried to hop over it, but his tail hit Eve with a thump. They had to stop the take. Eve moved the couch just a bit. The shot was the same, and Dax had a path. He came in with ease. The joke came from his odd hat now, and Eve could drink her tea with no tail in her cup.

title: The talent judge sock
target: Talent contests focus on arbitrary image details
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Flo sang a clear tune, but Gus gave her low marks for her plain socks. Flo asked the judge to wear fine socks and sing it too. Gus put a gold pair on his paws, held the mic, and made a rough peep. The crowd loved the joke. Gus said the socks did not help. Flo sang once more and got fair marks. She kept the plain socks for the last round, with her tail round the stool so no stage cloth could trip her.

title: The news desk tail peek
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Hal read the news at a desk too high for his stool. Ivy saw only the top of his fur on the TV. Hal tried to sit on his tail as a pad, but it slid out. Ivy took a firm box and set the stool on it. Hal read the next item with his whole face in view. A guest asked why he was so tall. Hal let them see the box after the show. Ivy put a safe step by it for each guest to use.

title: The makeover show paint chair
target: Makeover shows prioritize looks over usability
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Jay ran a show that gave old rooms a new look. Kit asked for a chair with a tail slot. Jay made the old chair gold but left the seat solid. Kit sat on its edge and fell off. Jay tried it and felt the same pinch in his fur. They cut a neat slot and made its edges blunt, then put on fresh paint. Kit sat in it for the last shot. The gold shone, but the slot gave her cause to smile.

title: The travel host toll lesson
target: Travel shows create false exotic drama
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Lou said a plain toll booth was a lost altar on his tour show. Mae, who ran the booth, asked the furry host for two coins. Lou tried a magic chant but did not pay. Mae kept the gate shut until he did. The crew shot the whole scene with the real booth name in view. Lou saw his error and got a map. His next show told the troop how to cross the creek, with no chant and no fake tale about the old toll booth.

title: The game show prize goat
target: Game shows neglect winners practical circumstances
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ned won a goat suit on the game show. Ora asked him to pose in it. The suit had four leg holes but no tail hole. Ned could move only in short hops. Ora bent down to cut a slot as the crew stood by. Ned could walk with ease, then gave a loud stage bleat that made Ora leap from her chair. They kept that take as the last gag. Ned took the suit home for the troop play next year, with his tail free to sway.

title: The series recap chain
target: Television recaps replace the actual story
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Paz shot a recap for the new show. Rue asked for a recap of that one, since it went on too long. The furry crew made a third clip to sum up the last two. Soon the day was gone and no new scene was done. Paz drew the last plot on one small card. Rue held it in view for ten beats, then began the new scene. The troop saw the new tale at last. Paz filed the old clips and kept the card for next week.

title: The stunt pool splash
target: Action films hide basic stunt planning
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ash had to leap into a pool for the chase film. Bina asked how deep it was. Ash posed on the rail but did not check. Bina put in a pole and found only a foot of water. The furry actor came down and let her fill it first. They tried a leap from a low step, then did the full shot. Ash hit the water with a great spray and no sore paws. Bina put the depth on a sign and used the pole to hang their wet coats.

title: The romance rose cart
target: Romance films treat expensive gifts as automatic love
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bram got a cart of roses for Cia in the love film. Cia had no room for them in her small flat. The furry actor left the cart in her door in hope of a kiss. Cia asked him to move it so she could go to work. Bram gave the roses to the park crew and went with her to the bus. The scene ended with a wave, not a kiss. He kept one rose in a cup where her tail would not knock it over.

title: The horror prop squeal
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Clem took the lid off a box in the scary film. Dara put on a loud wail. The box held a plain comb. Clem leapt so hard his tail hit the lid. The crew had to fix it. Dara used a quiet creak on the next take. Clem saw the comb, gave his fur a brush, and found a key in its case. The scene had a real clue now. Dara saved the loud wail for the last door, where the key did not fit and the hero had cause to fear.

title: The fantasy sword size
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dell got a huge sword for the quest film. Edie asked him to draw it, but his paws could not reach the whole way. Dell gave its case a tilt and the sword hit the stage floor. Edie gave him a short blade made of wood. The furry hero could walk and bow with no help. The shot was bold when she took it from low down. Dell hung the huge sword over the prop shelf. Its only job now was to look grand at the back of the shot.

title: The science film blinking panel
target: Science fiction relies on useless blinking interfaces
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Finn sat at a panel full of lamps in the space film. Gia asked him to press the key that would start the ship. None had a label. The furry actor took a guess and a lamp went out by his tail. Gia ended the take and wrote Start on one key and Stop on the next. Finn had a clear task now. The scene went well in one take. Gia left the other lamps off, so fans could see which key sent the ship on its way.

title: The spy film cuff
target: Spy heroes confuse elegance with functionality
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Glen wore gold cuffs in the spy film. One cuff held his tail in a snag as he tried to get the coded note. Hana had to wait as he spun in his chair. They took a break to put plain cloth cuffs on his coat. Glen read the note, then left the room with no snags. Hana kept the gold pair in a prop box for a close shot only. Glen asked for the cloth ones in each chase. A free tail gave him more speed than a bit of gold on his paws.

title: The film villain chair
target: Movie villains sit in impractical thrones
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Hugh was a cruel lord in a tall black chair. Iris asked him to turn to face the hero. The chair legs made a noise and held his tail tight. Hugh moved only an inch, then gave a yelp. Iris freed his tail, then put the chair on a board that could roll. Hugh could glide round for the next take. His grim face was good, but the board gave a creak. Iris oiled its axles. Hugh gave his final line at last, with no extra sound to make him seem like a cart full of mice.

title: The western film dust bag
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Jem rode a prop cart in the old west film. Kara shook dust from a bag to make the scene look wild. The furry actor got dust in his nose and could not say his line. Kara swept the track and let the cart make a small cloud on its own. Jem spoke with a clear voice at last. They gave his hat a rinse after the shot. Kara kept the dust bag for the empty road scene. No one would have to take air from the cloud she made there.

title: The musical bus fare
target: Musicals interrupt mundane transactions with songs
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Kip sang for five whole tunes while he tried to board a bus in the stage show. Lila stood with her paw on the fare box. The furry star did a dance on the step but did not pay. Lila asked for the coin first. Kip paid, sat down, and sang the rest from his seat. The scene could move at last, with the bus on its way to town. Lila got a short solo at the next stop about the rule that all tails must stay clear of the doors.

title: The epic film map
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Leo held up a map to show where his army would march. Mina saw the route cross the page edge and jump to the other side. The furry actor had put two maps the wrong way round. Mina gave one a turn and found the road ran by a lake. Leo gave a new talk about the safe shore path. The troop took that route in the next shot. Mina made a neat fold, and the final fight could begin in a place that fans knew from the tale.

title: The rock band shoe beat
target: Rock musicians mistake gear for rhythm
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Max got heavy boots to make his drum beat sound tough. Nora heard him stomp off time at the drum. His tail hit a plate at each wrong step. Nora set a small clock by the drum and asked him to tap in plain socks. Max found the beat again. He kept the boots by the door for the walk home and did the show in socks. Nora gave him a loud cheer. That was the only extra crash for the final tune to end well.

title: The choir fur tickle
target: Choirs prioritize costumes over vocal comfort
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Nim wore a plume ruff for the choir show. It made his fur itch, and he gave a cough in the first verse. Opal asked him to take it off, but Nim felt he would look plain. She gave him a blue scarf that lay flat. Nim sang the next verse with a firm voice. The troop heard the tune at last. Opal hung the plume ruff on a music stand as trim. It could look grand there and stay far from each neck, so the whole choir could sing in peace.

title: The pop tour case
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Odo put ten shiny balls in cases for his pop tour. Pia asked where the drums and mics would fit. The furry star waved at a tiny gap by the van door. Pia took one case lid off. It could hold all the stage gear if the balls came out. Odo kept one ball and left the rest at home. The show began on time with clear sound. Pia put the spare empty cases under the stage, where they held coats and left the aisle free for the crowd.

title: The radio play fruit bite
target: Radio dramas forget incidental live sounds
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Poe ate an apple while he read a royal tale on radio. Quin heard the crisp bite and felt sure a door had split. The furry actor tried to speak with his mouth full. Quin ended the take and gave him a plate out of the booth. Poe ate the rest, wiped his paws, and came back to read the tale in a clear voice. Quin taped one bite for a later food stall scene. The king could now rule in peace until the play asked him to eat.

title: The folk singer rhyme
target: Folk songs force rhymes at the expense of truth
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rai sang that the mill fell down just to rhyme with town. Rosa ran the mill and asked the furry bard to come see it. The walls stood firm, and the wheel spun in the creek. Rai wrote a new verse about grain and flour. He kept the rhyme with carts that came into town. Rosa gave a cheer at the next show and had bread for the troop. Rai tried more ways to rhyme prior to his song about the road, which also still lay firm and would not crack for a verse.

title: The art school apple
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Sol gave an art class with an apple on a desk. Tess drew it as a box, sure that bold ideas would win stars. Sol asked her to bite the apple. Her furry paws held the round fruit, and her teeth left a round mark. Tess drew that shape next. The class could see what she had seen. They ate the fruit after the class. Sol put the box on the wall too, with a label that said Box, not Apple.

title: The grand mural tiny brush
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Tom took a tiny brush to paint a mural on the town hall. Una saw him make one dot per hour while his tail held the paint can. She gave him a wide brush for the broad blue sky. Tom used it, then saved the tiny one for bird eyes. The mural was done by dusk. Una asked him to sign it, and he chose the tiny brush for that final mark. The troop could now see both the whole sky and the small birds from the lane.

title: The mime glass test
target: Mime performers confuse illusion with real obstacles
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Val mimed a glass wall at the fair. Willa tried to hand the furry actor a coin, but Val would not leave his pose. She put the coin on the floor and went away. Val bent down to get it. The crowd saw him pass the wall he had made. He gave a shy bow. On the next round he mimed a door in the wall and used it to take each coin. Willa came back with tea and used that door to give it to him.

title: The dance shoe glue
target: Dancers trust lucky shoes over maintenance
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Wes wore old shoes to each dance. He felt they gave him luck. Yara saw a sole peel away as he spun. His tail held a rail so he could sit to mend it. The glue took time to set. Yara lent him a plain spare pair for the show. Wes did each step well and saw that the skill was his, not in the old soles. He put the old shoes on a shelf at home. The new pair fit his paws with no need for glue.

title: The gallery snack label
target: Art galleries create uncertainty about ordinary objects
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Zed set fruit on a stand at the art show. Ada asked if it was art or a snack. The furry host said it could be both. Ada took a grape, and Zed cried that the work was not whole now. She put it back, but the bite mark was there. Zed wrote a new label about bites. Ada paid for the grape and asked for a clear food table. Zed made one by the door. The next guest could eat there and leave the art alone.

title: The novel chapter cake
target: Authors delay endings to extend a series
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ames wrote a tale about a baker who lost her cake. Bess read each part and asked where it was. Ames added a new quest each time, his pen firm in a furry paw. At last Bess drew a cake on the final page and wrote Found It. Ames saw how tired she was. He wrote a real close at the bake shop door. The cake was there on a cart. Bess paid for the book and made a cake to eat while he wrote his name on the cover.

title: The stage dragon fan
target: Theater effects fail to consider performers
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Axel wore a beast head in the troop play. Bree blew smoke into it with a fan. The furry actor could not see his cue. He gave a roar at the wrong king and fell in a prop well. Bree cut the smoke and got him out. They put the fan by the back wall so smoke would flow past his head. Axel saw the next cue and gave his roar on time. Bree left the fan on low after the show to cool the hot suits.

title: The critic blank notebook
target: Critics prepare conclusions before seeing work
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo wrote a harsh piece about a play while the stage was still dark. Cora saw his notes from her seat. She asked the furry guest what the play was about. Bo did not know. Cora lent him a clean page and asked him to watch the first scene. He found two jokes and wrote them down. His final piece gave those parts high marks and named one slow scene. Cora kept the old page as proof that a neat line could be full of empty air.

title: The poetry rhyme fee
target: Poetry clubs impose arbitrary formal rules
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Cy ran a verse club and took a coin for each line that did not rhyme. Dora read a poem about rain on her fur. The last word was Roof. Cy asked for a rhyme. Dora put a pail under the leaky club roof. Its drips rang in the pause. The troop kept time with their paws. Cy used the fees to fix the leak and ended the rhyme tax. Dora read the poem again next week in a dry room, with no need for a pail.

title: The museum arrow loop
target: Museum signage traps visitors in repetitive routes
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Don put signs on the art hall floor to lead the troop round the rooms. Etta read them and came back to the same bowl six times. Her tail drew a dusty ring by it. Don saw one sign aimed the wrong way. He gave it a turn and took the whole route with Etta. They found the exit at last. Don swept the ring away and gave Etta free entry next month. He added a small map she could hold in her paw on the next tour.

title: The poster tiny date
target: Designers hide critical information in decorative layouts
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ed made a vivid sign for the troop show. Faye could read the huge title from afar but could not find the date. Ed held his paw by tiny print near a blue star. Faye came close, her fur flat on the wall. She asked for a large date and a small star. Ed drew it in bold type and moved the star to the edge. The crowd came on the right day. Ed kept a copy by his desk to test each new date from afar.

title: The puppet crown swap
target: Puppet theaters complicate simple costume changes
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Eli used a new doll for each royal role in the play. Fern had to pull ten furry kings on cords at the back of the small stage. Their tails tied knots in the cords. Eli took a pause and moved them apart. Fern used one doll and a new crown for each king. The troop knew each role by its hat. Eli put the spare dolls by the door, where young fans could pose with them. No cords could tie knots in those tails now.

title: The choir late echo
target: Choirs perform in unsuitable acoustic spaces
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ewan led the choir in a stone hall. Flo sang the last note, then heard it come back after the next verse began. The echo made the furry troop lose their place. Ewan tried a quick beat, which made more noise. Flo hung thick rugs on the back wall. They sang once more, and the words came in order. Ewan kept the rugs for each show. Flo took one home after the final song. It was her own rug, and her floor felt cold.

title: The jazz club soup spoon
target: Jazz performances mistake incidental noises for music
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ezra sang jazz by the food stand. Gale let a spoon fall in a bowl. The furry band took the clang as a cue and chose a new key. Gale held the spoon up to show the cause. Ezra used the new key for one verse, then came back to the tune. Gale moved the bowls away from the stage. The next clang meant soup was ready. The band took a real break and ate from quiet cups prior to the final set.

title: The piano lid pledge
target: Musicians protect image while neglecting instruments
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Finn kept the piano lid shut so his grand coat could lie on it. Hope asked the furry star how the sound would reach the hall. Finn hit a chord, and it came out dull. Hope hung the coat on a hook and put the lid up. The next chord rang clear. Finn did the whole show in his plain vest. The crowd did not miss the coat. Hope put its hook by the door, far from the keys and lid, for each later night.

title: The record label rush
target: Record labels prioritize release dates over readiness
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gus asked Iona to sing her new song that night. The furry star had only half the words. Gus said the rest could wait for the next disc. Iona sang one verse and sat down in the long empty pause. Gus heard how odd it was. He gave her a week to end the tale. Iona wrote about the lost kite at home with its owner. The song came out whole. Gus kept a blank disc on his desk to show what a rush could yield.

title: The dance film close shot
target: Dance films crop away the actual choreography
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Hal shot Joss as she did her dance, but kept the frame tight on her face. The furry star asked him to watch the film. He saw a smile and no steps at all. Joss asked for a wide shot with her tail and both paws in view. Hal moved the lens back and shot the whole dance again. Fans could copy the steps now. He kept one close shot for the final bow. Her feet were still then, and her face could have its turn.

title: The stage rain bucket
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Hank put real water on the stage for the storm scene. Kira slid as she went on it, and her tail held the rail. The furry actor asked for a dry floor. Hank used blue cloth and a sound tape for the next storm. Kira could walk and say her lines with ease. The crowd knew it was rain, but no one got wet. Hank used the water left in his pail to mop the floor after the show. No actor had to cross it then.

title: The art fair price frame
target: Art sellers confuse expensive framing with artistic worth
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ian put a small piece of art in a huge gold frame at the fair. Lana asked what it cost. The furry host named a high price based on the frame. Lana liked the art but had no wall space for all the gold. Ian took it out and gave a price for the paper alone. Lana paid for it and put it in a plain book. Ian used the empty frame round his stall sign. Its shine led the crowd to the real art for sale below.

title: The cartoon cliff rail
target: Cartoons disregard safety even within practical staging
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ivan drew a hero who ran off a cliff and hung in the air. Lena asked why his tail could not grab a tree. Ivan said the fall had a joke in it, his furry face grave. Lena drew a tree in the next panel and let the tail catch it. Ivan added an odd face as the hero swung back to the path. The strip still had a joke. The hero could do his task now. Lena drew a rail in the last panel for the next safe trip.

title: The soap show clock
target: Soap operas stretch time until plots lose sense
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Jake shot a soap scene in which Mara had to wait for her tea. Five shows went by and the cup still had not come. The furry actor asked if her guest must have a dry mouth for a month. Jake put tea in the next scene and let her drink. Mara could talk about the lost ring at last. Jake kept a clock on the set after that. Each long pause had to leave room for the plot to move. The tea pot had a real place by the stove.

title: The news show fake crowd
target: News programs mistake stock footage for live reporting
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Jude put a tape of a large crowd at the back of the news set. The furry host said the town plaza was full. Neve saw a wool coat in the tape, but the live day was hot. She asked Jude to show the real view. Two fans and a cart stood in the plaza. Neve told that true count on air. Jude wrote the date on the old tape and kept it for past clips. The next live count came from the plaza lens with no old coats in view.

title: The quiz prize bill
target: Game shows hide practical costs of winnings
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Jules won a huge piano on the quiz show. Nola asked the furry guest to sign for it. Jules saw that cart hire to get it home cost more than his rent. He asked for a small drum. Nola read the prize list and let him pick one that fit in his bag. Jules hit it on the bus home, then quit when asked. Nola added cart costs to the prize cards. The next guest knew the full price prior to using a pen to claim a shiny prize.

title: The costume coat hem
target: Costume departments use dramatic accessories impractically
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Karl wore a long royal coat on stage. Oona had to walk after him with its tail end in her paws. It would catch on seats if she let go. The furry actor saw her lose all her own cues. They put the coat hem up with pins until it came to his knees. Karl could walk alone, and Oona could play her role. The coat was still grand from afar. After the bow Karl took the pins out, and Oona hung it flat for the next show.

title: The encore note card
target: Performers fail to distinguish demand from closure
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Kent sang a last song each time he heard claps. Pru tried to leave the hall, but the furry star began again when she gave a clap on her way out. She held a card that said Good Night. Kent bowed and let the song end. The troop could go home at last. Pru put the card by the mic for the next show. Kent used it after one extra tune, then gave a small wave. The crowd could clap at the close and still walk out of the open door.

title: The pea with a receipt
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pip, Queen Ada, all fictional monkeys
text: Queen Ada hid a pea beneath the guest bed. Pip, a small monkey, felt no lump at all. His tail did find a receipt that said the bed cost ten bananas. He took the receipt to Ada and asked why a fine bed had loose springs. Ada tried it herself. One spring poked her fur. She hired Pip to mend the bed and served the pea in soup.

title: A slipper for the wrong foot
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Moss, Prince Jem, all fictional monkeys
text: Moss left one glass shoe at the ball. Prince Jem toured the woods with it, sure he would find his bride. Each monkey tried a foot. Moss tried his tail. The shoe fit that best, since he had worn it as a tail bell all night. Jem felt a bit silly. They hung the shoe over the gate and rang it when fresh bananas came to the hall.

title: The bean pole toll
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Nell, Giant Gus, all fictional monkeys
text: Nell grew a bean stalk so tall that clouds caught in its leaves. Giant Gus charged each monkey three bananas to climb it. Nell saw that he used the toll to buy boots that crushed her beans. She set a small stall at the root and sold bean soup. Gus climbed down for lunch. His boots sank in the mud, so he stayed to help pick beans in bare feet.

title: The wolf stamp
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo cried that a wolf had come. No wolf came, but all the monkeys left their work. Wren gave him a red stamp to use for real danger. Bo stamped his own fur just to test it. The mark would not wash off. When a wolf did pass, Bo held up his red tail. The troop shut the gate, then paid him bananas to guard it with a plain bell.

title: The short cut race
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rook raced Tess round the lake. His monkey feet flew while Tess took small steps. He found a short cut through a shed full of bananas and stopped to eat. Tess reached the last bend and sat down. A cart had tipped and blocked the route to the line. Rook came out with a full mouth and helped her shift it. They crossed at once, and shared the prize bench for a nap.

title: The crown in the well
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: King Kit, Frog Finn, all fictional monkeys
text: King Kit dropped his crown in a well. Finn, a monkey in a frog suit, said a kiss would bring it back. Kit peered down and saw the crown caught on a nail. He lent Finn his long tail as a rope. Finn fetched it, but the wet suit stuck to his fur. Kit paid him bananas and a dry towel. Finn quit the frog act and opened a tool shop.

title: The three small inns
target: Three houses and a hungry wolf
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Ash, Elm, Oak, all fictional monkeys
text: Ash built an inn of straw. Elm used sticks. Oak used brick. Their monkey guests ate bananas in all three. A great wind blew down the first two inns, and all the guests ran to Oak. His door was too small for the crowd. Ash wove a broad mat roof and Elm built a long bench in the yard. Oak sold his bricks to buy tea for the new open inn.

title: The mirror takes a day off
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Queen Bea, Dot, all fictional monkeys
text: Queen Bea asked her mirror who had the best fur. The mirror gave no reply. Dot, the monkey who cleaned it, found a leaf stuck over its mouth. Bea pulled the leaf away. The mirror asked who had the best manners. Bea brought Dot a chair and some bananas while she worked. The mirror praised the clean glass. Bea liked that answer enough to stop asking about her own fur.

title: The trail of shells
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
text: Lark and Reed left bits of banana on the path to mark their way home. Birds ate the bits. The young monkeys reached a pond and saw no trail. Reed cracked nuts and placed the shells in pairs on stones. Lark climbed a tree to spot their roof. They laid more shells on the path toward it and came home at dusk. Next day they took a map and kept the bananas for lunch.

title: The goose on a break
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: May, Goose Gil, all fictional monkeys
text: May kept a goose that laid gold eggs. Gil was a monkey in a feather cape, and the eggs were brass balls from his shed. May asked for ten more each day. Gil put down his cape and showed her his sore hands. May helped polish the old balls. They sold them as door bells and split the bananas they earned. The goose nest became a soft chair for both to rest.

title: A boot full of wishes
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sol, Fairy Rue, all fictional monkeys
text: Fairy Rue gave Sol three wishes. Sol wished for more bananas, then for a boot to hold them all. The boot grew so large that it blocked his hut. His monkey tail stuck beneath the heel. Rue waited for his last wish. Sol asked for the boot to have wheels. He rolled it to the square and made a fruit cart. Rue bought the first bunch and got a free ride.

title: The dragon needs a shelf
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sir Nim, Drake, all fictional monkeys
text: Sir Nim rode to a cave to face a dragon. Drake was a large monkey with a smoke pot and wings of cloth. His heap of bananas kept falling on the pot, so the cave smelled burnt. Nim put down his lance and built a shelf. Drake stacked the fruit on it and took off the wings. Nim earned a medal for fire safety, though he asked for a chair instead.

title: The giant shade hat
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Poe, Giant Meg, all fictional monkeys
text: Giant Meg wore a hat that hid the sun from the village. Poe, a monkey tailor, climbed its brim to ask her to move. She could not see where her feet went. Poe cut eye holes in the hat, then tied its top with his tail. Meg saw the huts and stepped round them. She paid him with bananas and used the spare cloth to shade the village in hot weather.

title: The fox and the low grapes
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Fox Fen, Ivy, all fictional monkeys
text: Fen wore a fox mask and claimed he could reach any fruit. A bunch of grapes hung just above his tail. He said they must taste bad. Ivy, a young monkey, placed a box below the vine and picked one. It was sweet. Fen climbed the box too, but it tipped. Ivy held it still. Fen shared the grapes and traded his mask for a basket that could hold fruit but could not boast.

title: The red cloak laundry
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Red Ren, Aunt Uma, Wolf Wes, all fictional monkeys
text: Ren took soup to Aunt Uma in her bright red cloak. Wes, a monkey in a wolf mask, tried to lure her down a dark path. Ren knew him by the strip of fur near his nose. She asked him to carry the soup while she washed her cloak in the stream. He waited so long that he got hungry. At the hut they shared soup and bananas, and he hung up his mask.

title: The spell that kept time
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Belle, Mage Lux, all fictional monkeys
text: Mage Lux cast a sleep spell on the hall. Belle stayed awake because she was outside peeling bananas. The monkey cooks slept over cold pans, and no one could serve lunch. Belle wound the old clock and set its bell for noon. The chime woke the hall. Lux said the spell should last years. Belle pointed to the lunch list. He changed it to a nap spell and joined the queue.

title: A shoe shop for elves
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Cobbler Dex, Elf Ona, all fictional monkeys
text: Dex left leather out for elves to sew at night. Ona, a monkey in an elf cap, made six shoes, but all had holes for tails. Dex found them useless until rain flooded the lane. He wore one on his tail and kept his fur dry. He sold the rest as tail boots. Ona got fair pay in bananas, and Dex moved the sewing shift to day so she could sleep.

title: The flute with one note
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Piper Hal, Mayor Liv, all fictional monkeys
text: Hal said his flute would rid the town of pests. He could play only one note. The monkeys came out to ask him to stop. Mayor Liv saw their tails twitch at each squeak and had an idea. She put them in a line to sweep the street in time. Hal played until each crumb was gone. The pests left for lack of food, and Hal earned bananas for a short song.

title: The lake gives back a spoon
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Axe Ari, Lady Eda, all fictional monkeys
text: Ari dropped his axe in the lake. Eda rose from the reeds with a gold spoon and asked if it was his. The monkey said no. She brought a silver fork. He said no again. At last she found the axe, stuck in a log beside the bank. Ari freed it with his tail. Eda gave him the spoon for his care. He used it to serve her mashed bananas on shore.

title: The bear chair repair
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Goldie, Bear Ben, all fictional monkeys
text: Goldie tried each chair in the bear hut. She was a monkey guest, but had lost her invite in the wind. One chair broke beneath her tail. Bear Ben came home and found her mending it with rope. He read the invite that stuck to his boot. The chair was his gift to her, though he had built it too small. They made a wider seat and ate bananas while the glue dried.

title: The tower has stairs
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Rae, Prince Cal, all fictional monkeys
text: Rae lived in a tower and let down her long tail when Prince Cal came. He climbed halfway, then sneezed from her fur. Rae hauled him in and showed him the stairs behind a curtain. The monkeys had missed them for years because the curtain said Keep Out. Cal took the sign down. Rae opened a stair cafe and sold bananas at each landing. Cal used the lift, which was a plain bucket.

title: The king has pockets
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: King Ned, Weaver Opal, all fictional monkeys
text: Opal sold King Ned a suit that no one could see. Ned walked out in his fur and asked where to put his keys. The monkey weaver offered a bag. Ned asked why he had paid for a suit with no pockets. Opal gave back the bananas and sewed him a plain coat. At the parade Ned held up each pocket for the crowd. They cheered the coat because it could hold their lost keys.

title: A troll with a ticket
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Troll Tom, June, all fictional monkeys
text: Tom sat under the bridge and charged a riddle as toll. June, a monkey bus driver, had twenty guests who all gave the same wrong guess. Tom would not let them pass. June handed him a ticket and a bunch of bananas. He rode across with them to see where the bus went. At the far bank he found a riddle club and stayed there, leaving the bridge free for traffic.

title: The wish fish dinner
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Fisher Fae, Fish Milo, all fictional monkeys
text: Fae caught a fish that offered wishes. It was Milo, a monkey in a blue suit, hiding from his dish chores. Fae wished for a grand meal. Milo led her home and cooked beans with bananas. She wished for clean plates. He sighed and washed them with his tail wrapped round the brush. Her last wish was for him to join her at the table. He did, still damp, and ate his share.

title: The moon cheese trial
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Otto, Sage Tess, all fictional monkeys
text: Otto saw the moon in a pond and thought it was cheese. He told the other monkeys to drain the pond. Sage Tess put a bowl of water beside it. The moon shone in that too. Otto tried a spoon and got only water on his fur. Tess gave him cheese on a leaf with ripe bananas. He ate that and left the moon in the pond so fish could have a lamp.

title: The acorn budget
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Ant Amy, Grass Gil, all fictional monkeys
text: Amy stored acorns for winter. Gil played songs and stored none. The monkeys met when snow sealed the nut shed. Amy could not reach its latch through the drift. Gil tapped a tune on the roof until the loose snow slid off. Amy opened the shed and shared nuts and bananas. Gil played while she counted the sacks. In spring he built a drum with a small food bin inside it.

title: The proud pond swan
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Duck Dax, Swan Sue, all fictional monkeys
text: Dax wore a duck cap to fit in at the pond. Swan Sue said his brown fur spoiled the flock photo. The monkey took his cap off and held it over the lens as a shade. The glare went away. Sue saw that the photo looked much better. She asked Dax to stand beside her for a new one. He did, with bananas in his cap, and every bird leaned toward the snack.

title: The crane lunch
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Fox Flo, Crane Kai, all fictional monkeys
text: Flo served soup on flat plates, though Kai had a long paper beak for the play. Kai planned revenge with tall jars. The monkey cooks stopped when both spilled soup on their fur. Flo found wide cups and Kai took his beak off. They ate in peace, then used the jars for flowers. Their guests brought bananas and asked to keep the plates, which made fine hats for the next play.

title: The lion net review
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Lion Leo, Mouse Min, all fictional monkeys
text: Leo wore a lion mane and laughed at tiny Min. Then his mane caught in a net while he chased bananas. Min was a small monkey with neat claws. She cut one knot and let him crawl out. Leo offered her a place on his royal staff. Min asked for a stool at the fruit stall instead. He built it that day, and she could reach the ripe bunches without his help.

title: The crow pebble tax
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Crow Cam, Wells Willa, all fictional monkeys
text: Cam wore black wings and dropped stones in a jug to raise its water. Willa watched the monkey work for an hour. Each stone cost him a banana at the stone stall. She tipped the jug into a shallow bowl. Cam drank, then took the stones back and got his bananas back. He kept one smooth stone as a weight so his new bowl would not blow away in the wind.

title: The wolf choir
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Wolf Walt, Kids Kira, all fictional monkeys
text: Walt wore a wolf suit to test the door guard. Kira asked him to sing the family song before she let him in. His voice was so rough that all the young monkeys laughed. He showed his bare tail, but Kira still said no. Walt fetched his lute and learned the tune from a window. At dusk she opened the door. He brought bananas, and they gave him the low part in their choir.

title: The magic pot lid
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Penny, Mage Mel, all fictional monkeys
text: Mel gave Penny a pot that made hot oats on command. Penny forgot the stop word, and oats filled the monkey hut. She slid the lid under the stream and used it as a chute to the yard. Friends came with bowls and bananas. Mel came back to find a feast in the yard. He said the stop word was Enough. Penny carved it on the lid, then asked for one last small bowl.

title: The twelve dancing tails
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Princess Pia, Guard Glen, all fictional monkeys
text: Pia and her sisters wore out their shoes each night. Guard Glen hid by the door to find out why. The monkeys used the shoes as drums while their tails danced. Pia feared the king would ban the noise. Glen lined the soles with soft moss and helped them set a quiet beat. The king slept well, the shoes lasted, and Glen got bananas for his first lesson in tail dance.

title: The ginger hut lease
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Baker Bess, Hans Hal, all fictional monkeys
text: Hal found a hut made of cake and bit the wall. Bess came out with a rent bill. The monkey said he thought it was a free sample. Bess showed him the plain door and asked him to mend the hole before rain came. Hal baked a brick of oats and bananas. It fit snugly. Bess hung a Sample sign on a tray outside, and Hal became her first regular guest.

title: The old dog mask
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dog Don, Pup Pat, all fictional monkeys
text: Don said he was too old to learn new tricks. Pat tied a dog mask over his monkey face and asked him to fetch a stick. Don refused until the stick held a bunch of bananas. He brought it back with his tail. Pat tried that too and fell on his nose. Don taught him how to curl his tail first. Pat gave him the fruit and asked for a slower lesson next time.

title: The donkey song ban
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Donkey Dot, Mayor Max, all fictional monkeys
text: Dot sang so loudly that the town asked her to leave. She was a monkey in a donkey hood and took the news badly. Mayor Max heard her voice shake loose ripe bananas from a high tree. He hired her to sing in the grove each morning. Dot could now choose any song she liked. The town slept late, the fruit crew wore ear plugs, and the hood became a sack for the crop.

title: The spindle cap
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Rose, Aunt Eve, all fictional monkeys
text: Rose found a spindle in the attic, despite a royal ban. The monkey touched its point and got a small prick. Aunt Eve heard her yelp and brought a bandage. No one fell asleep. Rose asked why the king had banned all sewing. Eve showed her a cap that kept the sharp tip covered. They made caps for every spindle and used the saved cloth to wrap bananas for the winter fair.

title: The mermaid dry seat
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Mira, Sailor Sid, all fictional monkeys
text: Mira wore a fish tail in the lake show. She wished to sit on land, but the tail made each chair tip. Sailor Sid brought a stool with a slot for it. The monkey slid in and ate bananas without falling. Mira kept the fish tail for shows and her own tail for walks. Sid put wheels on the stool so she could roll from the lake to lunch in one smooth trip.

title: The sand castle king
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: King Kip, Builder Uma, all fictional monkeys
text: Kip ruled a sand castle and charged monkeys bananas to enter. Uma warned him that the tide would soon reach the gate. Kip ordered a taller wall. Uma dug a ditch instead and led the water around the yard. The castle still fell at dusk, but the guests had dry fur. Kip gave them their fruit back. Next day he made a sand park with free gates and a tide sign.

title: The seven soup bowls
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Snow Sia, Dwarf Dell, all fictional monkeys
text: Sia found seven bowls in a small hut and filled them with soup. Dell came home with six other monkeys, all in dwarf hats. They had meant the bowls for paint. Sia offered to wash them, but Dell tasted the soup and asked her to stay. They painted the hut after lunch. Sia used mashed bananas to make yellow paint for the door, which smelled so good that bees came to visit.

title: The royal pumpkin cart
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Cindy, Fairy Fay, all fictional monkeys
text: Fay turned a pumpkin into a cart for Cindy. At twelve it would turn back. Cindy, a monkey who hated waste, drove to the ball with bowls and a spoon. When the clock struck, she parked beside the kitchen. The wheels became seeds and the cart became a large pumpkin. She made soup for the late guests and packed bananas for the walk home. Fay admired the empty peel at dawn.

title: The wishing well queue
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Wes, Keeper Kay, all fictional monkeys
text: Wes threw a coin in the well and wished for bananas. Kay, the monkey keeper, fished the coin out to pay for rope. Wes said the wish had gone wrong. Kay showed him the broken bucket. Wes tied his tail to the rope and helped haul water for the fruit trees. A month later they picked a full crop. Kay gave him the first bunch and kept the well free of coins.

title: The hare alarm clock
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Hare Hank, Tortoise Ty, all fictional monkeys
text: Hank took a nap during the race and set an alarm in his fur. Ty walked past, heard it ring, and thought a monkey needed help. He woke Hank, who sprang up and ran the wrong way. Ty called him back to the trail. They came in late, after the prize bananas had gone soft. Hank mashed them into cake. Ty cut two large slices and they ate beneath the silent clock.

title: The straw gold label
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Spinner Sal, Imp Ian, all fictional monkeys
text: Ian offered to spin straw into gold if Sal guessed his name. Sal, a monkey with a seed shop, asked why anyone wanted gold straw. Ian said it sold well for nest trim. Sal painted a bundle yellow and labeled it Plain Straw. Birds bought that instead. Ian told her his name without a guess and asked for work. She paid him bananas to paint labels, where his fine small brush proved useful.

title: The queen of crumbs
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Queen Qia, Baker Bo, all fictional monkeys
text: Qia claimed every crumb on the bakery floor as royal land. Bo swept the crumbs up before she could build her palace. The monkey queen sat on his broom and refused to move. Bo gave her a tray where crumbs could stay dry. Qia made a tiny castle on it and charged ants a leaf to enter. Bo served bananas beside her tray, and the ants left his good bread alone.

title: The rainbow gate key
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Rin, Wizard Wil, all fictional monkeys
text: Wil told Rin that a key lay at the end of the rainbow. Rin crossed fields but the colors moved with her. The monkey came back wet and cross. Wil looked at his own wall and saw the key hung under a rainbow artwork. He had left out that part. Rin opened the garden, picked bananas, and painted a map on the gate. Wil now used that map when he gave advice.

title: The crown itch
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Prince Pax, Witch Wye, all fictional monkeys
text: Pax put on a cursed crown and felt an awful itch. Wye said only a rare herb could end it. The monkey prince took off the crown to scratch his fur. The itch stopped. Wye found rough wire inside the rim and blushed. She padded it with wool. Pax wore it for the feast, then hung it on a hook. He paid Wye in bananas for the pad and skipped the herb quest.

title: The rescue ladder rental
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Princess Plum, Knight Noel, all fictional monkeys
text: Plum offered a prize to anyone who could reach her balcony. Noel rode up with a ladder, but every knight wanted to borrow it. The monkey charged one banana each and watched them climb. Plum came down the same ladder to join the queue for snacks. She gave Noel the prize for making a safe route. He used it to buy more ladders, and Plum ran the desk that lent them out.

title: The marble egg mother
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Mum Mae, Chick Cora, all fictional monkeys
text: Mae found a marble egg and sat on it for days. Cora, a young monkey, brought her bananas while she waited for it to hatch. At last Cora saw a small hole through the stone. It was a bead from the royal curtain. Mae gave it back and got a soft cushion as thanks. She sat on that instead. Cora used the cushion box as a nest for toy birds that hatched on time.

title: The wise owl glasses
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Owl Odo, Fern, all fictional monkeys
text: Odo gave advice from a high branch while wearing an owl hood. Fern asked where her lost bananas had gone. He pointed to a cloud. Fern saw them on the branch beside his tail. The monkey had worn the hood back to front and could see only through its ear holes. She turned it round and gave him the fruit. Odo checked that he could see his own feet before each new advice session.

title: The pancake ceiling
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Chef Chip, Judge Jo, all fictional monkeys
text: Chip flipped his pancake so high it stuck to the ceiling. Judge Jo waited with her fork. The monkey chef climbed a shelf, but his tail knocked flour over the stove. Jo handed him a mop. Chip swept the cake down onto a clean tray and served it with bananas. Jo gave him a prize for floor care. He hung it at eye level and kept each new flip below it.

title: The soup whistle
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Cook Cleo, Pip, all fictional monkeys
text: Cleo asked for silence in her soup shop. Pip slurped once and got sent outside. The young monkey heard the pot whistle behind him. Cleo ran out to scold the sound, but Pip pointed at the stove. The pot was too full. He held a bowl while she poured some out. They added bananas to cool it. Cleo put a bell by the door and let guests ring it for more soup.

title: The cake tower brace
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Baker Baz, Host Hope, all fictional monkeys
text: Baz stacked cakes taller than his head. Hope asked how he would cut them for the judges. The monkey pushed his tail through the middle as a brace, which made the top cake tilt. Hope slid small plates beneath each layer. Baz served a whole row of flat cakes instead. The judges could taste them all without ladders. Baz put a tiny ladder beside one cake and won the prize for best tower.

title: The secret sauce jar
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Chef Cora, Aunt Ann, all fictional monkeys
text: Cora would not share her secret sauce with Aunt Ann. She hid the jar in a hollow stump. A monkey troop mistook it for glue and used it on a kite. Cora found the kite stuck to the tree, with a smell of bananas. Ann helped soak the joints in warm water. Cora wrote the sauce name on a fresh jar and gave Ann the recipe. The kite flew after lunch with no sticky tail.

title: The tiny pie slice
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pie Pam, Judge Jed, all fictional monkeys
text: Pam baked one pie for seven judges. Jed said each slice must weigh the same. The monkey used a scale, but crumbs kept falling into her fur. Pam cut the pie into small cubes and gave each judge a bowl. Jed still wanted a grand slice for the photo. Pam shaped his cubes into a wedge and put bananas beside it. He took the photo, then ate the same share as the rest.

title: The oven timer duet
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Cook Kit, Singer Sam, all fictional monkeys
text: Kit had ten minutes to bake buns on the show. Sam sang the last count so slowly that the monkey thought he had an hour. His buns burned while Sam held the last note. Kit sliced off the dark crust and made crunchy bits for soup. He served bananas as dessert. Sam got a real clock for the next round. Kit asked him to sing only when the food had left the oven.

title: The spoon draft
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Coach Cal, Spoon Sue, all fictional monkeys
text: Cal picked cooks by how fast they could stir. Sue used her tail and won a place on the monkey team. In the final, the soup needed slow care. The fast cooks spilled it onto their fur. Sue tied a bell to her spoon and kept it quiet. Cal made the team follow her pace. They served smooth soup with bananas and put the silent spoon above the cup they had won.

title: The salad trophy
target: Health food contests with absurd prizes
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Chef Sage, Judge Jay, all fictional monkeys
text: Sage made a salad in the shape of a trophy. Jay gave the monkey a real trophy for it. Sage tried to eat that one and found it much too hard. Jay said prizes were for shelves. Sage had no shelf, only a small hut full of bananas. He traded the trophy for seeds and grew a garden. At the next contest he served bowls and asked for an empty sack as his prize.

title: The burnt toast portrait
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Toast Tom, Guest Gia, all fictional monkeys
text: Tom called his burnt toast a bold new dish. Gia took one bite and coughed black dust onto her fur. The monkey chef said that was the style. Gia scraped the toast and used the dark bits to draw his face on a plate. Tom laughed, then made fresh toast at low heat. He served it with bananas and put her art on the menu. The new dish was called Take Your Time.

title: The rolling pin baton
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Baker Bea, Runner Ren, all fictional monkeys
text: Bea gave Ren a rolling pin for the kitchen relay. Ren raced so fast that dough wrapped round his monkey tail. He reached the next table with no dough left on the tray. Bea dusted his tail with flour and rolled it over the sheet. The dough came off in a neat spiral. They baked it with bananas inside. The judges asked for the recipe, so Bea drew a tail beside the rolling pin.

title: The goalie fruit basket
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Goalie Gus, Coach Nell, all fictional monkeys
text: Gus had no gloves for the big match. Nell gave him two fruit baskets. The monkey caught each ball, but bananas fell out at every save. The crowd ate them and cheered. At the last kick, a peel lay beside his foot. Gus used his tail to sweep it clear and caught the ball cleanly. Nell bought real gloves with the prize coins. Gus kept a basket by the goal for snacks at the break.

title: The slow sprint camera
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Runner Rue, Judge Finn, all fictional monkeys
text: Rue trained for the sprint, but the race camera could see only tails. Every monkey curled a tail over the line before their feet arrived. Judge Finn could not choose a winner. Rue set a second line behind the first and asked each runner to touch it with a foot. They raced again without tricks. Rue came third and won bananas for fixing the rules. Finn used the tail photo as a funny poster.

title: The tennis moon shot
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Ace Amy, Coach Dot, all fictional monkeys
text: Amy hit a tennis ball into the clouds. Dot praised her power, then asked how to win a point without a ball. The monkey tried a softer serve. It rolled under the net and hit a crate of bananas. Dot used a lid as a low target. Amy hit it ten times, then served over the net at last. The lost ball fell on the court at dusk and scored nothing at all.

title: The pool lane knot
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Swimmer Sid, Ref Rae, all fictional monkeys
text: Sid tied his tail to a float so he could rest between laps. During the race it caught the lane rope. The monkey kept going in one small circle. Ref Rae halted the race and cut the knot. Sid used the float to hold bananas at the pool edge instead. He swam the full course with a free tail. Rae gave him a plain ribbon and kept the shears close for the next event.

title: The jump pole lunch
target: Athletic equipment confused with food tools
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Jumper Jem, Coach Kim, all fictional monkeys
text: Jem used a tall pole to leap over a bar. Kim saw him stop halfway and pick bananas from a branch. The monkey said his grip needed a snack. Kim moved the bar to an open field. Jem jumped cleanly, then missed the branch where he had planned to land. Kim placed a soft mat there. Jem won the event and ate his fruit on the ground, with the pole flat beside him.

title: The chess cape
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Chess Chet, Rival Ora, all fictional monkeys
text: Chet wore a cape to every chess match. It made his monkey tail itch, but he thought it brought luck. Ora saw the cape brush three pawns off the board. They stopped and put the pieces back. Chet took the cape off and used it as a shade over their bananas. He lost the match by one move. Ora lent him her notes, and he studied them in the cool shade he had made.

title: The mascot penalty
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Mascot Moe, Captain Cass, all fictional monkeys
text: Moe wore a giant banana suit to cheer the team. His monkey tail dragged behind and tripped Cass near the goal. The referee sent Moe to the bench. Moe cut a hole for his tail, then made small flags from the spare cloth. He waved them from his seat and kept score with bananas. Cass scored twice. Moe gave the team the fruit and folded the suit into a tidy bag for the flags.

title: The bowling tail lane
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Bowler Belle, Lane Lee, all fictional monkeys
text: Belle rolled balls with her tail to impress the crowd. One ball curved into the snack stand and crushed the bananas. Lane Lee closed her lane until she learned to aim. The monkey used soft balls and empty cups in the yard. By dusk she could hit one cup at a time.
