Belle swept the snack stand, made a fresh fruit mash, and rolled a plain strike with both hands the next day.

title: The gold medal weight
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Lifter Lou, Coach Cole, all fictional monkeys
text: Lou trained to lift the largest weight in the hall. He won a gold medal so heavy it pulled his neck down. The monkey asked Cole to help him wear it. Cole put it on a stand, but the stand sank into the soft floor. Lou used the medal as a door wedge and hung a small leaf on his chest. He could carry his bananas again, which felt like a better prize.

title: The coach chalk storm
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Coach Craig, Player Pia, all fictional monkeys
text: Craig filled a board with arrows for the final play. Pia could not see which way to run. The monkey coach wiped half the lines away, then half again. Only one arrow stayed. Pia ran that way and found a basket of bananas beside the field. Craig had drawn on the lunch map by mistake. They ate, then drew the play on the proper board. Pia scored before the chalk dust settled.

title: The cape caught in the bus
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Hero Hal, Driver Di, all fictional monkeys
text: Hal leaped onto the bus to save it from a loose wheel. His cape caught in the door, leaving the monkey stuck on the step. Di stopped the bus and freed him. Hal used the cape to wipe grease off the axle while Di fixed the bolt. They drove to the shop at walking speed. The riders paid Hal with bananas. He cut his cape short and kept a wrench in the hem.

title: The alarm duck
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Hero Hett, Duck Dan, all fictional monkeys
text: Hett heard a loud quack and flew to the pond. Dan, a monkey in a duck suit, was testing the village alarm. Hett saved him from a puddle he meant to sit in. Dan made a sign that said Test Day. Hett helped hang it beside the bell and waited for a real call. When a cart tipped, they both went to lift it. The driver gave them bananas and a quiet thank you.

title: The mighty jar lid
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Hero Hugo, Cook Cat, all fictional monkeys
text: Hugo could lift a bridge, but he could not open a jam jar. Cat watched the monkey strain until his fur stood up. She tapped the lid with a spoon and ran warm water round its rim. Hugo turned it with one finger. He ate jam on bananas, then asked to learn the trick. Cat made him wash the spoon first. Hugo added a small tap move to his list of great powers.

title: The hidden hero badge
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Hero Hen, Friend Fay, all fictional monkeys
text: Hen changed into her hero suit behind the fruit stall. Fay saw her tail under the curtain and knew at once. The monkey begged her to keep the secret. Fay agreed, but the suit had no room for the bananas Hen had just bought. Fay lent her a plain bag. Hen saved a kite from a roof and came home with the fruit. Fay kept the badge safe while Hen washed the dusty suit.

title: The villain tea break
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Hero Herb, Villain Vee, all fictional monkeys
text: Vee stood on a crate to declare his plan to steal all the bananas. Herb waited in peace until the monkey villain lost his voice. Herb offered tea. Vee sat down and said he wanted fruit for his hungry guests. Herb led him to the market, where the bruised fruit cost little. Vee bought enough and gave up his grand plot. Herb carried the crate home so Vee could use it as a tea table.

title: The sidekick map
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Hero Heath, Sidekick Sid, all fictional monkeys
text: Heath charged into the cave while Sid checked the map. The monkey hero reached a wall and struck a bold pose. Sid found a side door that led to the stolen bananas. Heath tried to claim the rescue, but his cape was still caught on a nail inside. Sid freed him and shared the fruit. Heath gave Sid the map badge and asked him to lead the next mission while he carried bags.

title: The moon base broom
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Hero Haze, Cleaner Clio, all fictional monkeys
text: Haze built a secret base on the moon. Clio came to clean it and found dust in every crack. The monkey hero had no broom, only a ray gun. Clio taped dry leaves to the gun and swept the floor. Haze tried to fire it, but Clio took out the power cell first. They packed bananas in the clean kitchen. Haze made a chore chart and put his own name on the first shift.

title: The tiny ray rescue
target: Shrink rays solve the wrong problem
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Hero Hank, Mayor Miri, all fictional monkeys
text: Hank shrank a jammed cart to get it through the gate. The bananas inside became so small that the monkeys needed a lens to eat them. Mayor Miri asked him to undo the ray. Hank grew the cart back outside, then took off its wheels and carried it through on its side. Miri paid him with one full banana. Hank used the ray only on the empty gate key, which fit his pocket much better.

title: The shield soup lid
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Hero Hazel, Cook Cam, all fictional monkeys
text: Hazel blocked hail with her shiny shield. The monkey crowd stayed dry, but Cam could not find the lid for his soup pot. Hazel looked at the handle on her shield and saw his name on it. She gave it back before the soup boiled over. Cam lent her a broad tray for the next storm. Hazel served bananas from it when the sky cleared and kept it out of the dish rack.

title: The hero fan club queue
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Hero Hero, Fan Fenn, all fictional monkeys
text: Hero spent all day signing cards while Fenn waited at the end of the line. A monkey shouted that a branch blocked the road. Hero feared the fans would leave if he stepped away from his desk. Fenn took the pen and signed a card that said Back Soon. Hero moved the branch and brought bananas for the queue. Fenn got the first card when he came back, with a real leaf on it.

title: The frozen yogurt race
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Chef Frost, Judge Jade, all fictional monkeys
text: Frost made yogurt so cold that the spoon froze to his fur. Jade waited for a taste while the monkey hopped around the kitchen. He held his tail near a warm lamp until the spoon fell free. Jade asked for small cups that thawed faster. Frost filled them and added bananas at the last moment. The judges ate before the next freeze. Frost won a warm pair of gloves and used them to carry the cups.

title: The bread door wedge
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Baker Bram, Guest Greta, all fictional monkeys
text: Bram baked a loaf that rang like a bell when Greta knocked on it. The monkey baker said the crust proved his skill. Greta could not cut it even with a saw. Bram sliced a softer loaf and served it with bananas. They used the hard loaf to hold the door open while the kitchen cooled. Guests praised the fresh air. Bram put less heat in the oven and kept the bell loaf by the door.

title: The cheese cloud
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Chef Chase, Guest Gem, all fictional monkeys
text: Chase made a cheese cloud for Gem and served it in an empty bowl. The monkey guest sneezed and blew the cloud into the vent. Chase stared at his dish. Gem asked for cheese she could hold. He cut a slice, added bananas, and set it on a plate. She paid the full price. Chase kept the cloud machine for party fog and put a napkin over the vent before his next test.

title: The secret menu tail
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Chef Cher, Guest Gus, all fictional monkeys
text: Cher kept a secret menu behind the counter. Gus guessed every code he knew, but none worked. The monkey leaned on his tail and knocked the menu onto the floor. It listed plain beans and bananas at half price. Cher said the secret was meant for regular guests. Gus came back each week, paid for lunch, and washed his own bowl. Cher put the menu on the wall so new guests could join him.

title: The food critic fork
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Critic Cliff, Cook Cia, all fictional monkeys
text: Cliff gave Cia low marks because her fork was bent. The monkey cook bent it back, but the critic found a dent in the spoon. Cia set a bowl of bananas beside him without any metal tools. Cliff ate with his hands and forgot to grumble. He wrote that the meal had a fine rustic style. Cia framed the review next to the tool rack, where the bent fork held spare towels.

title: The marathon snack mile
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Runner Ria, Marshal Mars, all fictional monkeys
text: Ria stopped at every snack stand during the long race. By the final mile the monkey carried more bananas than she could eat. Mars asked her to put the fruit down so she could finish. Ria gave each tired runner one and kept only a peel bag. She crossed last with a light tail and a full smile. Mars gave her the spare medal for best cleanup, then helped her carry the peel bag home.

title: The ski lift scarf
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Skier Sky, Lift Liz, all fictional monkeys
text: Sky wore a scarf twice as long as her tail. It caught on the ski lift and pulled her monkey cap off. Liz stopped the lift before the knot grew tight. Sky cut the scarf into short pieces and wrapped each pole handle. Her hands stayed warm on the next run. Liz used the spare piece to line her lunch box. Both ate bananas at the bottom, with no loose wool near the gears.

title: The golf sand picnic
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Golfer Glen, Caddie Cora, all fictional monkeys
text: Glen hit his ball into the sand pit six times. Cora offered the monkey a shorter club, but he wanted to prove his power. His next swing dug a hole beside the ball. Cora spread a cloth over it and opened the bananas. Glen sat down at last. After lunch he used the short club and cleared the sand. Cora raked the pit smooth and kept the long club as a picnic pole.

title: The referee ribbon maze
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Ref Rex, Runner Rose, all fictional monkeys
text: Rex tied ribbons across the track to mark each rule. Rose could not see a clear way through. The monkey referee blew his whistle when her tail touched one ribbon, then tripped on another himself. Rose helped untie them and laid one ribbon along the outside edge. Rex kept the rules on a card in his pocket. The race began late, but all the bananas stayed on the prize table until it ended.

title: The team photo tail
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Captain Clem, Photo Phil, all fictional monkeys
text: Clem held the team still for a photo before the match. Phil could not fit every monkey tail in the frame. Clem curled his tail up, and all the others copied him. Now their heads hid behind the fur. Phil asked them to sit on the bench with legs to one side. He took one quick picture. The team reached the field in time and won. Clem kept the photo beside the bowl of victory bananas.

title: The rescue robot spoon
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Hero Hilda, Builder Bolt, all fictional monkeys
text: Bolt built Hilda a robot that could carry any spoon. Hilda wanted it to rescue a cart full of bananas. The machine brought her one spoon and sat down. The monkey hero tied the spoon to a rope, hooked the cart axle, and pulled. Bolt saw his robot needed a broader job list. He taught it to hold rope next. Hilda kept the spoon in her kit because it had already earned its place.

title: The x ray lunchbox
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Hero Hex, Guard Gage, all fictional monkeys
text: Hex used his x ray gaze to check a sealed box at the gate. He saw long curved shapes and cried that it held secret weapons. Gage opened the box to show bananas. The monkey hero blushed beneath his mask. Gage asked him to read the label before using his gift. Hex checked the next box and found towels. He carried both boxes to the hall and used plain sight to serve lunch.

title: The rocket boots brake
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Hero Harry, Mechanic Mox, all fictional monkeys
text: Harry wore rocket boots to reach fires fast. He flew past a smoky shed and landed in a pond. Mox pulled the monkey out by his tail. The boots had a start button but no brake. Mox added one and made Harry train on the grass. The next smoke came from a grill. Harry stopped beside it, brought water for the cook, and stayed to eat bananas while the boots cooled in the shade.

title: The villain trap mat
target: Elaborate traps fail on practical details
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Villain Voss, Hero Holly, all fictional monkeys
text: Voss built a pit under a rug to catch Holly. The monkey hero saw that the rug sagged over a hole when her tail brushed it and stepped around it. Voss leaned down to check the edge and fell in himself. Holly lowered a basket of bananas, then a ladder. Voss ate before he climbed out. They filled the pit with soil and planted a tree. Holly kept the rug for the shade beneath it.

title: The hero hotline hold
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Hero Hugh, Caller Calla, all fictional monkeys
text: Calla rang Hugh because her kite was stuck in a tree. A taped voice told the monkey to hold. Calla put the phone down and built a stool from her fruit crates. Hugh picked up just as she freed the kite. She asked him to help put the crates back instead. He arrived with bananas and did the heavy lifting. Hugh cut the hold message and kept a pencil by the phone to note each real job.

title: The bake sale rival
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Baker Bina, Baker Burt, all fictional monkeys
text: Bina and Burt held rival bake sales across the lane. Each monkey lowered prices until a cake cost less than a crumb. Then rain drove all their guests away. Bina had a tent but no dry chairs. Burt had chairs but no tent. They joined the stalls and sold warm buns with bananas. Both earned enough to pay for flour. They kept one shared price sign and took turns holding it when the wind rose.

title: The relay tail knot
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Runner Rai, Runner Rem, all fictional monkeys
text: Rai and Rem tied tails to prove their team bond. The monkeys could run in a line but not turn at the track bend. They fell into the soft grass beside the bananas. Rem untied the knot and handed Rai a short stick instead. Rai ran his leg, passed the stick, and cheered from the edge. Rem crossed the line without hauling a friend. They tied a knot in the prize ribbon and hung it over the stick.

title: The pizza square corners
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Chef Pru, Guest Gabe, all fictional monkeys
text: Pru made square pizzas, but Gabe said real pizza must be round. The monkey chef cut off the corners and put them on a tray. Gabe ate his circle, then asked for the corners too. Pru charged him for a whole square. He paid and laughed. She named the corner tray after him and served bananas beside it for dessert. Gabe came back with friends who each ordered a square and kept every crisp edge.

title: The ice rink broom
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Skater Sia, Keeper Kip, all fictional monkeys
text: Sia tried a grand spin on the rink and hit a leaf. Her monkey tail swung out and she sat down hard. Kip offered to sweep before her next turn. Sia took the broom and pushed it while she skated a simple circle. The rink cleared, and she found a steady rhythm. Her final spin worked. Kip gave her bananas, and the broom got a place beside her shiny cup in the display case.

title: The hero retirement box
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Hero Hale, Student Star, all fictional monkeys
text: Hale packed his hero mask for his rest. Star wanted it, but the box also held bills for every broken window Hale had left behind. The young monkey read them and took a broom instead. Star swept the glass from the last rescue while Hale paid for repairs. They ate bananas on the new porch. Hale gave Star the mask at sunset, and Star put a repair fund beside it before she planned her first patrol.

title: The moon lunch leak
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pilot Pax, Cook Cora, all fictional monkeys
text: Pax flew to the moon with a crate of bananas. Cora found a leak in the food bag and called the monkey pilot back to the cabin. He patched it with his mission badge, but now no one could read his name. Cora wrote it on his helmet in sauce. They landed safely and shared lunch beside the ship. Pax kept the stained helmet as proof that the cook had saved the trip.

title: The alien doorbell
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Scout Sia, Alien Avo, all fictional monkeys
text: Sia heard a ring outside her ship. Avo stood there with a plate of bananas and a long green hat. The monkey scout thought the hat was an alien weapon. Avo took it off and showed more fruit inside. He had come to trade hats for spoons. Sia gave him one spoon and took the hat. They rang the bell twice for friends, then sat on the ramp and ate.

title: The robot tail brush
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Builder Bo, Robot Rex, all fictional monkeys; Rex wears a metal robot suit
text: Bo told Rex to tidy the room. Rex, a monkey in a metal suit, brushed the tail of Bo into a stiff cone and stacked bananas on it. Bo asked why the floor was still dusty. Rex said the tail had been the closest loose object. Bo moved the fruit to a bowl and showed Rex the broom. Rex swept one tile at a time. Bo sat still until the room was clean, then washed his tail back into shape.

title: The time machine cake
target: Time travel to fix tiny regrets
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Timer Tess, Baker Ben, all fictional monkeys
text: Tess used her time machine to save a burnt cake. She went back one minute, then tripped over her own tail and missed the oven again. The monkey tried twice more and found three copies of herself in the kitchen. Ben gave each Tess a job. One watched the clock, one washed dishes, and one sliced bananas. The first Tess baked a fresh cake. They ate four slices before the machine drew them back into one.

title: The star map stain
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pilot Pia, Navigator Nix, all fictional monkeys
text: Nix spilled tea on the star map. Pia steered toward the brown spot and found no planet. The monkey pilot checked through the window and saw that home lay just below them. Nix wiped the map clean with his tail. The stain stayed, so he marked it Tea, Not Star. They landed at the proper port and bought bananas. Pia kept the marked map to remind them where a snack break should be.

title: The gravity switch snack
target: Science fiction switches solve daily chores
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Scientist Sol, Guest Gem, all fictional monkeys
text: Sol turned gravity down to clean beneath his desk. Gem came in with bananas, and the fruit floated to the roof. The monkey guests chased it with their tails but could not reach. Sol tied a spoon to a cord and hooked each bunch down. He turned gravity back up before serving lunch. Gem asked for a plain broom next time. Sol kept the cord, which also pulled dust from behind the shelf.

title: The comet pet race
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Keeper Kit, Comet Coco, all fictional monkeys
text: Kit kept Coco as a pet comet in a glass bowl. Coco was a monkey with a silver cape who ran in circles so fast the bowl shook. Kit asked him to stop for bananas. Coco stopped at once, and the bowl fell quiet. They moved the game outside to a wide field. Kit drew a slow orbit round the picnic cloth. Coco could race each lap and still sit down for a snack.

title: The invisible ship ticket
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pilot Pea, Guard Gil, all fictional monkeys
text: Pea hid her ship with a cloak beam to avoid the port fee. Gil, a monkey guard, heard her tail drag down the ramp. He put a ticket on the empty air. Pea could not find it until she turned the beam off. She paid the fee in bananas and asked for a visible parking post. Gil gave her one. Pea left the beam off at the port and found her ship without bruised toes.

title: The distant planet mud
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Scout Sky, Captain Cam, all fictional monkeys
text: Sky found a strange brown sea on a new planet. Cam said the monkey must bring a sample home. Sky dipped his tail in and got stuck. Cam pulled him free with a rope. The sea was deep mud, much like the patch behind their hut. They marked it on the map and took a jar anyway. Back home they grew bananas in it, which earned the planet a useful name, Garden.

title: The moon flag laundry
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Captain Cal, Crew Cia, all fictional monkeys
text: Cal planted his flag on the moon, but Cia noticed it was a wet towel. The monkey captain had grabbed it from the wash rack. Cal wanted to leave it as a grand symbol. Cia needed it to dry her fur. They took a photo, folded the towel, and drew a flag on a flat stone. At home they ate bananas beneath the photo, while the real towel dried on its proper line.

title: The spy peel code
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Agent Ace, Agent Ada, all fictional monkeys
text: Ace wrote a code on a banana peel. Ada ate the fruit, then tossed the peel into the bin. The monkey agents needed the code to open a safe. Ace fetched the peel with his tail and read it upside down. The safe opened to show six clean plates. Ada set the table while Ace copied the code onto paper. They ate more bananas and put every new peel into the compost box.

title: The hat bug
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Agent Ash, Clerk Clay, all fictional monkeys
text: Ash put a tiny sound bug in the hat of Clerk Clay. The monkey clerk lent his hat to a fruit seller, so Ash heard only prices all day. He went to fetch the bug and found it stuck to a bunch of bananas. Clay helped him take it off with a spoon. Ash paid for the damaged fruit. His report said the market had fresh stock, which was true and useful to the cook.

title: The spy door password
target: Secret agents forget their own codes
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Agent Elm, Guard Glen, all fictional monkeys
text: Elm reached the secret door but forgot the code. Glen offered a hint, saying it was a yellow fruit. The monkey tried lemon, then mango, then pear. His tail brushed a crate of bananas beside the wall. Glen pointed at it. Elm spoke the right word and entered. Inside, he changed the code to Tail so he would always have a hint with him. Glen moved the fruit crate into the kitchen.

title: The briefcase picnic
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Agent Fern, Agent Fay, all fictional monkeys
text: Fern left a case on the park bench for Fay. A gust blew it open, and bananas rolled across the path. The monkey agents crawled after them as if they had to inspect the paving stones. Fay caught the last fruit with her tail. They sat down and ate because the case had held only lunch. Fern put a latch on it before the next swap. Fay brought a cloth to cover the bench.

title: The fake moustache glue
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Agent Moss, Barber Bea, all fictional monkeys
text: Moss glued a false lip patch over his monkey nose. It hid his face so well that Bea would not let him into her shop. He tried to state his secret name, but the glue sealed his mouth. Bea handed him warm water through the window. Moss melted the glue and peeled the hair away. Bea trimmed his real fur and fed him bananas. Moss used a loose hat for his next guise instead.

title: The spy clock fast
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Agent Reed, Watchmaker Wren, all fictional monkeys
text: Reed raced to the tower before noon to stop a secret trade. The monkey arrived early and found no one but Wren mending clocks. His watch was an hour fast. Wren fixed it while Reed shared his bananas. At noon a cart came to swap old clocks for new ones. Reed checked its permit and let it pass. He sent a report about the false alarm, with the correct time on every page.

title: The decoder drum
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Agent Rue, Musician Min, all fictional monkeys
text: Rue heard taps through the wall and thought a spy sent a code. The monkey wrote each beat down, then fed the marks into his decoder. It said Bring Bananas. Min opened the next door with a drum under her arm. She was playing a new tune. Rue brought fruit anyway and asked her to play it again. His decoder made a fine beat clock once he stopped asking it to read secret notes.

title: The stealth squeak
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Agent Vale, Mechanic May, all fictional monkeys
text: Vale wore silent shoes for a night mission. His monkey tail creaked against the shiny floor instead. May heard him from the shop and handed him a cloth. Vale wrapped his tail, crossed the hall, and found the lost key beside the sink. May had left it there while washing bananas. Vale gave it back, then removed his shoes. His bare feet were quiet enough, and the cloth became his regular tail towel.

title: The spy boat oar
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Agent Birch, Pilot Plum, all fictional monkeys
text: Birch leaped into a boat to chase a secret courier. Plum pushed off, then found the oars missing. The monkeys used flat boxes from their lunch as paddles. They reached the other boat at the dock. The courier had brought their oars back from the repair shop. Birch took them and paid with bananas. Plum kept the boxes as spare paddles, after washing all the soft fruit out of their corners.

title: The secret tunnel sign
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Agent Alder, Guest Gus, all fictional monkeys
text: Alder made a hidden tunnel to his spy hut. Gus could not find it and spent an hour going round the grove. The monkey agent wanted to keep the route secret, but his lunch guest had all the bananas. Alder hung a small sign that said Roots with an arrow toward the hatch. Gus read it and knocked. After lunch they changed the sign to a plain leaf mark that both could read from the path.

title: The missing pie rim
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Detective Dex, Baker Bina, all fictional monkeys
text: Dex looked for a stolen pie. Bina showed him a pie dish with just a ring of crust left. The monkey found crumbs on his own tail. He had sat on the sill deep in thought and eaten the pie there. Dex paid Bina in bananas, then helped bake a new one. He closed the case with a plain note about his snack. Bina served him lunch before she hired him for another search.

title: The muddy paw clue
target: Mystery clues identify the wrong suspect
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Detective Dot, Gardener Gale, all fictional monkeys
text: Dot found muddy prints by the empty banana shelf. She accused Gale, whose monkey feet were always dirty. Gale showed her a fresh broom he had used to clean the shed. Dot swept the floor and found a loose wheel track under the prints. The fruit cart had rolled away through the open gate. They fetched it as a team. Dot washed her own muddy feet before writing the report and sharing the bananas.

title: The locked room window
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Detective Dan, Host Hope, all fictional monkeys
text: Hope locked a room with bananas inside. When she opened it, the fruit was gone. Dan checked the lock, then the ceiling, then his monkey hat. Hope asked why he had not checked the open window. Dan climbed out and found the fruit on a ledge where wind had blown it. He brought it back dry in his hat. Hope shut the window and put a small latch on it before dinner.

title: The vanishing ink list
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Detective Dawn, Cook Chet, all fictional monkeys
text: Dawn saw blank pages where Chet had written the meal list. The monkey sleuth blamed secret ink. She warmed a page over the stove, but no words came back. Chet showed her the sponge he had used to wipe sauce off the book. He had wiped the pencil too. Dawn wrote a fresh list on a board. Chet hung it above the sink, and they ate the bananas the old list had omitted.

title: The clue under the hat
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Detective Dale, Assistant Ari, all fictional monkeys
text: Dale found a key beside the empty fruit box. He hid it in his hat, then checked the room for hours. Ari asked the monkey to take a break and brush his fur. The key fell onto the desk. It opened the box in the next room, where all the bananas sat safe from ants. Dale thanked Ari and made a tray for clues. His hat held only his head on the next case.

title: The bell tower whisper
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Della, Keeper Kian, all fictional monkeys
text: Della heard low voices in the bell tower and went up to face a ghost. Kian, a monkey keeper, stood below with a basket of bananas. Della found a pipe that carried his voice to the top. He had asked if she wanted lunch. She spoke into the pipe and asked for two bananas. Kian sent them up in a bucket. Della labeled the pipe Lunch Call and left the ghosts out of her report.

title: The jewel ice cube
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Dune, Host Hana, all fictional monkeys
text: Hana lost a blue gem at the feast. Dune checked every monkey pocket and found only crumbs. His own drink had a blue ice cube. He let it melt in a dish, and the gem fell out. Hana had dropped it while filling the ice tray. Dune gave it back and drank plain water. Hana served bananas in dry bowls so no one had to wait for dessert to thaw.

title: The map false fold
target: Treasure maps misread by eager hunters
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Demi, Guide Gil, all fictional monkeys
text: Demi dug beneath an old tree where the map showed a cross. Gil saw that the map had folded over on itself. The monkey hunters opened it flat and found the cross marked a tool shed. Inside lay a note that told them to dig by the river. They found a chest of bananas there, left by the camp cook. Demi ate one and put the map in a stiff frame for the walk home.

title: The missing shadow
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Dora, Lamp Lyle, all fictional monkeys
text: Dora woke with no shadow and feared a spell. Lyle checked the monkey room and found lamps on every wall. Their light hid the dark patch behind her feet. He turned all but one lamp off. Dora saw her shadow stretch across the floor. She fed Lyle bananas for his help, then asked him to move the lamps into the garden. Her night party had bright paths, and each guest kept a shadow.

title: The blue fur case
target: Detectives infer crime from odd color
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Davy, Painter Paz, all fictional monkeys
text: Davy saw blue fur on Paz and asked who had hurt him. The monkey painter showed him a mural of the sea. He had leaned into the wet paint as he reached for bananas. Davy fetched soap and helped wash his tail. The blue faded, but one patch stayed on his ear. Paz kept it until the mural dried. Davy wrote the case up as Paint Spill and used the spare soap to clean his desk.

title: The alien lunch stars
target: Space gift exchanges with ordinary rules
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pilot Pine, Trader Tia, all fictional monkeys
text: Tia gave Pine a sealed alien cube. The monkey pilot opened it and found six bananas, each wrapped in foil. He thought the foil was a rare space metal. Tia said it was just there to keep lunch fresh. Pine folded it into stars and hung them in his cabin. He sent Tia a thank you note and gave the empty cube back. She filled it again, this time with a spoon beside the fruit.

title: The starship tail seat
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pilot Pearl, Builder Beck, all fictional monkeys
text: Beck made a ship seat with no tail hole. Pearl sat in it and could not reach the buttons. The monkey builder cut a slot, but loose foam clogged the air vent. Pearl held a bag under the seat while Beck brushed the foam out. They tested each switch before takeoff. The ship flew well, and Pearl ate bananas in comfort. Beck added tail slots to every seat on his plan that evening.

title: The clone chore chart
target: Clones multiply trouble instead of labor
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Scientist Suri, Clone Sal, all fictional monkeys
text: Suri made a clone to do her chores. Sal was another monkey who also wanted a clone to do his chores. Suri stopped the machine before it made a third. They split the list, with Suri washing dishes and Sal on broom duty. The work ended sooner than they had hoped. They ate bananas on the clean floor. Suri changed the machine label to Friend Maker and kept the switch off unless a guest truly wished to stay.

title: The planet name vote
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Captain Cove, Scout Seren, all fictional monkeys
text: Cove named the new planet after himself. Seren said no because she had found it first. The monkeys argued until their fuel gauge flashed. They landed and saw trees full of bananas beside a clear pond. Cove wrote Snack on the map while Seren filled the fuel tank at a pump by the pond. She liked the name. They left a small flag with the pond marked on it, then flew home with fruit and enough fuel for a calm trip.

title: The space suit sneeze
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Pilot Petal, Medic Mica, all fictional monkeys
text: Petal sneezed inside her space suit and could not wipe her nose. Mica told the monkey to come into the air lock before taking her helmet off. Petal waited through the slow cycle, then found a feather stuck to her fur. Mica removed it and cleaned the glass. Petal kept bananas outside the suit for lunch. Her next walk went well, with no feather and a clear view of each moon rock.

title: The spy pen jam
target: Gadget pens cannot do ordinary work
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Agent Aura, Clerk Creek, all fictional monkeys
text: Aura used a pen that could shoot rope, flash light, and play songs. Creek asked her to sign for a parcel of bananas. The monkey pressed the wrong switch and tied the parcel to the desk. Creek lent her a plain pencil. Aura signed, cut the rope, and put the pen back in its case. She used the parcel string to tie a pencil onto the case so it would always be close.

title: The secret handshake ache
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Agent Dawn, Agent Dell, all fictional monkeys
text: Dawn and Dell devised a secret hand grip with twelve turns and a tail twirl. The monkeys forgot the last twist and tied their tails in a knot. Dawn reached for bananas with one free hand while Dell read the rules. They undid the knot by turning the other way. Their new hello was one plain nod. Dell burned the old rules in the stove and used the warm pan to cook a snack before they left for work.

title: The spy pigeon basket
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Agent Dove, Keeper Dovea, all fictional monkeys
text: Dove sent a message by pigeon, but the bird landed at the fruit stall. Dovea found it pecking bananas beside the monkey agent. Dove saw he had used a page covered in fruit stains. He wrote a clean copy and tucked it into a dry tube. Dovea sent the bird again. It reached the right hut before dusk. Dove washed his desk and ate the ripe fruit far from his paper stack.

title: The night vision lamp
target: Advanced spy gear defeated by simple light
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Agent Dusk, Guard Gray, all fictional monkeys
text: Dusk wore night goggles to enter a dark hall. Gray turned a lamp on, and the monkey agent saw only glare. Dusk took the goggles off and found Gray holding his lost bag of bananas. There was no secret vault, just the coat room. Dusk thanked him and checked the room number on his note. He went to the next door with plain eyes and left the goggles in their padded case.

title: The spy magnet spoon
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Agent Frost, Cook Flora, all fictional monkeys
text: Frost turned on a pocket magnet to catch a stolen key. Every spoon in the kitchen flew toward his monkey coat. Flora asked him to turn it off before her soup got cold. Frost caught the spoons in a bowl as they fell. The key landed among them. He opened the pantry and brought out bananas for dessert. Flora let him keep one wooden spoon, which did not move when he tested the magnet again.

title: The silver trail snail
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Drake, Gardener Greta, all fictional monkeys
text: Drake saw a silver trail near the locked fruit shed. The monkey thought a thief had dragged a chain there. Greta lent him a lens, and he traced the trail to a snail. It had crossed a wet leaf in the moon glow. Drake opened the shed with Greta and found the bananas safe. He moved the snail to a damp patch beside the fence. Greta gave him the lens to check small facts first.

title: The ringing empty box
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Flint, Clerk Cora, all fictional monkeys
text: A box rang on the counter though no one had put a bell inside. Flint held it to his ear and shook it while Cora watched. The monkey finally opened the bottom flap. A small clock had slipped between the layers of card. Cora stopped its alarm and found the shop receipt tucked beside it. Flint packed the bananas in a new box. Cora took the clock home, where it woke her in time to open the shop.

title: The twin hat clue
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Flynn, Twins Finn and Fawn, all fictional monkeys
text: Flynn accused Finn of taking the red hat. Fawn wore it at the other end of the room. The monkey twins had traded seats while Flynn checked his notes. Flynn asked each to stand by a window and stay there. Finn showed a blue hat in his bag. Fawn gave the red one back to its hook. They shared bananas and labeled their bags, so Flynn could count objects and see who had moved.

title: The clue tree fruit
target: Mystery clues are mistaken for snacks
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Grove, Scout Greer, all fictional monkeys
text: Grove hung red tags on limbs to mark a trail. Greer thought the tags meant ripe bananas and picked every bunch along it. He took the tags off as he went. The monkey sleuth came back to find no markers but a full basket. Greer showed him each branch he had climbed. Grove drew the route on paper while they walked. They found the lost camp tent beside the stream and ate the fruit there, with the map tucked safely under a stone.

title: The attic footstep drum
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Hark, Musician Harp, all fictional monkeys
text: Hark heard heavy steps in the attic each night. He climbed up with a lamp, his monkey tail stiff with fear. Harp sat there beating a drum with her feet while she ate bananas. She played after dark because the attic was cool. Hark moved a chair and rug up to soften the sound. Harp played him a quiet tune. The house stayed calm. Hark slept till dawn with his lamp off.

title: The moon rover picnic brake
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Driver Halo, Builder Iris, all fictional monkeys
text: Halo parked the moon rover beside a hill for lunch. It rolled down while the monkey peeled bananas. Iris chased it with a rope and tied it to a rock. Halo found the parking brake loose under his seat. They fixed the bolt, then tested it on a small slope. The rover stayed still. Halo put the rope in the tool box and ate his lunch on flat ground before the next drive.

title: The portal curtain
target: Dimensional doors mistaken for ordinary doors
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Mage Orbit, Guest Opal, all fictional monkeys
text: Orbit built a portal behind his kitchen curtain. Opal stepped through to fetch bananas and landed in the tool shed. The monkey mage had linked the wrong doors. Opal came back with a rake and asked where lunch was. Orbit moved the link to the pantry, then hung a clear sign on the curtain. They ate side by side in the kitchen. The rake stayed by the back door, which led to the garden without magic.

title: The spy bubble trail
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Agent Mist, Guard Maple, all fictional monkeys
text: Mist wore soap shoes to slide quietly across the hall. Each step left bubbles behind the monkey spy. Maple traced the trail and found him under a desk, peeling bananas. Mist said he was testing a stealth route. Maple gave him a mop and helped dry the floor. They were done before anyone slipped. Mist swapped the soap with soft felt and tested one quiet step at a time, while Maple looked for new trails.

title: The vanished picnic blanket
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Lake, Host Lila, all fictional monkeys
text: Lila set bananas on a blanket and went for cups. The blanket was gone before she came back. Lake checked the monkey yard and saw a square patch of shade under a tree. The wind had lifted the blanket into its limbs. Lake climbed up while Lila held a basket below. The fruit fell safely into it. They tied stones to each corner of the blanket and ate their picnic beneath the same tree.

title: The case of the extra tail
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Laurel, Actor Alder, all fictional monkeys
text: Alder walked into the hall with two tails. Laurel feared a strange spell. The monkey actor showed her one tail, then the other, both moving in time. She asked him to turn round. A string led from the false tail to his wrist. Alder was testing a costume for a two headed beast. Laurel helped hide the string under his fur. They ate bananas after the test, and the spare tail became a curtain tie.

title: The meeting to end meetings
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Manager Mabel, Clerk Cole, all fictional monkeys
text: Mabel called a meeting to cut talks. Cole brought a clock and a bag of bananas. Every monkey got one minute to speak, but Mabel used hers to list the agenda. Cole turned the clock round so she could see it. Mabel stopped before the bell. They cut the next meeting and used its hour to fix the loose shelf. Cole put the clock there, with enough space beside it for lunch.

title: The desk hot spot
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Manager Mina, Worker Wade, all fictional monkeys
text: Mina chose hot desks by daily vote. Wade got the desk beside the stove and singed his monkey fur. Mina said hot meant shared, but Wade asked for a cooler spot. They rolled the desk to the window and marked seats with clips instead of heat. Wade hung bananas from his clip during lunch. Mina banned food on desks, then took one because she had not brought a snack of her own.

title: The inbox nest
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Clerk Corin, Boss Brin, all fictional monkeys
text: Corin printed every unread note and built a nest beneath his desk. Brin wanted the monkey to answer them all. Corin sorted the pages by date and found most asked about a feast held last year. He filed those in a box and handled the three new queries. Brin gave him bananas for lunch. Corin used the empty nest as a foot rest, and Brin stopped sending each note to every desk.

title: The growth chart roof
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Founder Faye, Analyst Ash, all fictional monkeys
text: Faye showed a chart where sales rose through the roof. Ash checked the scale and found it counted peels instead of bananas. The monkey founder had called every peel a new client. Ash weighed the actual fruit and drew a smaller chart. Faye first frowned, then saw that the stock would last a week. They sold the peels as compost and counted that money once. The new chart fit neatly on one page.

title: The mission plaque door
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Boss Basil, Clerk Clio, all fictional monkeys
text: Basil hung a huge mission plaque over the door. Clio could not carry boxes of bananas through without tilting her monkey head. Basil said the words would inspire the team. Clio asked him to read them from the hall. He could see only the frame. They moved the plaque to a side wall and cleared the door. Clio got the boxes in before noon. Basil wrote Keep Door Clear on a smaller card by the hinge.

title: The pitch deck banana
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Founder Finn, Investor Ivo, all fictional monkeys
text: Finn made fifty slides for his fruit service pitch. Ivo asked what the service did. The monkey founder flipped through charts until his lamp rig failed. Finn took one banana out of his bag and peeled it for Ivo. That was the whole service. Ivo paid for lunch and asked what it cost to run. Finn wrote the costs on one sheet of paper. He sold the lamp rig and bought better fruit, leaving the slide deck in its box.

title: The office quiet jar
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Boss Bea, Clerk Creek, all fictional monkeys
text: Bea charged a coin when someone made noise. Creek dropped a mug and owed three coins for the crash. The monkey asked how to report a fire under the quiet rule. Bea opened her mouth, then shut it. Creek put a bell beside the jar and offered one free ring for urgent news. Bea agreed and gave back the coins. They filled the jar with bananas instead, though each peel made a small rustle at lunch.

title: The team spirit costume
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Boss Bram, Worker Wil, all fictional monkeys
text: Bram gave each worker a bright team cape. Wil wore his over his monkey fur, but the cape dragged through glue at the packing bench. Every box stuck to him. Bram tried to help and stuck his own cape there too. Wil cut both capes free and used the cloth as packing pads. The boxes shipped safely. Bram ordered plain aprons next time and gave each worker bananas instead of another speech about team spirit.

title: The memo margin war
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Writer Wren, Editor Eve, all fictional monkeys
text: Wren wrote a memo about a broken tap. Eve changed its margins six times. The monkey writer watched water drip onto a crate of bananas while the page passed back and forth. Wren took a wrench to the tap and stopped the leak. Eve cleared the seventh margin just as he was done. Wren sent a one line note that said Fixed. Eve kept it on her desk because no one needed to edit its shape.

title: The break room spoon vote
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Clerk Cedar, Boss Brook, all fictional monkeys
text: Cedar asked for a spoon in the break room. Brook formed a panel to choose its shape. The monkeys met for weeks while their soup grew cold. Cedar carved a spoon from a fallen branch and ate lunch. Brook asked if it met the new policy. Cedar handed him a bowl of bananas and the spoon. Brook used it without reading the policy. The panel closed, and the branch gave them three more spoons for the drawer.

title: The startup pivot bench
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Founder Fern, Builder Bly, all fictional monkeys
text: Fern planned an app to find seats. Bly built a bench for the demo. The monkey founder changed the plan to a snack app, so Bly put bananas on the bench. Fern changed again to a fitness app. Bly asked guests to walk to the bench for lunch. They paid for the food and sat down happily. Fern kept the bench service and dropped the app. Bly wrote the price on one plank in large clear letters.

title: The infinite free trial
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Founder Frost, User Uma, all fictional monkeys
text: Frost offered a free trial of his banana club. Uma signed up each week with a new hat and got more fruit. The monkey founder ran out of stock before anyone paid. Frost asked her to show her tail instead of her hat. Uma said it was the same tail every time. She paid for one month and helped sort the signups. Frost kept the free sample to one banana, which was still enough to taste.

title: The funding jar echo
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Founder Gale, Investor Ike, all fictional monkeys
text: Gale brought an empty jar to Ike and called it a new fruit hub. Ike tapped it and liked the echo. The monkey founder asked for cash to make more empty jars. Ike instead put bananas inside and asked Gale to sell them. Gale sold every jar at the market that day. He brought the bills back without a fancy name. Ike funded the next crop, and Gale used the echo jar to store small coins.

title: The beta bug picnic
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Coder Glen, User Ula, all fictional monkeys
text: Glen built a lunch app that sent bananas to the wrong desk. Ula got six orders while the other monkeys got none. Glen called it a beta bug. Ula wrote desk names on six cards and handed them to the cook. Lunch reached the right seats. Glen copied that simple list into the app and tested each name once. Ula passed the spare orders along and ate her own share, and Glen stopped using beta as an answer.

title: The office cloud shelf
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Boss Hazel, Clerk Clover, all fictional monkeys
text: Hazel told Clover to put all files in the cloud. The monkey clerk carried the boxes to a high shelf where steam from the kettle rose. Paper curled in the damp air. Hazel meant an online store, but had given no login. Clover moved the boxes to a dry cabinet and asked for the account. Hazel wrote it down but kept the code safe. They sorted files side by side over bananas, then moved only the needed pages online.

title: The permit for a chair
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Inspector Iris, Clerk Rowan, all fictional monkeys
text: Rowan bought a chair but could not sit until Iris cleared it. Iris tested the legs with her monkey hands, then asked for a diagram of the tail hole. Rowan stood to draw it. Iris sat to review it and found the seat quite safe. Rowan asked if that counted as a test. Iris stamped the form and stood up. Rowan finally sat, ate bananas, and used the cleared diagram to make a cushion that fit the hole.

title: The stamp pad drought
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Clerk Juniper, Clerk Lark, all fictional monkeys
text: Juniper could not issue fruit permits because the stamp pad was dry. Lark asked the monkey to sign each form instead. Juniper said names lacked the right shape. Lark drew a small square around each signed name. The permits went out and the bananas reached the market before noon. Juniper ordered fresh ink that day. When it came, she used the stamp only on final forms and kept her pen beside it for dry days.

title: The queue number zero
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Clerk Kestrel, Guest Moss, all fictional monkeys
text: Kestrel gave Moss ticket Zero and called One through Ten. The monkey guest sat all morning with bananas getting soft in his bag. Moss asked when Zero would come. Kestrel checked the board and found it started at One. She served him next, then printed a new first ticket. Moss shared his soft fruit with the waiting guests. Kestrel put Zero in a frame to show that a neat count must still include the first person.

title: The lost form folder
target: Forms require proof of missing forms
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Clerk Laurel, Guest Flint, all fictional monkeys
text: Flint lost the form needed to request a new form. Laurel asked for the old form as proof. The monkey guest showed his empty folder. Laurel stared at it until Flint offered her bananas from his other bag. She ate one and thought again. Laurel wrote Lost on a fresh sheet and let Flint sign it. He got the form he needed. She kept the empty folder as a place to put rules that needed review.

title: The window height rule
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Inspector Maple, Clerk Oak, all fictional monkeys
text: Maple ordered the service window raised to keep tails off the counter. Oak, a short monkey clerk, could no longer see guests. He stacked boxes of bananas to reach it. Maple saw the boxes wobble and asked him to stop. Oak moved the window lower and added a rail for tails instead. Maple tested it with her own tail and signed the change. The fruit went back into storage, and Oak served guests from the floor.

title: The badge gate loop
target: Access controls lock out their owners
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Guard Pine, Worker Elm, all fictional monkeys
text: Elm left his badge on his desk behind the locked gate. Pine asked the monkey worker to show it before entry. Elm pointed through the bars, where the badge lay in plain sight. Pine could see it but could not reach. Elm hooked it with his tail through the rail and held it up. Pine opened the gate. They put a spare badge locker outside and shared bananas while they fitted a simple lock.

title: The policy bookshelf tilt
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Boss Rose, Clerk Reed, all fictional monkeys
text: Rose printed each policy and stacked the binders on one shelf. Reed heard the wood crack above his monkey desk. He moved the bananas and files out of the way just before it fell. Rose wanted a rule about shelf weight. Reed asked her to remove old rules first. They kept three slim binders and sent the rest to the paper mill. Reed built a sturdy shelf and left half of it empty, where the fruit could sit safely.

title: The lunch receipt ruler
target: Expense audits obsess over tiny sums
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Auditor Sage, Clerk Sol, all fictional monkeys
text: Sage checked the lunch receipt with a ruler. Sol had spent one coin extra on bananas. The monkey auditor asked for a note on the extra cost. Sol showed her the large fruit and the smaller one on sale. Sage weighed both and found the larger was cheaper per bite. She cleared the receipt after an hour. Sol offered her half his lunch, and Sage said she would weigh costs before paper next time.

title: The suggestion box lock
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Boss Thistle, Worker Thyme, all fictional monkeys
text: Thistle locked the idea box so no one could steal ideas. Thyme had a note but no key to the slot cover. The monkey worker slid it under the box instead. Thistle found it while dusting and read the request for an open slot. He removed the cover and posted his answer beside it. Thyme put bananas on the shelf as thanks. Thistle ate one and left the box open for the next small useful note.

title: The quarterly tail review
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Boss Willow, Worker Wisp, all fictional monkeys
text: Willow rated Wisp by how often his tail moved at work. The monkey clerk could file pages without moving it at all. Willow gave him low marks despite the empty inbox. Wisp tied a ribbon to a fan so it waved beside his chair. Willow praised his energy, then noticed the trick. They counted the neat stacks instead. Wisp got his fair score and a bowl of bananas, while the ribbon waved over the fan.

title: The remote office branch
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Manager Amber, Worker Arbor, all fictional monkeys
text: Amber sent Arbor a desk for remote work. The monkey lived in a tree, where the flat desk could not fit between the limbs. Arbor hung its drawers from ropes and used one as a lap tray. Amber saw him work well on a video call. She asked where the desk top had gone. Arbor aimed the camera below. It was a roof over the mail box, keeping every letter dry.

title: The mute button tail
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Manager Briar, Clerk Bri, all fictional monkeys
text: Briar asked Bri to give a report on the call. The monkey spoke for ten minutes with her mic off. Each peer waved a tail at the screen, but Bri thought they liked her speech. Briar held up a card that said No Sound. Bri turned the mic on and gave one clear line with the sales total. The call ended early. Briar kept the card on his desk beside the mute switch.

title: The password fruit bowl
target: Security rules that users cannot follow
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Clerk Birch, Guard Beryl, all fictional monkeys
text: Beryl made Birch choose a new code each morning. The monkey wrote them on banana peels because he had no spare paper. At lunch he forgot which peel had the current code and could not open his desk. Beryl helped him sort them by color. They chose one strong code and put it in a safe record book. Birch threw the peels into compost and stopped storing office keys beside his lunch.

title: The onboarding tail maze
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Boss Cedar, Newcomer Nettle, all fictional monkeys
text: Cedar gave Nettle a stack of guides on her first day. The monkey could not see the door over the pages. She set the stack down and asked where to put her coat. Cedar found the coat hooks hidden behind a poster about welcome habits. He moved it, then led her through the office with one short map. Nettle filed the guides and took her first real task, sorting mail that had waited all morning.

title: The morale plant
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Boss Cori, Clerk Cypress, all fictional monkeys
text: Cori gave Cypress a plant to boost morale. The monkey clerk had asked for a new lamp, since his desk sat in the dark. The plant drooped there too. Cypress moved it to the bright window and took the window desk as well. Cori noticed that both looked better. He bought a lamp for the old desk and kept the plant by the sun. Cypress named it Request and watered it at lunch each day.

title: The startup bell schedule
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Founder Dahlia, Coder Dax, all fictional monkeys
text: Dahlia put in a bell that rang when Dax should change tasks. It rang while the monkey fixed a line of code, so he lost his place. Dax cut power to it and fixed the fault. Dahlia said the tracker showed no work done. Dax opened the working app on her screen. She tried it and rang the bell by hand in praise. They kept it for jobs done and let the clock handle lunch.

title: The office trophy cupboard
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Boss Dove, Clerk Dune, all fictional monkeys
text: Dove gave Dune a trophy each month for tidy work. Soon the awards filled the shelf where the monkey kept his tools. Dune put the awards in a cabinet and asked for no more. Dove said praise should be visible. Dune showed him the clean desk and the files in order. Dove gave him a day off instead. Dune cleaned one small cup before leaving and used it to hold his best pens.

title: The jargon glossary jam
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Boss Ewan, Clerk Ember, all fictional monkeys
text: Ewan asked Ember to align the fruit task flow. The monkey clerk asked if he meant sort the bananas. Ewan said the task was part of a grander plan. Ember put ripe fruit in one bin and green fruit in another. Sales stopped wasting soft stock. Ewan praised the new bins. Ember wrote Sort Fruit beside the phrase in his word book. The next clerk read that line and got to work without needing a long meeting.

title: The calendar chair block
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Manager Flora, Clerk Finch, all fictional monkeys
text: Flora booked every chair in the planner so her team would have space. Finch arrived alone and found the monkey hall empty but fully booked. He sat on the floor to mend a file box. Flora came in and tripped over his tail. Finch showed her the unused chairs. She cleared all but the two needed for a call. Finch sat at last, and the file box stayed safely beneath the desk.

title: The fire drill form
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Officer Fern, Clerk Fox, all fictional monkeys
text: Fern told Fox to fill a drill form before leaving the hall. The monkey clerk smelled smoke from the toaster and took the troop outside first. Fern carried the blank forms after him. They counted all staff by the gate, then called the kitchen crew. A burnt bun was the only loss. Fox filled the form in the yard. Fern moved the pen box outside so the next safe exit could stay clear.

title: The budget banana peel
target: Budget cuts cost more than they save
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Boss Grove, Clerk Gilda, all fictional monkeys
text: Grove cut the bin budget to save coins. Gilda stacked banana peels in a corner because the monkey office had no bins left. Grove slipped on one and broke a desk leg. Gilda paid for a cheap bin from the spare coin jar and swept the floor. Grove added the desk repair to his savings chart. The total fell below zero. He renewed the bin budget and thanked Gilda for the clean walk to his chair.

title: The email reply chain
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Clerk Holly, Boss Heath, all fictional monkeys
text: Heath emailed one query to the troop. Holly replied, then every monkey replied to thank her. The inbox filled while the work waited. Holly sent a last note that asked for no more thanks. It caused another dozen replies. Heath walked to each desk and asked them to stop. He wrote the answer on the wall for anyone who needed it. Holly shut her mail app and did the job before the kettle boiled.

title: The elevator pitch stairs
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Founder Iris, Buyer Ivy, all fictional monkeys
text: Iris tried out her lift pitch all week. Ivy worked above in a hall with no lift. The monkey founder climbed six flights and arrived too winded to give the speech. Ivy handed her water and asked what she sold. Iris said Light Bags. Ivy bought one to carry bananas down the stairs. Iris used the money to make more bags and put the speech away until she could say it in one breath.

title: The server room fern
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Boss Jade, Tech Jun, all fictional monkeys
text: Jade filled the server room with ferns to make it calm. Jun saw water drip onto a cable while he checked the fans. The monkey tech moved the pots outside and dried the floor. Jade asked why the room looked bare again. Jun showed her the hot air path each fern had blocked. They made a garden by the break room instead. Jade watered it there, and Jun could hear the servers humming without a drip.

title: The office smell survey
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Boss Kelp, Cleaner Kit, all fictional monkeys
text: Kelp sent a survey about a bad smell near the desks. Kit, the monkey cleaner, found a rotten banana beneath the fridge. He removed it before anyone filled the survey out. Kelp still wanted data, so Kit wrote One Old Fruit on the form. The next survey asked if the room smelled better. Kit opened a window and went home. Kelp cut the third survey and added a weekly sweep under the fridge instead.

title: The printer jam chart
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Boss Linden, Clerk Lilac, all fictional monkeys
text: Linden drew a chart to explain why the printer jammed. Lilac opened its tray and found a twig inside. The monkey clerk pulled it out with her tail and printed the chart. Linden studied the page, which blamed low morale. Lilac taped the twig over those words. He laughed and rewrote the cause as Wood In Tray. They posted the new chart beside the machine and kept all plant pots on a second shelf.

title: The bonus fruit scale
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Boss Marsh, Clerk Mari, all fictional monkeys
text: Marsh paid bonuses by fruit weight. Mari got a bunch of green bananas, while senior staff got soft ripe ones. The monkey weighed her share and found it heavier but too hard to eat. She brought a ripe bunch to compare. Marsh tested a slice of each and saw the problem. He let workers choose when to collect their fruit. Mari waited three days and got a ripe bunch at the same fair weight.

title: The lunch room rebrand
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Boss Myrtle, Cook Moss, all fictional monkeys
text: Myrtle renamed the lunch room the Fuel Hub. Moss asked for a new stove because the old one would not heat soup. The monkey boss ordered a shiny sign instead. Moss served cold soup beneath it. Myrtle took one taste and called the repair crew. They fixed the stove that day. Moss hung a small card under the sign that said Hot Lunch At Noon. All staff used that name, since it told them when to come.

title: The time sheet tail
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Boss Nova, Clerk Night, all fictional monkeys
text: Nova made Night record every minute on a time sheet. The monkey spent half an hour noting how long the notes took. Nova asked why filing had slowed. Night showed her the loop of entries about entries. They set one box for the full filing task and one for lunch. Night filled both after work and went home on time. Nova could read the simple sheet in just one minute.

title: The vacant office tour
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Founder Orchid, Guest Olive, all fictional monkeys
text: Orchid showed Olive a vast office for his new fruit firm. Only one monkey worked there, peeling bananas in a corner. Olive asked how rent got paid. Orchid said future growth would cover it. Olive moved the table into a small stall outside and watched the first guests buy fruit. Orchid ended the office lease when it expired. His grand tour now took two steps, leaving more time to peel and sell the actual stock.

title: The policy rain test
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Clerk Pebble, Inspector Poppy, all fictional monkeys
text: Poppy told Pebble to post all permits outside. Rain soaked them until the ink ran. The monkey clerk could no longer prove the fruit stall was legal. Poppy came back to issue a fine, but her own note got wet. Pebble lent her a clear sleeve and put one on each permit. Poppy voided the fine and added Dry Cover to the rule. The bananas stayed under the awning while every form stayed clear beside them.

title: The stamp color feud
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Clerk Quill, Clerk Quartz, all fictional monkeys
text: Quill used a red stamp, but Quartz would accept only blue ones. The monkey clerks sent a fruit permit back and forth until the page turned purple. The cart waited outside with bananas going soft. Quill signed a fresh page and Quartz signed it too. The cart left. They put both stamps in a drawer and used plain names from then on. The purple page became a desk mat to show how much ink their silly feud could waste.

title: The desk plant promotion
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Boss River, Clerk Rain, all fictional monkeys
text: River praised Rain for the tallest plant in the office. Rain wanted credit for her work, but the monkey boss watched only the leaves. She moved the plant to his desk and left a file summary on hers. River watered the plant all week and found it quite hard. He read the summary at last and gave Rain the lead role. She took the files to the next floor and left him clear notes about water.

title: The training video pause
target: Mandatory training cannot account for reality
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Trainer Sable, Clerk Snow, all fictional monkeys
text: Sable played a safety film about lifting fruit boxes. Snow saw a real box lean off the shelf behind him. The monkey clerk paused the film and caught it. Sable scolded her for missing the safety lesson, then noticed the box over his head. He helped her lower it. They used that box for the next live lesson and put the film away. Snow taught the proper grip with her tail clear of the floor.

title: The annual report doorstop
target: Corporate reports have unintended practical uses
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Boss Spruce, Clerk Stone, all fictional monkeys
text: Spruce printed a thick annual report for each worker. Stone could not find the desk space to open hers. The monkey used it to hold the windy door open while fruit carts rolled in. Spruce came to demand that she read it. Stone pointed to the front page, which said Remove Blocks To Sales. He let the book stay. They read the key totals on one sheet and sold all the bananas before the door swung shut.

title: The raincoat clue
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Slate, Client Coral, all fictional monkeys
text: Slate stood in the rain to look grim while Coral waited indoors. The monkey sleuth soaked his notes and could no longer read the address of her missing cart. Coral gave him a towel and drew the route on the back of a dry bill. Slate traced it to the shed next door. The cart sat under a tarp, full of bananas. He wheeled it back and wrote his report by a warm stove.

title: The dame with the wet shoes
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Storm, Client Pearl, all fictional monkeys
text: Pearl asked Storm to find her stolen shoes. The monkey sleuth saw wet prints from her chair to the door. Pearl had put the shoes by the stove, then lost track of them. Storm fetched them but found the heels warped by heat. He lent her flat boots for the walk home. Pearl paid him with bananas and bought new heels the next day. Storm kept a shoe rack far from his own stove after that case.

title: The alley sax clue
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Steel, Player Sax, all fictional monkeys
text: Steel heard a sad sax tune in the alley each night. He thought it marked a secret trade. The monkey watched from behind a crate of bananas until Sax opened the back door. Sax played there because his room had thin walls. Steel asked him to play inside with a rug by the door. The sound grew soft. Steel gave Sax the empty crate to sell for a mute. Both could sleep after the late night tunes.

title: The shadow on the wall
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Soot, Clerk Ember, all fictional monkeys
text: Soot saw a giant shadow at the bank and called Ember to lock the safe. The monkey clerk turned the lamp and found a small moth on its glass. Soot put his hat over the insect and carried it outside. Ember counted the coins and found none missing. Soot wrote Moth on the case file. He kept the lamp farther from the wall, and the bank opened in time to buy the morning bananas.

title: The noir coffee spoon
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Smoke, Waiter Wren, all fictional monkeys
text: Smoke took his coffee black and cold to look tough. Wren saw the monkey shiver and added hot water. Smoke argued until his tail stopped shaking. He finally asked for a spoon and milk. Wren served bananas with the cup. Smoke solved the case of a missing coat while he warmed up, finding it on the hook behind him. He left a fair tip and wore the coat on the rainy walk home.

title: The gumshoe gum
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Grit, Cleaner Gale, all fictional monkeys
text: Grit stepped in gum outside the fruit stall. Each monkey foot stuck to the next, and he could not follow the thief. Gale brought cold water and a flat scraper. Grit freed his shoes and found the fruit seller had taken the bananas inside to avoid rain. There had been no theft. He paid Gale for her work and helped sweep the stall. His new case notes began with a check of the weather.

title: The coded neon sign
target: Noir detectives read patterns into faults
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Grim, Owner Opal, all fictional monkeys
text: Grim watched a neon sign blink over the club. He read its flashes as a secret warning. Opal, the monkey owner, found him writing dots and lines on a napkin. She showed him a loose wire behind the sign. Grim held the ladder while she fixed it. The sign lit up. It said Open. Grim went inside, ordered bananas, and used the napkin to wipe his muddy shoes before sitting at a table.

title: The midnight parcel
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Gray, Baker Bram, all fictional monkeys
text: Bram hired Gray to guard a parcel until twelve. The monkey sleuth kept it under his coat and watched every shadow. At twelve, Bram asked for it back and opened a box of cake candles. He had wanted them safe until his secret party. Gray lit each one and carried the cake inside. The guests cheered. Gray got a slice with bananas and a dry place to hang the coat he had kept shut all night.

title: The witness tail curl
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Flint, Witness Fern, all fictional monkeys
text: Flint thought Fern lied because her tail curled when he asked about the safe. The monkey witness said her chair was too close to the hot pipe. Flint moved it and asked again. Her tail relaxed, and she named the clerk who had changed the lock. Flint checked the receipt and found a legal repair. Fern helped him file the case. He gave her the cool chair and put a guard over the pipe.

title: The fog ferry bill
target: Noir chase scenes miss transport rules
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Frost, Captain Tide, all fictional monkeys
text: Frost chased a shadow onto the ferry without paying. Tide stopped the boat and asked for his fare. The monkey sleuth pointed at the shadow, but it came from a coat on the rail. Frost paid and helped Tide haul the coat in before it blew away. A guest claimed it at the far dock. Frost ate bananas on the ride back and kept his ticket visible in the brim of his hat.

title: The saloon door swing
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sheriff Sage, Owner Oak, all fictional monkeys
text: Sage strode through the saloon doors, which swung back and caught his monkey tail. Oak helped him free it before the piano tune ended. Sage wanted the doors fixed before the next grand entry. Oak fitted soft edges and a catch that held them open. Sage tested the walk slowly, then ordered bananas at the bar. He kept one hand on the door when he left, so the next guest could come in safely.

title: The high noon shade
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sheriff Sunny, Rival Rust, all fictional monkeys
text: Sunny called Rust to a duel at noon. Both monkeys stood in the dust with dry mouths and hot fur. Rust asked if they could settle the cattle fence dispute under a tree. Sunny agreed. They drew the field border in the shade and split the cost of a new gate. No shots fired. They ate bananas at one, then spent two hours fitting hinges while the sun moved off the road.

title: The cowboy cart ride
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Rider Reed, Stable Stella, all fictional monkeys
text: Reed arrived at the stable in full cowboy gear. Stella had no horse, only a cart pulled by two monkeys. Reed refused to ride until he saw the cart shade and the bananas in its basket. He sat down and held his hat over his tail. The ride reached town faster than his planned walk. Reed paid both pullers and helped them oil the wheels before taking the cart back along the dusty lane.

title: The gold pan dinner
target: Gold rush greed finds domestic value
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Prospector Pip, Cook Pru, all fictional monkeys
text: Pip panned the creek all day and found no gold. The monkey brought the empty pan to Pru, who filled it with beans and bananas. Pip ate and noticed that the heavy pan stayed warm. He sold similar pans to the camp cooks instead of digging another hole. Pru tested each one over the stove. By winter Pip had a steady trade, and the creek ran clear where he no longer stirred the mud.

title: The wanted poster sketch
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sheriff Rowan, Artist Ash, all fictional monkeys
text: Ash drew a wanted poster from a vague report. Every monkey in town had brown fur and a long tail, just like the sketch. Rowan held no one. He asked Ash to add the missing red scarf and broken boot. Only one guest wore both. The guest had lost his luggage, not stolen it, and showed the claim tag. Rowan gave back the bag of bananas and asked for written facts before the next poster.

title: The tumbleweed toll
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Mayor Mesa, Rider River, all fictional monkeys
text: Mesa charged a coin for each dry weed that crossed the main road. River saw the monkey town funds swell as wind blew the weeds back and forth. No one could afford to drive a cart through. River caught the weeds in a fence and sold them as dry fuel. Mesa removed the toll when she saw the clear lane. They used the dry fuel to bake bananas at the town feast and kept the road open from then on.

title: The prairie hat well
target: Western hats solve the wrong problem
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Cowboy Clay, Farmer Fenn, all fictional monkeys
text: Clay lost his broad hat down the well. Fenn offered a hook, but the monkey decided to go down like a hero. His tail tangled in the rope before he reached the water. Fenn pulled him up and used the hook herself. The hat came back full of water and one banana leaf. Clay let it dry on the fence. He bought Fenn bananas and kept the hook beside the well for future rescues.

title: The stagecoach bench vote
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Driver Dust, Guest Della, all fictional monkeys
text: Dust drove the coach so fast that Della bounced off her seat. The monkey guests voted to stop until he slowed down. Dust claimed the mail needed speed. Della showed him the letters shaken open in the rack. He tied them with a cord and set a slower pace. The coach reached town with every page intact. Della bought bananas for the guests, and Dust checked the wheels for loose bolts, then joined them.

title: The cactus fence gap
target: Western property claims cause silly conflicts
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Rancher Thorn, Neighbor Moss, all fictional monkeys
text: Thorn planted cactus along his border. Moss could no longer bring bananas through to the shared market. The monkey rivals argued until Thorn caught his own tail on a spine. Moss trimmed a clear path and helped pull the thorn out. They built one gate between the cactus rows. Thorn kept his fence, Moss kept the route, and both could carry crates without needing thick rugs over their fur on every trip.

title: The deputy badge shine
target: Western deputies mistake polish for duty
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Deputy Dew, Sheriff Silt, all fictional monkeys
text: Dew rubbed his badge until it flashed across the town. Silt asked the monkey to find a missing fruit cart. Dew kept at it, sure the shine would scare any thief. Silt traced the cart tracks to a loose wheel by the creek. Dew used the badge pin to hold a patch in place while Silt fixed the axle. They brought the bananas home. Dew let the badge stay scuffed, since it had finally done useful work.

title: The heist empty safe
target: Heist crews steal before checking contents
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Planner Plume, Picker Puck, all fictional monkeys
text: Plume drew a grand plan to steal a locked safe. Puck opened it in seconds, and the monkey crew found only dust. The bananas had been moved to the pantry because a safe had no airflow. Plume paid the owner for the broken lock and asked to work off the rest. Puck fitted pantry latches instead. They earned fair wages by keeping fruit safe, and no longer hauled a steel box through the woods at night.

title: The getaway cart brake
target: Heist escapes undone by small mechanics
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Driver Drift, Planner Dune, all fictional monkeys
text: Dune planned a heist of the prize melon. Drift waited in the getaway cart with his monkey tail over the brake. The melon rolled onto the cart, but the cart would not move. Dune pushed until the owner arrived. Drift lifted his tail, then chose to stay. They gave back the melon and paid for its bruise with bananas. The owner hired them to move the rest of the crop, after testing the brake first.

title: The vault echo rehearsal
target: Heist crews practice in inappropriate venues
