author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Planner Echo, Guard Ember, all fictional monkeys
text: Echo tried his vault speech in a tunnel. Ember heard each word through the vent by the monkey guard desk. She came down with a map and showed Echo where the sound went. Echo gave up the theft plan and offered a tunnel tour instead. Ember checked the route and sold tickets for daytime visits. Echo earned bananas from guests who liked the echo. He kept all talks away from the old vault wall.

title: The stolen replica spoon
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Thief Glint, Curator Gem, all fictional monkeys
text: Glint stole a silver spoon from the gallery. Gem found the monkey hiding it under his fur at the gate. She showed him the real spoon, locked in a glass case. His was a wooden model painted gray. Glint gave it back and asked how to carve one himself. Gem put him in the shop for a lesson after he paid the fine. He made a plain spoon and used it to eat mashed bananas at home.

title: The heist rope job
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Planner Haven, Climber Hazel, all fictional monkeys
text: Haven tied ropes across the yard to reach a roof safe. Hazel climbed one, but the monkey found the roof held only an empty water tank. Haven had misread the plan. They took the ropes down and said sorry to the owner. She needed wash lines in the same yard. Hazel fitted them neatly and Haven washed the dirty cloths. The owner paid them bananas for the work, and the tank stayed empty until the next rain.

title: The jewel swap label
target: Heist teams mix up their replicas
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Planner Jewel, Maker Juno, all fictional monkeys
text: Jewel packed two gems, one real and one false, for a swap at the fair. Juno put both in plain boxes. The monkey planner could not tell which held which. She asked the seller to test them and told the seller her plan before any swap. The seller kept the real gem and paid Juno for the fine model. Jewel sold bananas to cover the fine, then labeled every box in the shop before going home.

title: The museum wax fruit
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Thief Keen, Guard Kia, all fictional monkeys
text: Keen crawled beneath red beams to reach a display of gold bananas. Kia watched the monkey from the door. She turned the beams off and pointed to the open gift stall. The gold fruit was wax, sold for one coin each. Keen paid for one and put it in his bag. Kia let him leave after he wiped his muddy crawl marks off the floor. He kept the wax fruit on his desk, still whole.

title: The key mold crumble
target: Heist gadgets fail basic material tests
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Planner Locke, Baker Lio, all fictional monkeys
text: Locke made a copy of the vault key out of dough. Lio baked it, but the teeth curled in the oven. The monkey planner tried to flatten them and broke the key in half. Lio served both bits with bananas and asked why he had not asked for a real key. Locke went to the owner and applied for work. He earned a legal key to the store room, and Lio baked plain rolls for his first shift.

title: The roof rain cover
target: Heist crews fail to identify targets
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Thief Moon, Roofer May, all fictional monkeys
text: Moon saw a metal box on the roof and planned to steal it. May caught the monkey lifting it and showed him the vent beneath. It was a rain cover, not a safe. Moon put it back before the storm arrived. May asked him to help fit the loose screws as payment for the damage. He did, then bought bananas at the market. The roof stayed dry and he looked inside boxes before making plans from then on.

title: The grand vault dust
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Planner Opal, Guard Orin, all fictional monkeys
text: Opal broke into the old vault and found years of dust. Orin closed the door behind the monkey and asked who would pay to clean the mess. Opal put down his bag and picked up a broom. He swept until the floor shone, then mended the latch. Orin opened the door and gave him a receipt for the repair debt now paid. Opal used his bag to carry bananas home instead of stolen gold.

title: The court banana scale
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Judge Alder, Claimant Ash, all fictional monkeys
text: Ash sued over a small banana in his lunch box. Judge Alder asked the monkey to weigh it beside the large one given to his friend. The large banana had a thick peel and less fruit. Ash weighed only the fruit and found his own share larger. He dropped the claim. Alder split both bananas between them for lunch and ordered the stall to list edible weight, so guests could compare the actual shares.

title: The witness chair squeak
target: Courtroom drama treats noise as testimony
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Judge Birch, Witness Bea, all fictional monkeys
text: Bea sat in the witness chair and it creaked. Birch thought the sound meant the monkey was nervous. Bea shifted her tail, and the chair creaked again. She stood to give her account clearly. The clerk found a loose bolt beneath the seat. Birch paused the hearing while it was fixed. Bea then sat without a sound and told the same facts. The judge weighed those facts alone, with no note about the faulty chair.

title: The jury lunch lock
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Judge Cedar, Juror Clover, all fictional monkeys
text: Cedar sent the jury to a locked room to decide the case. Clover found bananas on the table but no water. The monkey juror knocked until the clerk came. Cedar feared they wanted help with the verdict. Clover held up an empty cup. The clerk brought a jug and opened the side kitchen. The jury did its work with clear heads. Cedar kept a small needs list beside the rules for every later session.

title: The lawyer footnote tower
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Lawyer Dell, Client Dax, all fictional monkeys
text: Dell wrote a brief with more notes below than text. Dax could not find the request from the monkey lawyer for his missing cart. Dell read the pages aloud until his voice failed. Dax drew the cart on one sheet and wrote Give It Back below. Dell added proof that Dax owned it and filed that instead. The court gave back the cart, full of bananas. Dell kept the long brief under his desk to raise the short leg.

title: The oath echo
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Judge Elm, Witness Ember, all fictional monkeys
text: Elm asked Ember to repeat the oath. The monkey said every word, even the request to say it again. The court clerk tried not to laugh. Elm asked one plain query about the lost fruit box. Ember said that she had placed it in the shade behind the gate. The clerk fetched the bananas and checked her account. Elm wrote a clearer oath for the next hearing, without a line that sounded like part of the pledge.

title: The exhibit spoon
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Lawyer Fenn, Judge Fern, all fictional monkeys
text: Fenn showed a spoon as proof that a cake had been stolen. Fern asked how a spoon proved that claim. The monkey lawyer showed crumbs, but the crumbs were from his own lunch. Fern set the spoon aside and asked for the shop record. It showed the cake had been sold and paid for. Fenn cleaned the spoon and gave it back to the cook. He ate bananas with his hands while he rewrote the report.

title: The custody tail kite
target: Legal custody disputes over shared objects
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Judge Grove, Owners Glen and Gale, all fictional monkeys
text: Glen and Gale both claimed a kite. Grove asked each monkey to hold one end of its string. Their tails pulled apart until the paper tore. Grove stopped them and ordered a joint repair. Glen patched the paper while Gale tied a new tail. They flew it side by side at the field after court. Grove split the fee in half and ate bananas on the bench while the shared kite stayed high above them.

title: The courtroom wig vent
target: Judges dress codes cause practical trouble
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Judge Heath, Clerk Holly, all fictional monkeys
text: Heath wore a huge white wig in court. The monkey judge leaned forward and blocked the desk fan. Holly saw the papers heat and curl beside his lamp. She asked him to move the wig, but he called it a symbol of the law. Holly turned the fan toward his face. The wig blew off onto the filing rack. Heath wore a small cap from then on and let the clerk keep cool while noting each case.

title: The bailiff lost gavel
target: Legal symbols hide in plain sight
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Bailiff Iris, Judge Ivy, all fictional monkeys
text: Iris lost the gavel just before court. Ivy refused to begin without it. The monkey bailiff checked every drawer and found only bananas. Ivy tapped a wooden handle on her desk while she waited. Iris pointed at the head beneath the papers. It was the gavel she had held all morning. Ivy cleared her desk and began the case. Iris put a small tray beside her hand, clearly marked for the gavel alone.

title: The appeal ladder
target: Legal appeals confused with physical heights
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Lawyer Jun, Client Jade, all fictional monkeys
text: Jade asked Jun to take her case to a higher court. The monkey lawyer rented a room on the top floor and carried the files up. Jade asked where the new judges were. Jun checked the notice and learned higher meant an appeals panel across town. He gave back the room key and took the files there. Jade bought bananas for the walk. Jun kept the proper address on the front page, ahead of every grand legal phrase.

title: The train bandit timetable
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Bandit Kestrel, Clerk Kit, all fictional monkeys
text: Kestrel waited by the track to rob the noon train. Kit walked past with bananas and asked what the monkey was doing. Kestrel pointed at the rails. Kit showed him a notice that the route had closed last year. Kestrel took his mask off and helped Kit clear weeds from the old train stop. The town opened a fruit stall there. Kestrel sold tickets for cart rides instead, keeping each time on a sign he could read.

title: The frontier piano key
target: Western bars rely on one dramatic tune
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Player Lark, Owner Laurel, all fictional monkeys
text: Lark played one tense tune each time the saloon door opened. Laurel wanted a gentler song for lunch, but his piano had only six working keys. The monkey opened the lid and found bananas stacked against the strings. Laurel had stored them there in the cool dark space. They moved the fruit to a cabinet and tuned the freed keys. Lark played a happy lunch song, and the door could open with no hint of a duel.

title: The western sunset delay
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Rider Mesa, Partner Moss, all fictional monkeys
text: Mesa wanted to ride home at sunset for a fine outline. Moss asked the monkey to leave sooner because their bananas would bruise on the dark road. Mesa waited until the sun dipped, then could not see a rut. The cart wheel sank. Moss lit a lantern and helped push it free. They reached home late and mashed the bruised fruit for the next meal. Mesa set the next trip before dusk, with the lantern packed under his seat.

title: The safecracker ear cone
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Picker Nix, Owner Nell, all fictional monkeys
text: Nix pressed a cone to the safe to hear its clicks. Nell asked the monkey why he had not tried the key she gave him. Nix said his craft needed time. The cone picked up the kitchen timer instead. Nell opened the safe with her key and took out the shop coins. Nix said he had guessed every sound. He gave the fee back and helped Nell count the coins before they bought bananas.

title: The getaway disguise cart
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Planner Oak, Driver Orla, all fictional monkeys
text: Oak painted his cart to look like a bush for the getaway. Orla could not see the path through its thick leaves. The monkey driver stopped at the gate before it crashed. Oak cut a clear window and saw the bush would never fool anyone on wheels. They dropped the heist and sold the cart as a garden shade wagon. Orla took plants in it all summer, with bananas beneath the leafy roof for lunch.

title: The contract tail line
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Lawyer Pine, Client Pax, all fictional monkeys
text: Pax signed a deal to sit for a picture. The bench had no tail gap, and the monkey could not keep still. Pine read the deal and found it offered only a seat. Pax asked the painter to cut a notch or refund his fee. The painter cut it, then did the picture in an hour. Pine added Tail Space to the next deal and sat at ease, holding bananas that the painter could leave out if he wished.

title: The courtroom banana peel
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Judge Reed, Lawyer Rue, all fictional monkeys
text: Rue brought a banana peel to prove the hallway floor was unsafe. The monkey lawyer left it by the witness chair. Reed nearly slipped and ordered it put in a sealed box. Rue said sorry and showed the photo taken before the fall. The court used that image and kept the floor clear. Reed ruled that the hall needed a bin. Rue paid for a second bin beside his own desk, where loose proof had begun to pile.

title: The noir window blind
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sleuth Quill, Client Quartz, all fictional monkeys
text: Quill kept the blinds shut to make his office look grave. Quartz came to ask about a missing cart, but the monkey sleuth could not read the receipt in the gloom. She opened one blind. The cart stood outside the window, where the driver had parked it. Quill gave the fee back and helped carry the bananas in. He kept the blind open for the next client, saving the dark room for naps after work.

title: The western duel coin
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sheriff Rust, Shopkeeper Rain, all fictional monkeys
text: Rust called for a duel after Rain gave him the wrong coin. The monkey seller set both coins on the counter and showed they had the same value. Rust stared at the varied faces and finally read the rims. He put his hand away from the empty holster. Rain sold him bananas at the proper price. Rust carried a small coin chart after that, and the town settled coin rows at the counter, leaving the dusty square to lizards.

title: The heist crew invoice
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Planner Sable, Builder Stone, all fictional monkeys
text: Sable hired Stone to build a tunnel for a heist. Stone sent a bill larger than the value of the stolen bananas. The monkey planner checked each charge and found digging, boards, and cart hire all cost real money. Sable stopped the theft and paid Stone for the work done. They turned the short tunnel into a cool fruit cellar with consent of the owner. Sable rented shelf space there and earned the money back over a season.

title: The sitcom door key
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Actor Alf, Neighbor Nell, all fictional monkeys
text: Alf burst into the flat every day for the sitcom. Nell finally changed the lock. The monkey actor stood outside while the laugh track played to no one. He knocked and asked to come in. Nell opened the door and offered bananas. The scene worked better with one real pause. Alf kept a knock in every later script, and Nell could finish her tea before his daily grand entry began.

title: The laugh track leak
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Actor Bea, Sound Sol, all fictional monkeys
text: Bea gave a sad speech while Sol played a loud laugh track. The monkey actor stopped and pointed to the wrong tape. Sol rewound it, but laughs still filled the room. Bea cut power to the speaker and spoke in silence. The crew heard the scene clearly at last. They ate bananas during the reset. Sol labeled each tape by mood, and Bea let him test the sad one before she began her next line.

title: The reality show broom
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Host Chet, Guest Gilda, all fictional monkeys
text: Chet told Gilda to fight another guest over the last broom. The monkey guest took a dust pan and swept with dry leaves instead. Chet said that made poor drama. Gilda showed him the clean floor and asked for a task worth a prize. He gave the guests a shelf to build as a team. The show aired their work with no staged row. Gilda won bananas for the neatest shelf and used the broom only later.

title: The quiz prize box
target: Game shows offer unsuitable grand prizes
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Host Dell, Player Dara, all fictional monkeys
text: Dara won the quiz and got a huge stone bowl. The monkey player lived in a small tree hut. Dell asked her to pose beside the prize while her tail shook as she tried to lift it. Dara asked to swap it for seeds. The show agreed. She planted bananas and sent a photo when the first fruit grew. Dell used that image in the next prize list, where each gift now had a choice of size.

title: The soap opera letter
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Actor Enid, Actor Echo, all fictional monkeys
text: Enid found a letter that could settle the plot. Echo urged the monkey to hide it until the next season. Enid read it aloud instead. It was a receipt for bananas, not a secret wedding. Echo stared at the wrong prop in her hand. The crew found the right letter beneath a cup and shot the scene again. Enid put all letters in marked trays, so a lunch bill could never run the plot twice.

title: The talent show tail
target: Talent contests prize spectacle over skill
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Singer Fia, Judge Fern, all fictional monkeys
text: Fia sang well, but Fern wanted a bigger finish. The monkey tied ribbons to her tail and spun while holding the final note. She grew dizzy and forgot the words. Fern gave her water and asked for a simple song. Fia sat on a stool and sang it cleanly. The crowd sat still, then cheered. Fern gave her a plain mic and bananas as the prize, leaving the loose ribbons for the stage curtain.

title: The weather show window
target: Broadcasts trust scripts over visible weather
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Host Gale, Producer Gus, all fictional monkeys
text: Gale read a report of clear skies while rain hit the studio window. Gus pointed at the script, asking the monkey to keep going. Gale set the page down and looked outside. She told viewers to bring coats, then opened the window to show the rain. Gus fetched a towel for the wet floor. They amended the report and moved the bananas away from the sill. The next script left a blank for what Gale saw herself.

title: The cooking show camera bite
target: TV cameras interfere with food preparation
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Chef Herb, Camera Ivy, all fictional monkeys
text: Ivy moved her camera close to film Herb taste the stew. The monkey chef knocked the lens with his spoon and left a red smear. Herb cleaned it with a soft cloth while the stew bubbled. Ivy filmed the pot from the side instead. The viewers saw the food clearly with no spoon in the way. Herb served bananas after filming, and Ivy put a safe space mark on the floor for the next shoot.

title: The reunion show missing chairs
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Host Jade, Guest Jun, all fictional monkeys
text: Jade booked eight guests and six chairs for the reunion show. Jun refused to fight over a seat. The monkey fetched two crates and put soft pads on them. Jade tried to ask who hated whom, but Jun asked who could help move the set after filming. All eight raised hands. They did the work before tea and bananas arrived. Jade aired that scene, which got more praise than the old clips of their rows.

title: The detective show clue light
target: Crime television hides evidence in darkness
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Actor Kestrel, Lighting Kit, all fictional monkeys
text: Kestrel checked a dark room for the prop clue. Kit dimmed the lamp further to make the scene tense. The monkey actor stepped on the clue and broke it. Kit turned the light up and fetched a spare prop clue. They cleared the broken bits, reset the clue, and shot again with enough light to see. Kestrel solved the case on camera. Kit saved the darkest lamp setting for the credits, after every actor left.

title: The movie explosion cart
target: Action films prioritize spectacle over sense
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Director Lark, Stunt Laurel, all fictional monkeys
text: Lark wanted Laurel to leap from a cart as smoke burst behind it. The monkey stunt actor asked where the cart would stop. Lark had planned only the leap. Laurel fitted a brake and marked a soft landing patch. They tested the route without smoke before filming. The shot looked grand and no fruit spilled from the prop crate. Laurel ate the bananas after the scene, while Lark added a stop point to every later stunt plan.

title: The romance airport gate
target: Film romances depend on missed departures
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Actor Mira, Actor Moss, all fictional monkeys
text: Mira ran to the airport to confess her love before Moss left. The monkey found him at the wrong gate, eating bananas. His flight had moved, and he had not read the board. Mira gave the speech while they walked to the right gate side by side. Moss thanked her and agreed to call. The film boss kept the scene because Moss reached his flight on time, with no need to halt a plane on the runway.

title: The horror basement bulb
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Actor Nix, Prop Nell, all fictional monkeys
text: Nix went down into the cellar with a dying torch. Nell held a box of fresh bulbs beside the monkey actor. The script called for dark scenes, but Nix could not see the stairs. He fitted a new bulb before the camera rolled. The scene still felt eerie because the door creaked behind him. Nell stayed close with the spare torch. They found the prop bananas on the bottom shelf and did the shot without falling over them.

title: The epic speech wind
target: Historical film speeches meet actual weather
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Actor Oak, Director Orla, all fictional monkeys
text: Oak gave a vast speech on a hill while wind tugged his monkey cape. Orla could hear none of the words. Oak tried yelling, then lost his hat down the slope. The crew filmed his stance without sound and taped the speech indoors later. Oak fetched the hat and wrapped the bananas inside it for lunch. Orla kept the wind in the final scene, but the viewers could finally hear what the hero had said.

title: The sequel spare door
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Director Pine, Actor Pax, all fictional monkeys
text: Pine wanted the broken door left hanging so a sequel could use it. Pax saw the hinge wobble over the monkey crew. He propped the door safely and asked to film a repair scene. Pine agreed, though he feared it would end the story. The viewers liked seeing the hero finish the job. Pax carried the spare hinge home, and Pine planned a new sequel about a new door instead of leaving this one unsafe.

title: The montage mop
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Actor Quill, Cleaner Quartz, all fictional monkeys
text: Quill trained for the fight in a fast montage. He threw ropes, sacks, and towels across the monkey gym while music played. Quartz stopped the shot when a sack rolled under his foot. They cleaned the floor and filmed a final sweep in the montage. Quill reached the match with a clear space to train. Quartz got a screen credit, and the bananas stayed on a shelf where no flying towel could strike them.

title: The silent film sneeze
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Actor Reed, Pianist Rue, all fictional monkeys
text: Reed played a silent hero with a solemn face. His monkey fur tickled his nose, and he sneezed during the take. Rue matched the sneeze with a sharp piano chord. The crew laughed and kept filming. Reed turned it into a scene where the hero blows dust off a lost gold map. Rue played a light tune as he found the bananas marked on it. The final film had no speech, but the sneeze still got the biggest laugh.

title: The film festival queue
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Director Sable, Usher Snow, all fictional monkeys
text: Sable brought a short film to the film fair. The entry speech took longer than the film, and the monkey viewers waited with tired tails. Snow cut the speech to one line and started the reel. All guests saw the full story before the hall closed. Sable thanked Snow and served bananas outside after the credits. At the next event she printed her notes on a small card, leaving the screen for the film itself.

title: The superhero trailer chair
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Editor Thorn, Actor Thyme, all fictional monkeys
text: Thorn cut a trailer that made Thyme lifting a chair look like saving the world. The monkey actor asked what the full movie would show. Thorn watched the source reel and saw only a room move. He recut the trailer as a funny tale about finding space for guests. Viewers came for that story and enjoyed it. Thyme carried bananas to the first show, then put the same chair beside the table where people could really sit.

title: The space opera wig
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Actor Vale, Costume Wren, all fictional monkeys
text: Vale wore a vast silver wig as ruler of the stars. The monkey could not fit through the ship door. Wren took the wig off and tested the doorway with a small cap. Vale could enter, sit, and reach the buttons at last. Wren put the silver hair on the throne behind him. It looked grand in the wide shots. Vale ate bananas without hair in his mouth, and the ship scenes ended on time.

title: The orchestra banana rest
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Conductor Ash, Player Alder, all fictional monkeys
text: Ash told Alder to take a rest during the slow passage. The monkey player lay down on the stage with bananas by his tail. Ash stopped the band and told him that rest meant silence for a few beats. Alder sat back up and counted them. The tune flowed well on the next try. After the concert Ash marked a real break on the plan. Alder ate then, with his horn safe in its case.

title: The drum solo clock
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Drummer Birch, Singer Bea, all fictional monkeys
text: Birch played a drum solo so long that Bea missed the last bus. The monkey singer sat by the stage with her bag of bananas. Birch finally stopped when the hall clock chimed. Bea asked him to use that chime as a limit next time. They walked home side by side and shared the fruit. At the next show his solo ended in four minutes. Bea caught her bus, and Birch could pack his drums before the hall closed.

title: The guitar hero string
target: Musicians favor poses over equipment care
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Guitarist Cedar, Tech Cora, all fictional monkeys
text: Cedar struck a grand pose and broke his guitar string. Cora handed the monkey a spare while the crowd waited. He tried the pose again, but she pointed at the sharp edge on his guitar bridge. They filed it smooth and fitted the string. Cedar played a simple tune and did not twist the guitar behind his head. The crowd sang along. Cora got bananas in the wings, and Cedar kept the spare strings beside a small file in his case.

title: The pop star mirror
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Singer Dawn, Dresser Dell, all fictional monkeys
text: Dawn wanted every strand of fur in place before her concert. Dell combed the monkey for an hour while the guests waited. One curl refused to lie flat. Dell tied a small ribbon around it and opened the stage door. Dawn sang with the curl waving above her brow. Fans copied the ribbon next day. Dawn kept the combing short from then on and ate bananas with Dell in the spare time before each show.

title: The bass note floor
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Bassist Ember, Builder Elm, all fictional monkeys
text: Ember struck one low note and felt the stage shake. The monkey bassist stopped before the next chord. Elm checked beneath the boards and found a loose support. They moved the crowd to the yard while he fixed it. Ember played on a solid crate, with her tail clear of the strings. The outdoor show sounded good. Elm ended the repair before rain came, and the bananas served at the break stayed under the tent.

title: The gallery blank frame
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Artist Fenn, Guest Fern, all fictional monkeys
text: Fenn hung an empty frame and called it the essence of bananas. Fern asked the monkey artist why the real fruit sat hidden in a drawer. Fenn said the gap invited thought. Fern put one banana in the frame and let guests draw its shape on scrap paper. They stayed longer than before. Fenn served the fruit after the session and hung the art next day, with the same frame around the newest sketch.

title: The sculpture tail crack
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sculptor Grove, Builder Gilda, all fictional monkeys
text: Grove made a tall stone monkey with a thin tail. Gilda saw a crack near its base before the opening. Grove wanted guests to see it as it was. Gilda roped the area off and tested the tail with a padded pole. It broke into the soft grass. Grove carved the stump smooth and set the fallen tail beside it. The show opened safely, with bananas on a low table well away from the heavy stone pieces.

title: The poetry slam whisper
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Poet Haze, Host Heath, all fictional monkeys
text: Haze wrote a poem about a lost spoon. Heath told the monkey to shout it to win the slam. Haze tried, but her voice broke before the last line. She asked for a quiet reading instead. The room hushed, and guests heard where the spoon had gone, into the banana mash. Haze pulled it from the prop bowl at the end. Heath gave her the prize for the clear story, not the volume.

title: The ballet tail balance
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Dancer Iris, Coach Ivy, all fictional monkeys
text: Iris tucked her tail into a belt for the ballet. The monkey tipped to one side on each turn. Ivy asked why she hid the tail, and Iris pointed to a rule in the old book. Ivy undid the belt and let her try again. Iris spun neatly with her tail held out. They changed the rule and marked the safe space around each dancer. Iris ate bananas after class, her tail resting freely over the bench.

title: The art auction cough
target: Art auctions mistake accidental sounds for bids
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Auctioneer Jade, Guest Jun, all fictional monkeys
text: Jun coughed at the auction and won a giant picture. The monkey guest had meant to bid on nothing. Jade paused the sale and asked for a clear raised hand. Jun drank water and kept both hands on his knees. Another guest bought the picture with a real bid. Jade placed number cards at each seat for later bids. Jun bought bananas in the lobby, where a price tag could not mistake his cough for a promise.

title: The novelist locked ending
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Writer Kestrel, Editor Kit, all fictional monkeys
text: Kestrel wrote a mystery with no final chapter. Kit asked the monkey writer where the stolen bananas had gone. Kestrel said the reader should decide. Kit found three clues that led to the pantry and asked him to open its door on the page. Kestrel wrote the scene, and showed that the cook had stored the fruit safely. Kit took the book. Kestrel left one tiny riddle about the pantry key for the next story, which had its own ending.

title: The theater ghost rope
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Actor Lark, Stagehand Laurel, all fictional monkeys
text: Lark blamed a ghost when the curtain rose by itself. Laurel traced the rope to a snag under the stool used by the monkey actor. Each time Lark leaned back, his tail pulled the rope. Laurel freed it and moved the stool. Lark bowed to the empty wings as an apology to the ghost he had named. The curtain stayed down until the right cue. Laurel ate bananas during the break without needing to watch a haunted knot.

title: The critic paint shoe
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Critic Mira, Painter Moss, all fictional monkeys
text: Mira called the picture dull while she stepped in wet blue paint. The monkey critic left prints across the gallery floor. Moss handed her a mop before he spoke about the review. Mira cleaned each print and noticed how the blue changed under varied lights. She wrote a more careful piece about those colors. Moss hung it near the final canvas. Mira left her shoes outside the next studio and brought bananas instead of mud on her soles.

title: The jazz solo map
target: Jazz improvisation loses the shared tune
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Sax Nix, Drummer Nell, all fictional monkeys
text: Nix strayed so far from the melody that Nell could not follow. The monkey drummer held a steady beat while Nix looked for the chorus. At last Nell tapped the opening phrase on a small bell. Nix heard it and joined the song again. They wrote the key changes on one card for the next show. After the set they ate bananas, and Nix kept the bell close as a simple way back home.

title: The museum audio nap
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Guide Oak, Visitor Orla, all fictional monkeys
text: Oak taped a long audio guide for one small bowl. Orla heard it until the monkey fell asleep on a bench. Oak found her there beside a bag of bananas. He cut the guide to a short account of who made the bowl and how it was used. Orla woke and tried the new version. She could now tour the whole room before lunch. Oak kept extra facts in a booklet for guests who chose to stay longer.

title: The poster face price
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Designer Pine, Seller Pax, all fictional monkeys
text: Pine made a poster with a huge monkey face and no fruit. Pax asked how guests would know he sold bananas. Pine said the face looked warm. Pax set a real bunch beside the draft and asked for its shape on the page. Pine drew it and added the price. More guests came to the stall that day. He kept the face small in the corner, where it could smile without hiding what was for sale.

title: The folk song kettle
target: Folk music turns every object into lore
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Singer Quill, Cook Quartz, all fictional monkeys
text: Quill wrote a ballad about the old kettle. The monkey claimed it had crossed seas and lasted through wars. Quartz showed him the shop receipt from last spring. Quill rewrote the song about a kettle that made good tea each day. The chorus was short enough for guests to join. Quartz served bananas during the encore. Quill sang the true price as a joke, and all guests knew what the useful little kettle had really done.

title: The opera stair breath
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Singer Reed, Director Rue, all fictional monkeys
text: Reed climbed six flights before singing his grand aria. The monkey had no breath left when Rue raised the baton. Rue asked him to arrive earlier or use the lift. Reed came early next night, warmed his voice slowly, and sang the full tune. Rue moved the heavy costume up above in advance. Reed could eat bananas after the show instead of gasping on the stairs, and the guests heard every word of the final song.

title: The comic strip tail panel
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Artist Sable, Reader Snow, all fictional monkeys
text: Sable drew a monkey leap across three panels, but the tail was gone in the middle one. Snow asked how the hero could land without balance. Sable added a small panel where the tail curled round a branch. The scene made sense, and Snow laughed at the banana peel waiting below. Sable drew the hero as he caught that too. The strip ended with both feet on dry ground and the peel in a bin, where the next reader could see it.

title: The portrait sitter banana
target: Portrait painters ignore their sitters comfort
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Painter Thorn, Sitter Thyme, all fictional monkeys
text: Thorn asked Thyme to hold one pose for hours. The monkey sitter gripped bananas until the fruit went soft. Thorn liked the solemn face, but Thyme was simply hungry. They paused for lunch and swapped the fruit with a wooden model. Thyme held it lightly while Thorn did the picture. The face now looked calm. Thorn listed breaks in his next booking, and Thyme took the real fruit home without another bruise.

title: The radio silence cue
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Actor Vale, Sound Wren, all fictional monkeys
text: Vale acted a grim silent glare in the radio studio. Wren waited, but the monkey fans heard only empty air. She asked him to speak one short line or rustle the note in his hand. Vale tore the prop note and said he would not sign. The scene became clear without a face to see. Wren saved the glare for the cast photo, then served bananas while Vale tried keeping his paper close to the mic.

title: The documentary tripod tail
target: Documentaries claim authenticity through poor equipment
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Filmmaker Ash, Subject Alder, all fictional monkeys
text: Ash filmed Alder sorting bananas with a shaky camera. He said the wobble felt honest. The monkey subject asked viewers to see his hands clearly. Ash set the camera on a tripod, but one leg stood on his own tail. He moved it, tested the frame, and filmed with no shake. Viewers could tell ripe fruit from green. Ash kept one shaky shot of the market outside and used the calm view for every step of the sorting lesson.

title: The costume drama zipper
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Actor Birch, Dresser Bea, all fictional monkeys
text: Birch wore a royal coat in the period play. The monkey could not hide the bright zipper down its back. Bea sewed a flap over it, but caught his tail in the stitch. They undid the seam and made a new tail opening. The coat looked old from the seats and came off easily in the wings. Birch thanked Bea with bananas and hung the coat on a wide hook, so the flap would not crease before the next day.

title: The stage sword of foam
target: Stage battles need sensible prop design
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Actor Cedar, Prop Cora, all fictional monkeys
text: Cedar swung a metal sword and knocked a lamp off the stage. Cora caught it before the monkey could begin his next move. She made a foam sword and painted it gray. Cedar tried the same fight slowly, keeping well clear of the lights. The viewers saw a grand duel, but every strike was soft. Cora stored the real sword in a locked rack and used the spare foam to line the box of prop bananas.

title: The album cover soup
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Singer Dawn, Artist Dell, all fictional monkeys
text: Dawn chose a cover showing a bowl of soup for her album of love songs. Dell asked the monkey how it linked to the music. Dawn said the colors matched her fur. Dell played the songs and drew two tails linked instead. Dawn liked that better and kept the soup picture for a recipe card. The album sold well. Dell ate bananas at the launch and gave guests the soup card as a useful extra.

title: The mural window block
target: Public art fails its surrounding building
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Painter Ember, Clerk Elm, all fictional monkeys
text: Ember painted a bright mural over the shop front, even the window. Elm could no longer see the monkey guests arrive. Ember peeled the paint off the glass and framed the window with vines instead. Guests could see bananas inside, and Elm could wave them in. The mural still looked lively along the wall. Ember signed it beside the clear pane and drew future wall plans on one sheet and window plans on another.

title: The poetry book page gap
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Poet Fenn, Binder Fern, all fictional monkeys
text: Fenn placed one word on each page of his poem. Fern needed a thick cover for the monkey book, though the poem lasted only a minute aloud. She laid the pages side by side on one sheet and asked him to read it. The rhythm stayed the same. Fenn chose that version and spent the saved paper on another poem. Fern bound both in a thin book, which fit beside the bananas in his small travel bag.

title: The award speech clock
target: Arts awards speeches exceed audience patience
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Actor Grove, Host Gilda, all fictional monkeys
text: Grove thanked every monkey he had ever met in his award speech. Gilda saw the hall clock pass twelve while his list still grew. She handed him a card with five blank lines. Grove chose the names from this film and closed with one clear thanks to the crew. The crowd clapped at last. Gilda served bananas before all guests left, and Grove sent the other thanks by letter in the morning.

title: The puppet tail string
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Puppeteer Haze, Helper Heath, all fictional monkeys
text: Haze tied puppet strings to her monkey tail for a new trick. The puppet danced, then pulled her back into the curtain. Heath held the stand and helped untie her. They put the strings on a small hand frame instead. Haze could bow without moving the puppet now. The show ended with a neat dance and no torn cloth. Heath gave the puppet a wooden banana, while Haze ate the real bananas after the curtain fell.

title: The last encore door
target: Concert performers ignore venue closing time
author: IMI Seven Letter Monkey Desk
cast: Singer Iris, Keeper Ivy, all fictional monkeys
text: Iris took a third encore while Ivy waited to lock the hall. The monkey crowd wanted more, but the last bus would soon leave. Iris sang one brief verse, thanked all guests, and opened the side door. Guests reached the stop in time. Ivy helped her pack the mic and cables. Iris left bananas in the crew room as thanks and put a clear final song on the next program, so claps could end without another endless encore.

title: The crown that peeled
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pip drew the gold crown from a stone and found a banana stuck beneath it. Moss bowed. The monkeys in the trees bowed too, until Pip bit the fruit. The crown slipped over his eyes. A terrible dragon had stolen their breakfast, Moss said. Pip could hear the dragon snore behind the stone. He fed it the peel, which made it sneeze up six baskets of fruit. Pip gave back the crown. A king should see his lunch.

title: The glass vine
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Nell had a splendid tail, but the glass shoe would not fit it. Bram tried every monkey in the palace. Nell asked why a tail needed a shoe. The prince had dropped it while climbing a vine. Nell took the shoe up the tree and caught rain in it. At breakfast the thirsty prince came for a drink. He found Nell beside his lost cup and asked to share her branch.

title: The sleeping gate
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Tuck found the castle asleep, including its gate. Wren shook the bars, but they only snored. Their breakfast was inside. Tuck made a generous offer of one banana if the gate would wake. It dreamed of fruit and opened its mouth. Wren slipped through with her tail round a bar and fetched the baskets. They left a banana in the hinge. The gate woke and thought lunch had grown in its teeth.

title: The bean receipt
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bo traded a banana cart for magic beans. Fern demanded a receipt. The seller had vanished, so they planted the beans beside his sign. A beanstalk rose into a cloud, taking the sign with it. Bo climbed with his tail round each stalk. A giant demanded rent. Fern showed the sign, which promised free lodging. The giant sighed. He gave them breakfast, then climbed down to change his sign.

title: The dragon tooth fairy
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Lark put a dragon tooth under her leaf pillow. Dot warned that a terrible fairy might come. Lark stayed awake with her breakfast banana. At dawn a tiny fairy tugged at the tooth, but it weighed more than her cart. Lark looped her tail round it and helped. The fairy offered a coin. Lark asked for a brush instead. Next day she cleaned the dragon teeth. The fairy hired a larger cart.

title: The wish pond drain
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Milo wished the pond would fill with bananas. It did, and Ash fell into the heap. Milo wished for a splendid boat, but it sat on top of the fruit. The pond spirit said he had one wish left. Ash poked a tail through the boat drain and pulled up a plug. Water rushed in beneath their breakfast. Milo wished for forks. They sailed home with fruit for the village and a boat full of lunch.

title: The honest mirror
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rose asked the magic mirror who had the finest tail. It said Kip, who had spilled breakfast on his. Rose called this a terrible error. The mirror showed Kip using his sticky tail to lift a trapped beetle. Rose wiped her own tail, then used it to pull a small monkey up a steep branch. That night the mirror named Rose. Kip asked who had the cleanest floor. The mirror went dark.

title: The moat soup
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Otto guarded the castle moat with a splendid spear. June came to rescue the royal banana trees, but the moat smelled delicious. A witch had turned it into soup. June dipped her tail, yelped, and fetched a spoon. Otto refused to leave his post until June showed him that the post was now a carrot. They ate a path across. The king thanked them, then asked why his bridge had no gravy.

title: The borrowed spell
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Fenn borrowed a spell to clean the monkey tower. Kit read the warning, but Fenn had waved his tail. Every banana peel grew a broom. They swept the beds into the yard and the wizard into a bucket. Kit held up the splendid spell book. Fenn found the word reverse on its cover. He turned the book round. The brooms swept the beds home, then took breakfast from the table as their pay.

title: The tiny quest
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Hazel packed a splendid sword for her quest. Tom packed breakfast. The map led through dark roots to a chest no bigger than a walnut. Hazel tried to pry it open with her sword, but the blade bent. Tom used the tip of his tail. Inside lay a tiny crown and a plea to guard an ant king. Hazel stuck her bent sword in the soil as a fence. Tom fed the ants banana crumbs.

title: The frog toll
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ada kissed the frog at the bridge. It stayed a frog and charged her a banana. Len said the tale promised a prince. The frog held up a contract, then pointed to the crown on its head. Ada read the fine print with her tail holding the page flat. The prince could choose his own shape. She paid for a return ticket instead. At breakfast the frog kissed her coin and hoped for gold.

title: The hood with pockets
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Red wore a hood with enormous pockets to carry bananas to Gus. A wolf asked which tree held her grandpa. Red gave it a map upside down. It ran straight into a pond. When she reached Gus, her pockets shook. The wet wolf had climbed from the pond and hidden in one. Gus offered it breakfast on the porch while Red stitched both pockets shut. The wolf went home with a full belly and a map it could finally read.

title: The straw palace
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Nico built a palace from straw. Tess built hers from banana crates. A terrible wind blew Nico into Tess through the open door. The king ordered a stone palace by breakfast. Nico had no stone, so he tied his tail to the crates and stacked them round the throne. Tess sold tickets to watch the wind test. It blew through the gaps. The king declared fresh air a royal asset and paid them in fruit.

title: The golden egg pan
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: May found a golden egg beneath her banana tree. Orin brought a splendid pan and tried to fry it. The egg dented the pan. May tapped the shell with her tail and heard a tiny voice asking for shade. They built a nest under leaves. At breakfast a golden goose hatched and ate every banana peel. Orin sold the dented pan as a nest bowl. May kept the goose, which laid plain eggs with shiny yolks.

title: The lost tower lift
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Fia waited atop a tower with a basket of bananas. Reed called for her to lower her tail. She had spent yesterday tying it into a splendid braid, so she lowered the basket instead. Reed climbed inside. Halfway up, he sneezed and shook the rope. Fia lowered him again and sent down a note asking for stairs. Reed built them from tree limbs. They ate on the first step. Fia untied her braid so the birds could take its loose ribbons.

title: The ogre shoe shop
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Sol opened a shoe shop in a hollow tree. Bea sold laces woven from strong vines. An enormous ogre asked for shoes by breakfast, but Sol had only monkey sizes. Bea looped her tail through a lace and measured the feet. Sol cut two banana boats into soles. The ogre stepped into the stream and floated off smiling. Bea put a sign on the tree offering shoes for wet days. Sol charged extra for oars.

title: The fairy cake tax
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Mina baked a cake for the fairy queen. Cobb ate its banana crown before she came. A terrible curse made his tail grow a cake at each sneeze. Mina feared a flood of frosting, but Cobb found the cakes delicious. He sneezed into empty pans until the queen arrived. She saw the bare first cake and the full table. Cobb paid her tax in cake. The queen lifted the curse because she had run out of plates.

title: The sword in the stump
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Elm tugged the sword in the stump with both hands. Joss tried her tail. Neither could free it. A messenger said whoever pulled it out would rule the forest. Elm noticed a splendid latch beneath the bark. He opened the stump like a box. The sword fell into his lap. Joss found the old king inside, eating bananas. He had hidden there to nap. Elm shut the latch and chose a quiet branch of his own.

title: The pumpkin coach seat
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Cleo needed a coach to reach the moon feast. Ned turned a pumpkin into one with a borrowed wand. It looked splendid until Cleo sat down and sank into soup. Ned read the wand label carefully. It made meals, not wheels. Cleo tied her tail to a vine, swung to the feast, and carried the pumpkin with her. The guests had brought dry bread. Her soup won the royal prize. Ned rode home in the empty rind.

title: The dragon library card
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ivy climbed into a dragon cave to fetch a stolen book. Mel waited outside with breakfast. The dragon curled round an enormous heap of books but could not turn a page with its claws. Ivy used her tail to hold the book open. Mel brought the banana bowl inside. The dragon lent them the book after the last page. Ivy made it a library card. Its first fine covered three scorched pages and one melted spoon.

title: The invisible cape peg
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Puck wore a splendid cape that made him vanish. Nia could still see his banana, floating through the hall. He ate it to hide, then dropped the peel on a guard. The guard followed the peel trail to the pantry. Puck hung the cape on a peg and asked Nia to hide him. She carefully put a bowl on his head. The guard found an empty cape and a strange bowl with a tail. He arrested the bowl.

title: The royal pea ladder
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ava stacked eight beds above a pea to test a royal guest. Finn climbed the tower with his tail round a post. At breakfast he said he had slept badly. Ava reached for the splendid crown, but Finn pointed to a loose bed leg. It rocked all night. She fixed it with the pea. Finn slept well the next night. Ava gave him the crown for finding the fault and kept the pea under the leg.

title: The cave echo oath
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Hugo swore to bring a treasure home from the cave. Mae heard the echo swear the same oath. They carried bananas through the dark. At a fork Hugo asked which way to go. His echo shouted both ways. Mae carefully tapped each wall with her tail. One wall rang like a drum. Behind it lay a chest full of bells. They took one home. The echo kept the rest and rang them whenever it felt lonely.

title: The witch broom parking
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Zia landed her broom in the royal banana tree. Rufus found three more brooms jammed beside it. The witches had come for a splendid feast but could not fly home. Zia carefully looped her tail round a branch and climbed to the top. She tied each broom to a leaf tag, then called its owner by name. Rufus held the ladder. Last came the queen, who had parked her broom upside down and lost her hat in the roots.

title: The shadow bridge toll
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Toby had to cross a bridge before breakfast. Sal, the troll guard, demanded a terrible riddle first. Toby asked what had a tail but could not climb. Sal guessed for an hour. Toby sat on the rail and peeled a banana. At last he pointed to the bridge shadow, which ended in a narrow tail. Sal leaned over to see. Toby crossed behind him. Sal charged the shadow a toll and spent all day waiting for payment.

title: The snow queen kettle
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Una found the banana grove trapped in ice. Beck brought a splendid sword to fight the snow queen. Una brought a kettle. She poured warm water over one stem, and the fruit came loose. The queen arrived to demand silence. Her teeth shook too much for speech. Una offered tea and breakfast. Beck used his sword to stir the pot. The queen thawed the grove in return for a kettle she could carry home.

title: The phoenix ash tray
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dara bought a phoenix to warm her tree house. Wes built an enormous perch. The bird burst into flame beside the banana bowl and left a pile of ash. Dara carefully swept it into a tray with her tail. At dawn it hatched again beneath a baked banana. Wes wanted a cage. Dara set out a fresh tray instead. Soon the village lined up for hot fruit. The phoenix got a new perch and a strict closing hour.

title: The gnome hat map
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Lulu found a tiny map sewn inside a splendid hat. Moss said it led to a gnome kingdom. They followed it through roots, over a log, and under the banana stall. Lulu carefully lifted a board with her tail. Beneath it sat a gnome counting crumbs. The map was his hat lining, and he wanted it back. Lulu traded it for a tour. The kingdom had one chair. Moss had to reign while standing outside.

title: The cursed spoon choir
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Jem stole a spoon from the witch kitchen. It sang whenever he tried to eat breakfast. Ora warned that a terrible curse could last forever. Jem tied the spoon to his tail and climbed to the grove. Each time he scooped banana mash, the song shook ripe fruit from the branches. Ora fetched baskets. By noon the witch came to reclaim it. Jem offered her half the crop. She left the spoon and asked for the tune.

title: The royal moat ferry
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Rex rode to rescue Pia from a tower. The bridge had fallen, and his horse refused to swim. Pia carefully lowered a basket on a vine. Rex put his splendid sword inside. She sent it back with a banana and a fare sign. He climbed in, tail curled round the rope. Pia hauled him across and opened a ferry service. Rex stayed to sell tickets. The horse got a season pass and a seat with a wider door.

title: The enchanted door bell
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Eli reached a splendid door in the mountain. Mo rang its bell with his tail. A voice asked them to state their quest. Eli wanted the golden banana. Mo wanted breakfast. The door opened for Mo and shut in front of Eli. Mo returned with a banana on a plate. Eli called this cheating. The door said it had run a cafe for years and wished heroes would read the menu. Eli ordered toast and got a seat.

title: The gingerbread repair
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bess found a splendid cottage whose sweet cake wall had a crack. Hal bit the loose edge. The witch charged him for damage. Bess used her tail to spread banana paste in the crack and carefully pressed the piece back. Hal offered to mend the roof. The witch handed him a bag of sweets and watched every bite. By dusk the cottage stood firm. Hal paid for one window he had eaten. Bess earned a room with a plain wooden door.

title: The unicorn mud bath
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Arlo sought a unicorn in the grove. Meg found hoof marks beside the banana pond. A splendid horn poked from the mud, but its owner refused to rise. It had spent yesterday posing for royal coins and wanted a rest. Arlo cleaned the horn with his tail while Meg held a towel. The unicorn let them ride home on one condition. They had to splash through every puddle. The royal painter met them at the gate and fainted.

title: The knight laundry flag
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Lio tied a splendid flag to his lance and rode toward the foe. Nan noticed it was her bedsheet. She chased him through the banana grove, holding his tail to slow him. A messenger met them at the border and mistook the sheet for a peace flag. Both armies stopped to talk. Nan demanded soap before any treaty. The generals washed her sheet in the stream. Lio went home with peace and a lance full of wet socks.

title: The wand warranty
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gail bought a wand that promised splendid spells. Poe used it to turn banana peels into shoes. The shoes walked away without them. Gail carefully read the warranty. It covered spells only while the wand was dry. Poe had dipped it in soup. Gail wrapped her tail round the shoes and pulled them back. They put the wand in the sun. Once dry, it turned the shoes into peels. Poe wore leaves home and kept the receipt.

title: The mermaid branch seat
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ria heard a mermaid asking for a seat in the banana tree. Dax built a splendid swing above the pool. The mermaid offered a pearl but could not reach the swing. Ria carefully lowered it with her tail until it skimmed the water. Dax pushed from the bank. The pearl rolled into the mud. Ria left it there. Each day the mermaid brought fish for Dax and songs for Ria. Ria gave her bananas in return and lowered the swing for each meal.

title: The royal dungeon window
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ira got locked in a dungeon for eating royal bananas. Hope brought an enormous file hidden in breakfast. Ira used it on the bars until his tail ached. Then Hope noticed the window had no glass, only thin bars across the lower half. Ira climbed over them and dropped into the garden. He returned the file to the cook. The king ordered higher bars. Hope planted a banana tree beneath them and sent Ira a ladder bill.

title: The spell book sneeze
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Alba opened the forbidden book on a splendid branch. Sid sneezed into its pages. A spell jumped out and turned the bananas blue. Alba carefully checked the index for a cure. Sid sneezed again, and the fruit turned gold. They fed one to a crow. It stayed a crow and asked for more. Alba closed the book before Sid took another breath. They sold golden fruit at the fair and used the money to buy him a cloth.

title: The royal river fee
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Cato declared himself king of a puddle beneath the banana tree. Joy built an enormous dock from twigs. A terrible drought shrank the realm before breakfast. Cato ordered rain, but the sky ignored him. Joy carried a bowl of water in her tail and poured it into the puddle. Cato named her royal river. She charged him one banana per bowl. By sunset he gave her the crown and went to fetch water from the pond.

title: The giant pocket maze
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Koa entered an enormous maze to find Elsie. He tied a vine round his tail and left bananas at each turn. A hungry giant ate the fruit trail. Koa heard Elsie call from above. The maze lined a pocket worn by the giant, and she had climbed a seam. Koa carefully followed her voice. They escaped through a button hole. The giant found a vine in his pocket and hung his keys on it, ending the maze for good.

title: The waterfall crown
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Uma found a crown behind a waterfall. Zed put it on and demanded a treasure. Water poured from the crown into his eyes. Uma read the marks inside. It belonged to the king of rain. She tied it to her tail and swung into the banana grove, where the trees had wilted. The crown watered each root. Zed became royal bucket keeper. He still wore it on feast days, with a leaf tucked over his nose.

title: The chocolate shield
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ari made a chocolate shield for the royal trial. Nola warned that the dragon had a terrible sweet tooth. Ari held the shield high as the dragon breathed fire. It melted over his tail. The dragon stopped and licked the shield instead. Nola tossed bananas into the warm pool of sweets. The judges tasted them and called the trial a draw. Ari opened a stall beside the arena. His next shield came with a spoon.

title: The dangerous lullaby
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bryn learned a dangerous song that put foes to sleep. Flo plugged her ears with banana bits and guarded him at the castle. Bryn sang at the gate. The guards slept, but so did his splendid horse. It lay across the path. Flo tied her tail round the gate latch and hauled it open. Bryn hummed in his own sleep. Flo dragged him home in a cart and made him practice with the song book shut.

title: The messenger goose
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Etta hired a messenger goose to call Gil to the palace. The goose ate her splendid seal and swallowed the note. Gil found it honking beside his banana tree. Etta arrived on foot, tail full of spare paper. She offered the goose a bowl of water. It coughed the note into the bowl, where the ink ran. Gil guessed that the queen wanted soup. He brought a pot. She had wanted supper, so he got a royal job.

title: The beautiful mud shoe
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Lena bought a spell to make her shoes beautiful. Otis spilled mud on them before the royal ball. She rubbed the shoes with her tail, but they began to sing. The witch had enchanted the mud instead. Lena went to the ball barefoot, carrying the shoes in a basket. The splendid court band lost its tune. Her shoes sang the right notes. The prince asked for a dance, then hired her basket for the rest of the night.

title: The pineapple prophecy
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Remy found a prophecy carved in a pineapple. Sia read that the king would fall when the fruit was ripe. They rushed to the splendid throne with their tails linked for speed. The king reached for the fruit and slid off his chair. Its leg had broken. Remy caught him while Sia fixed the chair with a stone. They ate the prophecy. The king ordered softer fruit for the next royal warning and a chair with four sound legs.

title: The dungeon orchestra
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Vera heard an orchestra beneath the castle. Ben said the terrible king had locked up the players. They climbed down using their tails and found six guards banging spoons on banana bowls. A rat had stolen their keys, and the noise kept it away from their lunch. Vera played a soft tune on a reed. The rat came to listen. Ben took the keys from its nest. The guards hired the rat to turn their sheet music.

title: The forgotten sunrise
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Esme had forgotten where she hid the sun after her magic show. Cal searched the cupboard with a candle. The banana grove had gone dark. Esme shook her splendid hat, but only socks fell out. Cal felt warmth under the table. He lifted the cloth with his tail and found the sun inside a melon bowl. Esme set it free through the window. The whole village woke late, except the baker, who had baked by the bowl.

title: The fireworks wand
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Jade had to light the royal candles to earn a wizard hat. Lou handed her a fireworks wand by mistake. She pointed it at the splendid cake. Sparks burst from the bananas and chased the king under a table. Jade wrapped her tail round a wet cloth and caught each spark. Lou put them in jars. The candles stayed dark, but the jars lit the hall. Jade earned her hat. Lou earned a job cleaning the royal ceiling.

title: The crocodile moat lease
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Tia leased the moat to a crocodile who promised to guard the palace. Evan planted banana trees along the bank. The splendid beast ate the fruit and let every guest across its back. Tia read the lease aloud. It had agreed to guard the palace from hunger. Evan laughed, but Tia asked for the rent. The beast opened its mouth and showed a gold coin beneath its tongue. They paid a dentist to fetch it and kept the tenant.

title: The spaceship banana rack
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Orla strapped bananas to the spaceship wall. Dex forgot to strap himself. When the engine stopped, he floated past the splendid rack and grabbed fruit with his tail. Each banana sent him spinning faster. Orla caught his belt with a long hook. She tied him beside the rack until the ship landed. The moon guard asked what cargo they carried. Dex said fresh fruit and one bruised pilot. Orla sold the guard a bunch and kept Dex tied down until the hatch opened.

title: The pirate compass cough
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Kira stole a compass from an enormous pirate ship. Abe hid it in a banana jar. The needle pointed toward the jar lid instead of north. Kira shook it and heard a cough. A tiny messenger sat inside, trying to breathe. She opened the case with her tail. He had been hired to point toward gold but wanted shore leave. Kira sailed where he asked. His home was a bank. She returned the compass and opened an account.

title: The glacier picnic flag
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Polly planted a splendid flag on the glacier. Seth put their breakfast beneath it while they mapped the coast. An hour later the flag had moved. Polly accused a rival crew. Seth followed banana peels across the ice and found their flag on a seal. Polly had stuck it in a harness left by a fisher. She used her tail to untie it. They shared their last banana and mapped the seal route as a very wet road.

title: The jungle map napkin
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Toma found a map to an ancient treasure on a cafe napkin. Eden packed a pineapple and a coil of vine. They climbed trees for three days before the marks led them back to the cafe. Toma held the napkin against the window with his tail. The map was a stain from spilled soup. Eden peeled the fruit beside the cook. Beneath its rind lay a gold ring the cook had lost. Toma claimed the soup had been right.

title: The moon cheese crater
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Nova landed on the moon and found an enormous wedge of cheese. Finn called the discovery home, then tried to plant a flag. The pole sank to its base. Nova looped her tail round it and pulled him out of a soft crater. They laid banana leaves over the hole to spread their weight. Finn took one cheese sample. Back home it melted in his pocket. Nova sold the stained flag as proof that space travel required better lunches.

title: The raft with brakes
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Liam built a raft to reach a waterfall. Rue warned that the map showed a terrible drop. Liam tied banana crates beneath the raft and called them brakes. At the edge Rue hooked her tail round a branch. The raft swung into the bank and the crates broke. Bananas drifted over the fall. Liam climbed down to fetch them and found a quiet pool. Rue built a path to it. Their next raft trip began at the bottom.

title: The alien tail socket
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Mara met an alien beside her banana tree. Gus offered it a splendid meal. It pointed at their tails, then at an empty socket on its spaceship. Mara refused to plug herself in. Gus stuck a vine into the hole. Lights blinked, and the ship rose one inch. The alien gave them a fruit tree in thanks. Mara planted it far from the house. When it grew, each branch had a socket. Gus bought very long cords.

title: The desert snow cart
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Dune pushed an enormous cart of snow into the desert. Cora said they should have brought water. Dune claimed the snow would save their banana crop at the distant camp. By noon the cart held a puddle. Cora carefully bent her tail round the drain plug and held it shut. They reached camp with warm water and a wet map. Dune planted the banana shoots. Cora kept the cart to carry shade cloth, which weighed much less than snow.

title: The captain cork eye
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Patch wore a cork over one eye to look like a dangerous pirate. Lila steered their splendid boat while he posed on the bow. He could not see the reef. Lila wrapped her tail round his waist and pulled him down before they struck it. The cork fell into a leak and stopped the water. Patch left it there. At port the crew asked about his pirate mark. He pointed at the deck and said his eye guarded the ship.

title: The cave of lost hats
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Evan entered a cave to seek buried treasure. Sol carried a lantern and a banana lunch. The ceiling dripped on their hats, which stuck fast when they looked up. The discovery was a cave full of honey. Sol climbed his shoulders and used her tail to peel each hat free. They carried one sticky hat home. The village bees followed it. Evan sold honey by the spoon and hired Sol to keep the cave map away from bears.

title: The submarine soup leak
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Bea took a submarine below the reef. Otto packed banana soup in an enormous flask. A leak sent bubbles past the window, and Bea ordered him to seal it. Otto poured soup into the crack. A crab plugged the hole with its claw to catch the meal. Bea rose toward shore while Otto fed the crab through the crack. They bought it a bowl before it let go. The repair shop charged them for one shell and two soups.

title: The time machine lunch bell
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Kit built a time machine from a splendid clock he bought yesterday and a banana crate. Aya climbed in with her tail round the bell. They meant to see next year, but the machine stopped at lunch. Kit tried again. Lunch again. Aya read the dial. He had bought a kitchen timer. They sold rides to hungry monkeys, each ending beside a full bowl. Kit never reached next year, but he knew the exact minute the cook served every meal.

title: The canyon rope choir
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Nell had to cross a canyon with a messenger bag. Remy tied a splendid rope between two banana trees. Nell walked onto it, tail high for balance, and heard a low note. Wind played the rope like a string. Remy tightened it until the tune rose. Nell sang along and crossed in time with the beats. They left the rope there. Each new traveler paid a banana to join the song. Remy bought ear plugs with the first fee.

title: The pirate weather spoon
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Tess stirred her tea with a spoon that foretold storms. Bo hung it beside the banana mast. It rattled all night, so they stayed in port. Each day it warned of dangerous seas, though the bay looked splendid. Tess caught Bo tapping it with his tail. He feared sailing because he could not swim. She taught him in the shallows. The spoon fell silent. On their first voyage it bent in a real gale and stirred soup very badly.

title: The robot peel judge
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pax built a robot to sort bananas. Mina wrote a splendid rule that ripe fruit went left. The robot put every banana left, then put Pax there too. His yellow coat matched its chart. Mina tried to pull him free with her tail, but the robot sorted her coat beside him. Pax called this a dangerous flaw. Mina took off both coats. The robot folded them into the peel bin. They fed it a new chart and kept their coats.

title: The buried chest lid
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Wren dug for treasure under a palm. Rex had counted nine steps from a waterfall. Their spades struck wood. Wren hooked her tail into a crack and tugged, but the lid rose with their whole camp on it. The island was a giant chest. Rex wanted to open it. Wren pointed to the tents, banana trees, and sleeping crew. They shut the lid and dug a smaller hole. Rex found a coin and agreed it was quite enough.

title: The comet umbrella
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Cleo opened an umbrella to shield their spaceship from a comet. Joss said space had no rain. A shower of tiny stones hit the splendid cloth. Cleo held its handle with her tail while Joss steered. The cloth tore, but the ribs caught a shining stone. At home the museum bought it. Joss bought Cleo a new umbrella. She opened it indoors to check the ribs. A second stone dropped into the banana bowl and paid for their next trip.

title: The volcano bath ticket
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Fern climbed an enormous volcano to study its smoke. Dax packed a towel and a pineapple. They reached a warm pool, where a guard demanded bath tickets. Fern showed her science pass. The guard charged extra for steam. Dax dipped his tail and found the water cold. The smoke came from a kettle behind a rock. Fern pulled its plug. The guard refunded their fee. They ate fruit on the crater rim and watched real clouds drift past.

title: The ghost crew wash day
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ivy boarded a ghost ship to search for treasure. Reed carried a lantern in his tail. Pale shapes flapped along the deck and moaned about breakfast. Ivy touched one and found a wet sheet. The pirate crew had hung laundry on the ropes, then hidden below to scare guests away from their bananas. Reed raised his lantern and found red socks tangled among the pink sheets. Ivy offered soap in trade for fruit. The pirates accepted and asked her to keep their secret.

title: The satellite tree swing
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Lou put a satellite above the banana grove. Dara used an enormous vine to anchor its shell. Each orbit pulled the vine across the trees and swept fruit into their baskets. Lou called it a science mission. Dara used her tail to release one knot before the roots came loose. The satellite flew free, taking their basket with it. Lou sent a second craft to fetch lunch. Dara picked the next crop by hand and charged him for the launch.

title: The lost continent spoon
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Ada found an ancient continent on a spoon handle. Ben packed bananas for the splendid voyage. They sailed across a pond and found a tiny island shaped like the map. Ada planted a flag with her tail. The ground shook. A turtle rose beneath them and paddled toward shore. Ben called their discovery a moving continent. Ada gave the turtle a banana peel and took down the flag. Their next map came on a plate, which stayed still.

title: The space helmet orchard
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Zed cracked his helmet beside the spaceship. Joy had one spare, but it held an enormous banana seedling. She moved the plant into a pot while Zed held his breath. Its roots clung to the glass. Joy used her tail to ease them free. Zed put on the helmet and breathed the scent of wet soil. Back home he planted the seedling in the yard. Joy kept the cracked helmet as a dome and grew herbs beneath it.

title: The pirate silent drum
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Milo led a raid with a splendid drum. Bea said its noise would warn the enemy. Milo wrapped banana leaves round the skin and struck it with his tail. The drum gave a soft cough. They crept across the deck, then found the enemy waiting with tea. A messenger had heard the cough and called a doctor. Milo admitted he wanted their gold. Bea bought their old coins instead. The doctor charged them for a quiet drum lesson.

title: The frozen mast flag
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Elsie sailed north to see the midnight sun. Tom tied bananas to the mast so they would not freeze on deck. They froze on the mast instead, making an enormous yellow flag. Elsie carefully chipped one free with a spoon held in her tail. The flag cracked and dropped fruit into the soup pot. A passing ship hailed their strange banner. Tom sold it hot banana soup. Elsie watched the sun while counting the coins in her warm mittens.

title: The asteroid pet leash
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Gail found treasure inside a small asteroid. Koa drilled a hole, and the rock began to roll away. Gail caught it with a leash held in her tail. Its shell cracked open to reveal a moon snail. Koa called the discovery a mining failure. Gail offered the snail banana leaves from their ship garden. It followed them home and ate the stone steps. Koa sold the smooth dust. Gail moved the leash to a very large stake.

title: The swamp boot ferry
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Pia stepped into the swamp and lost a boot. Seth pulled her out by the tail. Their splendid map said dry land lay beyond the reeds. Pia found her boot floating toward a crocodile. She threw it a banana instead. Seth tied a vine to the boot and used it as a tiny ferry for their packs. They crossed on roots. The crocodile followed the fruit to shore, where Pia traded it the other boot for safe passage.

title: The planet mirror sale
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Nova found a planet that mirrored each move. Hal waved his tail, and a splendid monkey waved back. They offered the mirror crew bananas. The other crew offered theirs too. Nova stepped closer and hit glass. The planet was a showroom window inside a spaceship. Hal found a price tag on the frame. They bought one mirror for the ship gym. Nova logged the discovery as useful furniture. Hal trained his tail with a partner who never missed a turn.

title: The captain salt chart
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Arlo drew a chart in salt on the deck. May warned that a dangerous wave would erase it. He built an enormous fence round the chart and tied his tail to the mast. The sea stayed calm, but a crew member spilled soup. Salt ran into every port mark. May tasted the soup and found it good. She sold bowls to the crew while Arlo drew a new chart on cloth. He marked the soup stall as their safest harbor.

title: The cave lantern refund
author: IMI Nine Letter Monkey Desk
text: Cobb bought a splendid lantern for his cave trip. Una bought bananas. In the cave the lantern went dark. Cobb shook it, and a firefly crawled out demanding breakfast.
